name.zh: 阿克苏姆国王埃扎纳皈依基督教

summary.en: Instructed by the Syrian captive Frumentius, later consecrated bishop by Athanasius of Alexandria, King Ezana embraced Christianity. His later stone inscriptions and coins replace the disc-and-crescent with the cross, making Aksum one of the first states to adopt the faith officially.
summary.zh: 国王埃扎纳受叙利亚俘虏弗鲁门修斯（后由亚历山大城的亚他那修祝圣为主教）影响皈依基督教。其后期石刻铭文与钱币以十字架取代日月纹，使阿克苏姆成为最早正式接受基督教的国家之一。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Ezana Stone
S. Munro-Hay, Aksum: An African Civilisation of Late Antiquity (1991)
Rufinus of Aquileia, Ecclesiastical History, X.9–10 (account of Frumentius)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Aksum
Rufinus of Aquileia, Historia Ecclesiastica X.9–10
Athanasius, Apologia ad Constantium 29–31 (letter of Constantius II to Ezana)

note: Conversion is dated only approximately (c. 330s–350s). 340 is used because Ezana succeeded as a minor c. 330 and, per Rufinus, adopted the faith after coming of age, when Frumentius returned as bishop. QID is the Ezana Stone, the inscription that records it; Wikidata dates the stone only to the 4th century.

story.en:
The church historian Rufinus tells how two Syrian boys, Frumentius and Aedesius, survived an attack on their ship on the Red Sea coast and were taken to the royal court at Aksum. Frumentius rose to be the king’s secretary and helped govern during the minority of the young Ezana. Later he travelled to Alexandria to ask Patriarch Athanasius for a bishop, and Athanasius consecrated Frumentius himself. Ethiopian tradition remembers him as Abba Salama, “father of peace”.

Ezana’s own monuments show the change. His earlier inscriptions credit victories to Mahrem, the Aksumite war god; later ones, in Ge’ez and Greek, thank the “Lord of Heaven” and name the Father, Son and Holy Spirit. His gold coins dropped the pagan disc and crescent for the cross, among the earliest coins anywhere to carry it.

Around 356 the Roman emperor Constantius II wrote to Ezana asking him to send Frumentius to be re-examined by an Arian bishop, a sign of how far Aksum now figured in Mediterranean church politics. The Ethiopian Orthodox Church traces its origins to this conversion.
story.zh:
据教会史家鲁菲努斯记载，两名叙利亚少年弗鲁门修斯和埃德修斯所乘之船在红海沿岸遇袭，二人幸存后被带到阿克苏姆宫廷。弗鲁门修斯后来成为国王的书记官，并在年幼的埃扎纳即位初期协助理政。之后他前往亚历山大，请求宗主教阿塔纳修斯派遣主教，阿塔纳修斯便直接祝圣他本人为主教。埃塞俄比亚传统称他为“阿巴·萨拉马”，意为“和平之父”。

埃扎纳自己的碑铭记录了这一转变。早期碑文把胜利归功于阿克苏姆战神马赫雷姆；后期用吉兹文和希腊文刻写的碑文则感谢“天上之主”，并称颂圣父、圣子、圣灵。他的金币也以十字架取代了异教的圆盘与新月，是世界上最早带有十字架图案的钱币之一。

约356年，罗马皇帝君士坦提乌斯二世致信埃扎纳，要求把弗鲁门修斯送去接受一位阿里乌派主教的审查，可见阿克苏姆已进入地中海教会政治的视野。埃塞俄比亚正教会将其起源追溯到这次皈依。

summary.en: Geiseric’s Vandals and Alans, who had crossed from Spain in 429, seized Carthage by surprise, breaking a treaty with Rome. The city became capital of a Vandal kingdom whose fleet dominated the western Mediterranean and sacked Rome in 455.
summary.zh: 429年自西班牙渡海的盖萨里克所率汪达尔人与阿兰人突袭攻占迦太基，撕毁了与罗马的条约。迦太基成为汪达尔王国都城，其舰队称霸西地中海，并于455年洗劫罗马。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Vandal Kingdom
Victor of Vita, History of the Vandal Persecution (c. 484)
Procopius, History of the Wars, Book III
Britannica: Gaiseric

story.en:
In 429 the Vandal king Geiseric ferried his people, by Victor of Vita’s count some 80,000 souls, across the Strait of Gibraltar into Roman Africa. They besieged Hippo Regius, where the aged Bishop Augustine died in 430, and in 435 Rome conceded them part of Numidia by treaty.

On 19 October 439 Geiseric broke that treaty and marched into Carthage, the second city of the western empire, apparently meeting little resistance. He later counted the years of his reign from that day. With Carthage came its dockyards, and the Vandals became a naval power that raided Sicily, Sardinia and Italy; in 455 they sacked Rome for two weeks and carried off the empress Eudoxia and her daughters.

As Arian Christians the Vandal kings confiscated Catholic churches and exiled bishops, episodes Victor of Vita recorded bitterly. Their kingdom lasted almost a century, until the Byzantine general Belisarius defeated King Gelimer in 533–534 and restored imperial rule.
story.zh:
429年，汪达尔国王盖萨里克率领其族人渡过直布罗陀海峡进入罗马阿非利加，据维塔的维克托统计约有八万人。他们围攻希波城，年迈的主教奥古斯丁于430年在城中去世；435年罗马通过条约把努米底亚部分地区让给他们。

439年10月19日，盖萨里克撕毁条约，开进西部帝国第二大城市迦太基，几乎未遇抵抗。他后来以这一天作为纪年的起点。夺得迦太基也就夺得了它的船坞，汪达尔人由此成为海上强权，劫掠西西里、撒丁和意大利；455年他们洗劫罗马两周，并掳走皇后欧多克西娅及其女儿。

汪达尔诸王信奉阿里乌派，没收公教会的教堂并放逐主教，维塔的维克托对此有沉痛的记载。这个王国延续近一个世纪，直到533—534年拜占庭名将贝利萨留击败国王盖利默，恢复帝国统治。

summary.en: An army of the Rashidun Caliphate under ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs entered Egypt in 639, took the Byzantine fortress of Babylon in 641 and received Alexandria by treaty, ending nearly a millennium of Greco-Roman rule. The new garrison town of Fustat became the seat of Islamic Egypt.
summary.zh: 639年，阿慕尔·伊本·阿斯率正统哈里发国军队进入埃及，641年攻克拜占庭的巴比伦要塞，并以条约接收亚历山大港，结束了近千年的希腊—罗马统治。新建的军镇福斯塔特成为伊斯兰埃及的治所。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Arab conquest of Egypt
Hugh Kennedy, The Great Arab Conquests (2007)
John of Nikiu, Chronicle (late 7th century)
Ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam, Futuh Misr (9th century)
Britannica: ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ
Alfred J. Butler, The Arab Conquest of Egypt (1902; 2nd ed. P. M. Fraser, 1978)

story.en:
In December 639 ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs crossed from Palestine at al-ʿArish with only about four thousand horsemen, reportedly pressing on before the caliph ʿUmar could recall him. Reinforced, he beat the Byzantine field army near Heliopolis in 640 and laid siege to Babylon, the Roman fortress at the head of the Nile delta, which surrendered in April 641.

The imperial governor and patriarch Cyrus, remembered in Arabic sources as al-Muqawqis, then negotiated the surrender of Alexandria in exchange for tribute and a safe departure of the garrison, which sailed in 642. A Byzantine fleet briefly retook the city in 645–646. The famous story that ʿAmr burned the Library of Alexandria on ʿUmar’s orders first appears centuries later and is rejected by historians.

For the Coptic majority the change of masters brought relief from persecution by the Chalcedonian church: their patriarch Benjamin came out of hiding. ʿAmr’s camp beside Babylon grew into Fustat, with the first mosque in Egypt, and Egypt became the granary and launching base for the conquest of the Maghreb.
story.zh:
639年12月，阿慕尔·本·阿斯仅率约四千骑兵从巴勒斯坦越过阿里什进入埃及，据说是在哈里发欧麦尔召回他之前抢先进军。获得增援后，他于640年在赫利奥波利斯附近击败拜占庭野战军，并围攻尼罗河三角洲顶端的罗马要塞巴比伦，该要塞于641年4月投降。

帝国总督兼宗主教居鲁士（阿拉伯文献称“穆盖格斯”）随后谈判，以纳贡换取守军安全撤离，交出亚历山大，守军于642年乘船离去。645—646年拜占庭舰队曾短暂收复该城。所谓阿慕尔奉欧麦尔之命焚毁亚历山大图书馆的故事，是数百年后才出现的，史家并不采信。

对占人口多数的科普特人而言，政权更替使他们摆脱了卡尔西顿派教会的迫害，其宗主教本雅明得以重新露面。阿慕尔在巴比伦旁的营地发展为福斯塔特，建起埃及第一座清真寺，埃及则成为征服马格里布的粮仓和出发基地。

name.en: Baqt treaty between Makuria and Muslim Egypt
name.zh: 马库里亚与穆斯林埃及的巴克特条约

summary.en: After Nubian archers repulsed an Arab siege of Dongola, King Qalidurut of Makuria and ʿAbdallah ibn Saʿd agreed the Baqt, an exchange of goods and non-aggression pact. It kept Christian Nubia independent for some six centuries, an exceptional arrangement in early Islamic history.
summary.zh: 努比亚弓箭手击退阿拉伯军队对栋古拉的围攻后，马库里亚国王卡利杜鲁特与阿卜杜拉·伊本·赛义德订立巴克特条约，约定互换物资、互不侵犯。该条约使基督教努比亚保持独立约六百年，在早期伊斯兰史上极为罕见。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Baqt
Derek A. Welsby, The Medieval Kingdoms of Nubia (2002)
al-Maqrizi, al-Khitat (15th century; preserves the treaty terms)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. III: Africa from the Seventh to the Eleventh Century (ed. M. El Fasi & I. Hrbek, 1988)

note: Traditionally dated 651/652 (AH 31); Wikidata gives only a century. The original text survives only in later Arabic authors.

summary.en: Over six decades Arab armies advanced from Egypt across North Africa against Byzantine garrisons and fierce Amazigh (Berber) resistance led by Kusayla and Queen Dihya (al-Kahina). Kairouan became the base, Carthage fell in 698, and by 709 the conquest reached the Atlantic, preparing the invasion of Iberia.
summary.zh: 六十余年间，阿拉伯军队自埃及向西推进，对抗拜占庭守军及由库赛拉和女王狄希雅（卡希娜）领导的阿马齐格（柏柏尔）人顽强抵抗。凯鲁万成为大本营，迦太基于698年陷落，至709年征服推进至大西洋沿岸，为进军伊比利亚铺路。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Muslim conquest of the Maghreb
Hugh Kennedy, The Great Arab Conquests (2007)
Ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam, Futuh Misr wa'l-Maghrib (9th century)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. III: Africa from the Seventh to the Eleventh Century (ed. M. El Fasi & I. Hrbek, 1988)
Britannica: Kāhina
Ibn Khaldun, Kitab al-ʿIbar (history of the Berbers)

note: Dates of individual episodes (especially Dihya’s defeat) vary by source; route points are approximate.

story.en:
The conquest of North Africa took far longer than that of Egypt or Syria. In 670 ʿUqba ibn Nafiʿ founded Kairouan as a camp city safely inland from the Byzantine-held coast. Later Arabic tradition says he rode west until his horse stood in the Atlantic surf and declared he would carry Islam further if the ocean allowed, a story best read as legend.

The Amazigh resisted fiercely. In 683 the chieftain Kusayla ambushed and killed ʿUqba near Biskra and held Kairouan for several years. After Hassan ibn al-Nuʿman took Carthage in the 690s, a woman of the Aurès mountains, Dihya, whom the Arabs called al-Kahina (“the prophetess”), defeated him and drove the Arabs back toward Tripolitania. Ibn Khaldun reports that she laid waste the lowlands to make them worthless to invaders; she was killed in battle around 701–703.

Musa ibn Nusayr completed the conquest by about 709, recruiting large numbers of Amazigh into the army. One of them, Tariq ibn Ziyad, crossed to Iberia in 711, and Berber converts soon carried Islam across the Sahara as well.
story.zh:
征服北非远比征服埃及或叙利亚漫长。670年，欧格白·本·纳菲在远离拜占庭控制海岸的内陆建立军营城市凯鲁万。后来的阿拉伯传说称他一路西进，直到战马踏入大西洋的浪花，宣称若非大海阻隔还要把伊斯兰传得更远，这一故事应视为传说。

阿马齐格人（柏柏尔人）抵抗激烈。683年，首领库赛拉在比斯克拉附近伏击并杀死欧格白，占据凯鲁万数年。7世纪90年代哈桑·本·努曼攻取迦太基后，奥雷斯山区的女首领迪希亚（阿拉伯人称她为“卡希娜”，意为女先知）击败了他，把阿拉伯军队逐回的黎波里塔尼亚。据伊本·赫勒敦记载，她焦土以待，使平原对入侵者失去价值；约701—703年间她战死沙场。

穆萨·本·努赛尔约在709年完成征服，并大量招募阿马齐格人入伍。其中一人塔里克·本·齐亚德于711年渡海进入伊比利亚，柏柏尔皈依者不久也把伊斯兰带过撒哈拉。

name.zh: 非斯卡拉维因清真寺（大学）创建

summary.en: Fatima al-Fihri, daughter of a merchant from Kairouan, endowed a mosque in Fez that grew into a major centre of Maliki law, theology and science. Al-Qarawiyyin is often cited as the oldest continuously operating institution of higher learning in the world.
summary.zh: 来自凯鲁万的商人之女法蒂玛·菲赫里在非斯捐建清真寺，后发展为马利克派法学、神学与科学的重要中心。卡拉维因常被视为世界上持续办学最久的高等学府。

sources.title: Wikipedia: University of al-Qarawiyyin
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Medina of Fez
Ibn Abi Zarʿ, Rawd al-Qirtas (c. 1326)

note: The 859 date and Fatima al-Fihri’s role rest on 14th-century chronicles.

summary.en: According to the Kilwa Chronicle, ʿAli ibn al-Hassan, a “Shirazi” prince, acquired the island of Kilwa Kisiwani. The Swahili city-state grew rich controlling the gold trade from Sofala and Great Zimbabwe and minted its own coins.
summary.zh: 据《基尔瓦编年史》，“设拉子”王子阿里·伊本·哈桑取得基尔瓦基西瓦尼岛。这一斯瓦希里城邦借控制来自索法拉和大津巴布韦的黄金贸易而致富，并自铸钱币。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Kilwa Sultanate
Kilwa Chronicle (Kitab al-Sulwa fi akhbar Kilwa, 16th century)
H. Neville Chittick, Kilwa: An Islamic Trading City on the East African Coast (1974)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani and Ruins of Songo Mnara

note: The 10th-century date is traditional; archaeology suggests the Shirazi dynasty emerged c. 1000–1100.

summary.en: After conquering Egypt, the Fatimid general Jawhar al-Siqilli laid out a walled palace city north of Fustat named al-Qahira, “the Victorious”. Caliph al-Muʿizz moved his court there in 973, and Cairo became the capital of a Shiʿi empire rivalling Abbasid Baghdad.
summary.zh: 法蒂玛王朝将领昭海尔·西西里征服埃及后，在福斯塔特以北修建城墙环绕的宫城，名为“卡希拉”（胜利者）。973年哈里发穆伊兹迁都于此，开罗成为与阿拔斯王朝巴格达相抗衡的什叶派帝国首都。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Cairo
Michael Brett, The Fatimid Empire (2017)
al-Maqrizi, al-Mawaʿiz wa al-Iʿtibar (al-Khitat), 15th century
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Cairo
Britannica: Cairo – History
André Raymond, Cairo (trans. W. Wood, 2000)

story.en:
In July 969 the Fatimid general Jawhar, a former slave of Sicilian or Slavic origin, entered Fustat with an army of Kutama Berbers after a nearly bloodless campaign. That same night, says the chronicle tradition, he marked out a rectangle of walls to the north-east for a new palace city reserved for the caliph, his court and his troops.

A later legend preserved by al-Maqrizi holds that astrologers waited for an auspicious moment to begin digging, signalled by bells hung on ropes along the trench; a raven landed on a rope too early, the workmen began, and the planet Mars, al-Qahir, was rising, so the city was called al-Qahira, “the Victorious”.

Jawhar founded al-Azhar mosque in 970, and in 973 Caliph al-Muʿizz arrived from Ifriqiya bearing the coffins of his ancestors. Cairo became the capital of a Shiʿi empire stretching from Tunisia to Syria and the Hijaz, rival to Abbasid Baghdad; under later dynasties it grew into the largest city of the medieval Islamic world.
story.zh:
969年7月，法蒂玛王朝将领昭海尔（原为西西里或斯拉夫出身的奴隶）率领库塔马柏柏尔军队几乎兵不血刃地进入福斯塔特。据编年史传统记载，他当晚就在东北方划出一片长方形城垣，作为专供哈里发、宫廷与军队居住的新宫城。

马格里齐记载的一则后世传说称，占星师在壕沟沿线的绳索上挂铃，等待吉时开挖；不料一只乌鸦过早落在绳上，工人随即动工，而此时火星（阿拉伯语称“卡希尔”）正在升起，于是这座城被命名为“卡希拉”，意为“胜利之城”。

昭海尔于970年创建爱资哈尔清真寺；973年哈里发穆伊兹携祖先灵柩从伊夫里基亚迁来。开罗成为一个从突尼斯延伸到叙利亚和汉志的什叶派帝国的首都，与阿拔斯王朝的巴格达分庭抗礼；在后来的王朝治下，它发展为中世纪伊斯兰世界最大的城市。

summary.en: Built by the Fatimids in their new capital and first used for prayer in 972, al-Azhar became a teaching mosque. After the Ayyubids restored Sunnism it evolved into the leading centre of Sunni learning, and it remains one of the world’s oldest universities.
summary.zh: 法蒂玛王朝在新都修建爱资哈尔清真寺，972年首次举行礼拜，随后成为讲学之所。阿尤布王朝恢复逊尼派后，它发展为逊尼派最重要的学术中心，至今仍是世界上最古老的大学之一。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Al-Azhar Mosque
Britannica: al-Azhar University
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Cairo

note: Built 970–972 (Wikidata gives 971 for inception).

name.zh: 穆拉比特王朝建立马拉喀什

summary.en: The Saharan Almoravid movement established Marrakesh as a fortified camp below the High Atlas, and Yusuf ibn Tashfin made it the capital of an empire stretching from Senegal to al-Andalus. The city later served the Almohads and Saadians as capital.
summary.zh: 来自撒哈拉的穆拉比特运动在阿特拉斯山脚建起马拉喀什营地，优素福·伊本·塔什芬以之为帝国首都，疆域从塞内加尔延伸至安达卢斯。此后穆瓦希德王朝和萨阿德王朝也定都于此。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Marrakesh
Amira K. Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Medina of Marrakesh

note: Disputed: Ibn Abi Zarʿ and Ibn Khaldun give 1062 (454 AH); Ibn ʿIdhari gives 1070, followed by Bennison and most recent scholarship. Britannica says only “mid-11th century”; Wikidata gives 1065. The founder may have been Abu Bakr ibn ʿUmar rather than Yusuf.

summary.en: At the Shashe–Limpopo confluence, Mapungubwe became southern Africa’s first class-stratified state, trading gold and ivory to the Indian Ocean for glass beads. Its elite hilltop burials, including the famous gold rhinoceros, precede the rise of Great Zimbabwe.
summary.zh: 马蓬古布韦位于沙谢河与林波波河交汇处，是南部非洲首个阶层分化的国家，以黄金、象牙与印度洋贸易换取玻璃珠。其山顶精英墓葬（包括著名的金犀牛）早于大津巴布韦的兴起。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Mapungubwe
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape
Thomas N. Huffman, Mapungubwe: Ancient African Civilisation on the Limpopo (2005)

note: Dates are archaeological (radiocarbon) estimates.

summary.en: Eleven monolithic churches were carved down into volcanic rock at Roha, the Zagwe capital, traditionally under King Gebre Mesqel Lalibela as a “New Jerusalem”. They remain an active Ethiopian Orthodox pilgrimage centre.
summary.zh: 扎格维王朝都城罗哈的十一座独石教堂由火山岩向下凿成，传统上认为是国王盖布雷·梅斯克尔·拉利贝拉为建造“新耶路撒冷”而修。至今仍是埃塞俄比亚正教的朝圣中心。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Rock-Hewn Churches, Lalibela
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Rock-Hewn Churches, Lalibela
David W. Phillipson, Ancient Churches of Ethiopia (2009)

note: Attributed to Lalibela’s reign (c. 1181–1221); Phillipson argues some churches are older. Wikidata dates the complex to the 13th century.

story.en:
At Roha in the Lasta highlands, masons of the Zagwe kingdom cut eleven churches downward into the red volcanic tuff, freeing each block from the hillside and then hollowing out naves, columns and windows from a single mass of rock. The most famous, Bete Giyorgis, stands in a deep pit shaped as a Greek cross.

Ethiopian tradition credits King Gebre Mesqel Lalibela, who is said to have wanted a New Jerusalem after Saladin took the holy city in 1187; a channel through the site is named the Yordanos (Jordan) and a hill Golgotha. Hagiography adds that angels carved by night what the workmen cut by day. Archaeologists such as David Phillipson argue that some structures began earlier as fortifications or dwellings and were converted into churches.

The town was later renamed Lalibela after the king. Listed by UNESCO in 1978, the churches remain living places of worship: at Genna, the Ethiopian Christmas, tens of thousands of white-robed pilgrims gather there.
story.zh:
在拉斯塔高原的罗哈，扎格维王朝的石匠向下开凿红色火山凝灰岩，先把整块岩体从山坡中分离出来，再从同一块岩石里掏出中殿、立柱和窗户，共凿成十一座教堂。其中最著名的圣乔治教堂矗立在一个希腊十字形的深坑之中。

埃塞俄比亚传统将其归功于国王格布雷·梅斯克尔·拉利贝拉，据说他在萨拉丁于1187年攻占耶路撒冷后想建造一座“新耶路撒冷”；遗址中的一条水渠被称为“约旦河”，一座小山名为“各各他”。圣徒传还说，工匠白天开凿多少，天使夜里便再凿多少。考古学家菲利普森等人则认为，部分建筑原为更早的堡垒或住所，后来才改建为教堂。

小城后来以这位国王的名字改称拉利贝拉。1978年列入联合国教科文组织世界遗产名录的这些教堂至今仍在使用：每逢埃塞俄比亚圣诞节“根纳”，数以万计身着白袍的朝圣者聚集于此。

summary.en: The Shona-speaking capital of the Kingdom of Zimbabwe built the largest dry-stone structures in sub-Saharan Africa, including the Great Enclosure. Wealth from cattle and gold exported via Sofala and Kilwa sustained perhaps 10,000–18,000 people before the site declined in the 15th century.
summary.zh: 说绍纳语的津巴布韦王国都城修建了撒哈拉以南非洲最大的干砌石构建筑群，包括“大围场”。牛群与经索法拉、基尔瓦出口的黄金带来财富，城中人口或达一万至一万八千人，15世纪后衰落。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Great Zimbabwe
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Great Zimbabwe National Monument
Innocent Pikirayi, The Zimbabwe Culture: Origins and Decline of Southern Zambezian States (2001)
Britannica: Great Zimbabwe

note: Chronology from archaeology; population estimates vary widely.

story.en:
On a granite hill above the plateau of south-eastern Zimbabwe, Shona-speaking builders raised walls of fitted granite blocks without mortar. The Great Enclosure below the hill has an outer wall about 250 metres long and up to 11 metres high, enclosing a solid conical tower whose purpose is still debated. Excavations found Chinese celadon, Persian pottery and glass beads, traded for gold through Sofala and Kilwa, and eight carved soapstone birds.

When the German explorer Karl Mauch saw the ruins in 1871 he imagined them as the Queen of Sheba’s palace, and white settlers in Rhodesia long insisted that Phoenicians or Arabs had built them. In 1929 the archaeologist Gertrude Caton-Thompson showed the site to be African, a finding the Rhodesian government later tried to suppress.

The city declined in the 15th century, perhaps from overgrazing and shifting trade toward Mutapa in the north. When the country won independence in 1980 it took the name Zimbabwe, “houses of stone”, and a soapstone bird appears on the national flag.
story.zh:
在津巴布韦东南部高原的一座花岗岩山丘上，说绍纳语的建造者不用灰浆，以拼合的花岗岩块砌起城墙。山下的“大围场”外墙长约250米，高达11米，墙内有一座实心圆锥形塔，其用途至今仍有争议。发掘出土了中国青瓷、波斯陶器和玻璃珠，这些都是经索法拉和基尔瓦以黄金换来的，此外还有八只皂石雕刻的鸟。

1871年德国探险家卡尔·毛赫见到遗址时，以为这是示巴女王的宫殿；罗得西亚的白人移民也长期坚称它出自腓尼基人或阿拉伯人之手。1929年考古学家格特鲁德·卡顿-汤普森证明遗址由非洲人建造，而罗得西亚政府后来竟试图压制这一结论。

这座城市在15世纪衰落，原因可能是过度放牧以及贸易北移至穆塔帕。1980年这个国家获得独立时取名“津巴布韦”，意为“石头房子”，国旗上也绘有一只皂石鸟。

summary.en: Sundiata Keita, leading a coalition of Mande clans, defeated the Sosso king Sumanguru Kanté. The victory, celebrated in the griots’ Sunjata epic, founded the Mali Empire, whose constitution tradition ascribes to the assembly at Kurukan Fuga.
summary.zh: 松迪亚塔·凯塔率曼丁各氏族联盟击败索索国王苏曼古鲁·坎特。这一胜利为格里奥传唱的《松迪亚塔史诗》所颂扬，奠定了马里帝国，传统认为其制度确立于库鲁坎富加大会。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Kirina
D. T. Niane, Sundiata: An Epic of Old Mali (trans. G. D. Pickett, 1965)
Ibn Khaldun, Kitab al-ʿIbar (in Levtzion & Hopkins, Corpus)
Nehemia Levtzion, Ancient Ghana and Mali (1973)
D. T. Niane, Sundiata: An Epic of Old Mali (1960; trans. G. D. Pickett, 1965)
UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage: Manden Charter, proclaimed in Kurukan Fuga

note: Known mainly from oral tradition; c. 1235 is the conventional date.

story.en:
The battle survives chiefly in the Sunjata epic, still performed by Mande griots, so its details are tradition rather than record. In the version written down by D. T. Niane, Sumanguru Kanté of Sosso was a sorcerer-king who had subdued the Mande chiefdoms and kept Sundiata’s griot Balla Fasséké at his own court.

According to the epic, Sundiata’s sister Nana Triban, held at Sumanguru’s court, learned the secret of his power: he could be harmed only by an arrow tipped with the spur of a white cockerel. At Kirina, near the Niger, Sundiata grazed Sumanguru with such an arrow; the king lost his magic, fled and vanished into the hills of Koulikoro.

Afterwards, tradition says, the allied clans met at Kurukan Fuga, where Sundiata was proclaimed mansa and rules for the clans, castes and kin obligations were laid down. UNESCO inscribed this “Manden Charter” as intangible heritage in 2009. The Arab historian Ibn Khaldun, writing in the 1370s, confirms that a king he calls Mari Jata conquered Sosso and founded Mali’s power.
story.zh:
这场战役主要保存在曼丁格格里奥（说唱艺人）至今仍在吟诵的《松迪亚塔史诗》中，因此细节属于传说而非史录。在尼亚奈笔录的版本里，索索国王苏曼古鲁·坎特是一位巫王，他征服了曼丁各部，还把松迪亚塔的格里奥巴拉·法塞凯扣在自己宫中。

史诗称，被扣在苏曼古鲁宫中的松迪亚塔之姊娜娜·特里班探知了他的秘密：唯有绑着白公鸡距的箭才能伤他。在尼日尔河附近的基里纳，松迪亚塔用这样一支箭擦伤了苏曼古鲁，国王法力尽失，逃入库利科罗的群山后消失无踪。

传说战后各盟族在库鲁坎富加集会，拥立松迪亚塔为“曼萨”，并订立了关于氏族、种姓和亲族义务的规则。2009年，联合国教科文组织将这部“曼丁宪章”列入非物质文化遗产名录。14世纪70年代写作的阿拉伯史家伊本·赫勒敦也证实，一位他称为“马里·贾塔”的国王征服了索索，奠定了马里的国力。

summary.en: The Geʿez “Glory of the Kings”, compiled under the early Solomonic dynasty, tells how Menelik I, son of Solomon and the Queen of Sheba, brought the Ark of the Covenant to Aksum. It became Ethiopia’s national epic and the ideological charter of Solomonic kingship.
summary.zh: 吉兹语《列王的荣耀》编成于所罗门王朝初期，讲述所罗门与示巴女王之子孟尼利克一世将约柜带到阿克苏姆的故事。它成为埃塞俄比亚的民族史诗和所罗门王朝君权的意识形态依据。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Kebra Nagast
E. A. Wallis Budge (trans.), The Queen of Sheba and Her Only Son Menyelek (Kebra Nagast) (1922)
Britannica: Kebra Nagast
Richard Pankhurst, The Ethiopians: A History (1998)

note: The colophon names Yeshaq of Aksum and implies c. 1314–1322; the text draws on older traditions and is treated here as tradition, not history.

summary.en: Mansa Musa of Mali crossed the Sahara with a vast retinue and so much gold that, al-ʿUmari reports, its value fell in Cairo for years. The hajj put Mali on Mediterranean maps such as the 1375 Catalan Atlas and brought scholars and architects back to the Sahel.
summary.zh: 马里的曼萨·穆萨率庞大随从穿越撒哈拉，携带黄金之多，据乌马里记载使开罗金价多年低落。这次朝觐使马里出现在1375年《加泰罗尼亚地图集》等地中海地图上，并带回学者与建筑师。

note: No Wikidata item for the pilgrimage itself. The trans-Saharan route is not recorded precisely; Tuat is a probable stage. Some historians date the hajj 1324–1325, Ibn Khaldun’s informants slightly differently.

story.en:
Mansa Musa reached Cairo in July 1324 with a caravan that later writers remembered as enormous, laden with gold. The scholar al-ʿUmari, who questioned Cairo officials a dozen years later, reports that Musa and his followers spent and gave away so much gold that its value in Egypt was still depressed when he wrote.

There was friction too. Musa at first refused to kiss the ground before the Mamluk sultan al-Nasir Muhammad, agreeing only to prostrate himself before God. Cairo merchants overcharged his party, and by the return journey he had run so short that he borrowed money at interest. In Mecca he performed the pilgrimage and recruited scholars and the Andalusian poet and architect Abu Ishaq al-Sahili, who is credited with buildings in Timbuktu and Gao.

The hajj made Mali famous in the Mediterranean. Fifty years later the Majorcan Catalan Atlas showed a West African king enthroned with a golden orb or nugget, labelled as the richest and noblest ruler of the land.
story.zh:
1324年7月，曼萨·穆萨率领驼队抵达开罗，后世作者回忆这支满载黄金的队伍规模极其庞大。十余年后向开罗官员调查此事的学者乌马里记载，穆萨及其随从花费和赠送的黄金之多，使埃及金价直到他写作时仍未回升。

其间也有摩擦。穆萨起初拒绝在马穆鲁克苏丹纳西尔·穆罕默德面前吻地，只肯说自己仅向真主叩拜。开罗商人对他的随行人员漫天要价，返程时他已囊中羞涩，不得不借高利贷。他在麦加完成朝觐，招募了学者以及安达卢斯诗人兼建筑师阿布·伊斯哈格·萨赫利，据说廷巴克图和加奥的一些建筑出自后者之手。

这次朝觐使马里名扬地中海世界。五十年后，马略卡岛绘制的《加泰罗尼亚地图集》上画着一位手持金球（或金块）端坐宝座的西非君主，并标注他是那片土地上最富有、最高贵的统治者。

name.zh: 廷巴克图津加雷贝尔清真寺落成

summary.en: On his return from Mecca, Mansa Musa commissioned the Andalusi poet Abu Ishaq al-Sahili to build a great mosque of earth and timber in Timbuktu. Rebuilt many times, it anchored the city’s growth as a centre of Islamic scholarship.
summary.zh: 曼萨·穆萨朝觐归来后，委托安达卢斯诗人阿布·伊斯哈格·萨赫利在廷巴克图用泥土和木材建造大清真寺。该寺历经多次重建，成为廷巴克图发展为伊斯兰学术中心的支柱。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Djinguereber Mosque
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Timbuktu

name.zh: 伊本·赫勒敦完成《历史绪论》

summary.en: In retreat at Qalʿat Ibn Salama in present-day Algeria, Ibn Khaldun drafted the introduction to his universal history. Its theory of ʿasabiyya (group solidarity) and the rise and fall of dynasties is regarded as a founding work of historiography and sociology.
summary.zh: 伊本·赫勒敦隐居于今阿尔及利亚的伊本·萨拉马堡，写成其通史的绪论。书中关于“阿萨比亚”（群体凝聚力）与王朝兴衰的理论被视为历史学和社会学的奠基之作。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Muqaddimah

summary.en: Blown south past the continent’s tip, Bartolomeu Dias’s Portuguese ships landed at Mossel Bay, where Khoikhoi herders resisted them, and sailed on to the Bushmans River before turning back, sighting the Cape of Good Hope on the return. The voyage proved a sea route to the Indian Ocean.
summary.zh: 迪亚士的葡萄牙船队被风吹过大陆南端，在莫塞尔湾登陆并遭科伊科伊牧民抵抗，继续航行至布须曼河后折返，归途中望见好望角。此行证明了通往印度洋的海路。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Bartolomeu Dias
João de Barros, Décadas da Ásia, I (1552)
Britannica: Bartolomeu Dias
João de Barros, Décadas da Ásia I.iii.4 (1552)

story.en:
Bartolomeu Dias left Lisbon in August 1487 with two caravels and a supply ship, under orders from King João II to find the end of Africa. Off the coast of what is now Namibia, storms drove the ships south for nearly two weeks out of sight of land. When Dias turned east and found only open sea, he steered north and struck the coast beyond the Cape.

In early February 1488 the Portuguese landed at a bay they named for São Brás, today’s Mossel Bay. Khoikhoi herders watering cattle there threw stones to drive them off, and Dias killed one with a crossbow bolt, the first recorded clash between Europeans and South Africans. A little further east his exhausted crews forced him to turn back; he planted a stone pillar at Kwaaihoek.

On the return voyage he sighted the great cape. The chronicler João de Barros says Dias called it the Cape of Storms and the king renamed it the Cape of Good Hope. Dias died in 1500 when his ship sank in a storm off that same cape.
story.zh:
1487年8月，巴尔托洛梅乌·迪亚士奉国王若昂二世之命，率两艘卡拉维尔帆船和一艘补给船离开里斯本，寻找非洲的尽头。在今纳米比亚沿海，风暴把船队向南吹了近两周，一直看不到陆地。迪亚士转向东航行却只见大海，于是向北行驶，在好望角以东抵达海岸。

1488年2月初，葡萄牙人在一处他们以圣布拉斯命名的海湾登陆，即今天的莫塞尔湾。在那里饮牛的科伊科伊牧民投掷石块驱赶他们，迪亚士用弩箭射杀一人，这是欧洲人与南非居民之间有记录的第一次冲突。再往东不远，疲惫不堪的船员迫使他返航，他在夸伊胡克竖起一根石柱。

回程中他望见了那座巨大的海角。据编年史家若昂·德·巴罗斯记载，迪亚士称之为“风暴角”，国王将其改名为“好望角”。1500年，迪亚士的船正是在这个海角附近的风暴中沉没，他也随之遇难。

name.en: Battle of Ridaniya: Ottomans take Egypt
name.zh: 里达尼亚战役：奥斯曼征服埃及

summary.en: Selim I’s Ottoman army, using field artillery and muskets, defeated the Mamluk sultan Tuman bay II outside Cairo. Tuman bay was hanged at the Zuwayla gate, ending the Mamluk Sultanate; Egypt became an Ottoman province for three centuries.
summary.zh: 塞利姆一世的奥斯曼军队凭借野战火炮与火枪在开罗城外击败马穆鲁克苏丹图曼贝伊二世。图曼贝伊被吊死于祖韦拉门，马穆鲁克王朝灭亡，埃及此后三个世纪为奥斯曼行省。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Ridaniya
Ibn Iyas, Badaʾiʿ al-Zuhur (early 16th century)
Britannica: Mamluk

name.zh: 埃塞俄比亚—阿达尔战争

summary.en: Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi (“Gran”) of Adal routed Emperor Lebna Dengel at Shimbra Kure in 1529 and overran most of the Christian highlands. Aided by a Portuguese expedition of 400 musketeers that landed in 1541, Emperor Gelawdewos killed the imam at Wayna Daga in 1543.
summary.zh: 阿达尔苏丹国的伊玛目艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐（“格兰”）于1529年在申布拉库雷大败皇帝莱布纳·丹格尔，占领基督教高原大部。1541年四百名葡萄牙火枪手登陆驰援，1543年格拉德沃斯皇帝在其协助下于韦纳达加击毙伊玛目。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Ethiopian–Adal War
Shihab al-Din ʿArab Faqih, Futuh al-Habasha (c. 1559)
Miguel de Castanhoso, account of the Portuguese expedition to Abyssinia (1564)
Richard Pankhurst, The Ethiopians: A History (1998)
Arab Faqih, Futuh al-Habasha, trans. P. L. Stenhouse (2003)

note: Marker placed near Wayna Daga (east of Lake Tana); the war ranged across the whole highlands.

story.en:
Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim, called Gragn (“the left-handed”) in Amharic, united the Somali and Afar troops of the Adal sultanate around Harar and declared jihad on the Christian empire. At Shimbra Kure in March 1529 he routed Emperor Lebna Dengel, and over the next decade his armies burned monasteries and churches across the highlands, including, by Ethiopian accounts, the cathedral of Aksum. His secretary Arab Faqih recorded the campaigns in the Futuh al-Habasha, “Conquest of Abyssinia”.

Lebna Dengel died a fugitive at the mountain monastery of Debre Damo in 1540, having appealed to Portugal. In 1541 some 400 musketeers under Cristóvão da Gama, a son of Vasco da Gama, landed at Massawa. Cristóvão was captured and beheaded by the imam in 1542, but his surviving men joined the young emperor Gelawdewos, and at Wayna Daga in February 1543 Ahmad was shot dead and his army scattered.

The war exhausted both states. Into the depopulated lands of the south moved Oromo pastoralists, whose migrations reshaped Ethiopia over the following century.
story.zh:
伊玛目艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣（阿姆哈拉语称“格兰”，意为“左撇子”）在哈勒尔一带联合阿达尔苏丹国的索马里和阿法尔部众，向基督教帝国宣布圣战。1529年3月，他在辛布拉·库雷大败皇帝列卜纳·丁格尔；此后十年间，他的军队在高原各地焚毁修道院和教堂，据埃塞俄比亚方面记载，阿克苏姆的大教堂也未能幸免。他的书记阿拉伯·法基赫在《阿比西尼亚征服记》中记录了这些战役。

列卜纳·丁格尔向葡萄牙求援，1540年流亡至山顶修道院德布雷达莫时去世。1541年，瓦斯科·达·伽马之子克里斯托旺·达·伽马率约400名火枪手在马萨瓦登陆。1542年克里斯托旺被伊玛目俘获并斩首，但幸存的葡萄牙人与年轻的皇帝加拉多斯会合；1543年2月在瓦伊纳达加，艾哈迈德中弹身亡，其军溃散。

战争使双方都精疲力竭。奥罗莫牧民随后迁入南部人口锐减的土地，他们的迁徙在此后一个世纪里重塑了埃塞俄比亚。

name.en: Battle of Alcácer Quibir (Battle of the Three Kings)
name.zh: 阿尔卡塞尔基比尔战役（三王之战）

summary.en: The Saadian sultan ʿAbd al-Malik crushed the invading army of King Sebastian of Portugal and his ally al-Mutawakkil. All three kings died; Ahmad al-Mansur took the Moroccan throne enriched by ransoms, while Portugal’s succession crisis led to union with Spain in 1580.
summary.zh: 萨阿德王朝苏丹阿卜杜勒·马利克大败入侵的葡萄牙国王塞巴斯蒂昂及其盟友穆塔瓦基勒。三位君主皆死于此役；艾哈迈德·曼苏尔凭赎金之利继承摩洛哥王位，而葡萄牙的继承危机导致其1580年与西班牙合并。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Alcácer Quibir
E. W. Bovill, The Battle of Alcazar (1952)
Britannica: Battle of Alcácer Quibir
Britannica: Battle of Alcazarquivir

story.en:
King Sebastian of Portugal, aged 24 and dreaming of crusade, landed in Morocco in 1578 to restore the deposed sultan Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad al-Mutawakkil against his uncle ʿAbd al-Malik. On 4 August, near the Wadi al-Makhazin outside Ksar el-Kebir, his army of about 20,000, heavy with nobles and foreign mercenaries, met a larger Moroccan force rich in cavalry and artillery.

ʿAbd al-Malik was already gravely ill; he died during the fighting, and his attendants hid his death so the army would not lose heart. The Portuguese were surrounded and destroyed. Al-Mutawakkil drowned trying to cross the river, and Sebastian vanished in the melee; a body identified as his was later handed over. Because no one was sure he had died, Portuguese “Sebastianism” long awaited his return.

ʿAbd al-Malik’s brother Ahmad was proclaimed sultan on the battlefield and took the name al-Mansur, “the Victorious”. Ransoms for thousands of captive nobles enriched Morocco, while Portugal, with no heir, passed to Philip II of Spain in 1580.
story.zh:
1578年，年仅24岁、怀抱十字军梦想的葡萄牙国王塞巴斯蒂昂在摩洛哥登陆，企图帮助被废黜的苏丹穆塔瓦基勒打败其叔父阿卜杜·马利克。8月4日，在凯比尔堡城外的马哈赞河附近，他那支约两万人、充斥贵族和外国雇佣兵的军队，遭遇了一支骑兵和火炮都占优势的更庞大的摩洛哥军队。

阿卜杜·马利克此时已病入膏肓，在战斗中死去，侍从秘不发丧以免军心动摇。葡萄牙军被包围歼灭。穆塔瓦基勒渡河时溺毙，塞巴斯蒂昂则在混战中失踪，后来交还的一具尸体被认定是他。由于无人能确定他已死，葡萄牙长期流行期待国王归来的“塞巴斯蒂昂主义”。

阿卜杜·马利克之弟艾哈迈德在战场上被拥立为苏丹，号“曼苏尔”，意为“胜利者”。数千名被俘贵族的赎金使摩洛哥大为富足，而无嗣的葡萄牙则于1580年归于西班牙国王腓力二世。

summary.en: After a gruelling Saharan crossing, a Moroccan army of musketeers under Judar Pasha, sent by Ahmad al-Mansur, routed the much larger Songhai host of Askia Ishaq II near Gao. The Songhai Empire collapsed and Timbuktu came under Moroccan pashas.
summary.zh: 艾哈迈德·曼苏尔派遣朱达尔帕夏率火枪部队艰苦穿越撒哈拉，在加奥附近击溃阿斯基亚·伊斯哈格二世人数远多于己的桑海大军。桑海帝国随之崩溃，廷巴克图落入摩洛哥帕夏统治之下。

story.en:
Sultan Ahmad al-Mansur of Morocco, eager to control the gold of the western Sudan, sent an expedition across the Sahara in late 1590 against the advice of his counsellors. It was led by Judar Pasha, a Spanish-born convert, and numbered some 4,000 soldiers, many of them arquebusiers and renegades from Iberia, with thousands of camels. Many men died during the crossing of about four months.

At Tondibi, north of Gao, Askia Ishaq II met them with a far larger army. According to the Timbuktu chronicles, the Songhai drove a herd of cattle ahead of their lines to break the Moroccan ranks; the gunfire terrified the animals, which turned back into the Songhai themselves. Musket volleys did the rest, and the askia fled.

Judar found Gao a disappointment, but the Moroccans occupied Timbuktu and Djenné, and in 1594 deported scholars including Ahmad Baba to Marrakesh. Songhai resistance continued downriver in Dendi, but the empire never revived. The pashas of Timbuktu soon became an independent military caste, and the trans-Saharan trade declined.
story.zh:
摩洛哥苏丹艾哈迈德·曼苏尔渴望控制西苏丹的黄金，不顾谋臣劝阻，于1590年底派遣远征军穿越撒哈拉。统帅朱达尔帕夏是一位生于西班牙的改宗者，军队约四千人，其中许多是火绳枪手和来自伊比利亚的叛教者，另有数千头骆驼。约四个月的沙漠行军中有大量士兵死亡。

在加奥以北的通迪比，桑海国王阿斯基亚·伊斯哈格二世率远为庞大的军队迎战。据廷巴克图编年史记载，桑海人驱赶一群牛走在阵前，试图冲散摩洛哥军阵；不料枪声惊吓了牛群，它们掉头冲向桑海人自己。火枪齐射随后决定了胜负，阿斯基亚败逃。

朱达尔对加奥大失所望，但摩洛哥人占领了廷巴克图和杰内，并于1594年把艾哈迈德·巴巴等学者押往马拉喀什。桑海人在下游的丹迪继续抵抗，但帝国再未复兴。廷巴克图的帕夏们不久便成为独立的军事集团，跨撒哈拉贸易随之衰落。

name.en: Fasilides makes Gondar the imperial capital
name.zh: 法西利达斯定都贡德尔

summary.en: Emperor Fasilides ended the roving royal camps of the Ethiopian monarchy by founding a permanent capital at Gondar, north of Lake Tana. His castle began the Fasil Ghebbi compound, whose palaces blend Aksumite, Indian and Portuguese-influenced styles.
summary.zh: 皇帝法西利达斯结束了埃塞俄比亚君主四处移驻的营帐制度，在塔纳湖以北的贡德尔建立永久都城。其城堡开启了法西尔盖比王宫建筑群，融合了阿克苏姆、印度与葡萄牙影响的风格。

name.en: Dutch East India Company settles at the Cape
name.zh: 荷兰东印度公司在开普建立据点

summary.en: Jan van Riebeeck landed at Table Bay to found a provisioning station for VOC ships. Expansion of free burgher farms dispossessed Khoikhoi herders, and enslaved people from Asia and Africa formed much of the labour force, laying foundations of later South African society.
summary.zh: 扬·范里贝克在桌湾登陆，为东印度公司船只建立补给站。自由市民农场的扩张夺走了科伊科伊牧民的土地，来自亚洲和非洲的奴隶构成主要劳动力，奠定了后来南非社会的基础。

summary.en: Forces of Portuguese Angola and their Imbangala allies defeated the army of the Kingdom of Kongo; King António I was killed and beheaded. The defeat plunged Kongo into decades of civil war between rival royal houses.
summary.zh: 葡属安哥拉军队及其因班加拉盟军击败刚果王国军队，国王安东尼奥一世阵亡并被斩首。此役使刚果陷入敌对王族之间长达数十年的内战。

name.en: Battle of Feyiase: rise of Asante
name.zh: 费亚斯战役：阿散蒂崛起

summary.en: The Asante confederacy under Osei Tutu, united by the priest Okomfo Anokye around the Golden Stool, defeated its overlord Denkyira. Independence gave Asante control of gold and trade routes to the coast and launched its expansion into a major West African empire.
summary.zh: 奥塞·图图领导、由祭司奥孔福·阿诺基以“金凳子”凝聚的阿散蒂联盟击败宗主国登基拉。独立使阿散蒂掌握了黄金与通往海岸的商路，开始扩张为西非强国。

summary.en: Over three and a half centuries about 12.5 million Africans were forced aboard ships for the Americas, of whom some 10.7 million survived the Middle Passage. Ports such as Ouidah, Luanda and Bonny were central; the trade reshaped African states and demography until its suppression in the 19th century.
summary.zh: 三个半世纪间，约1250万非洲人被强行押上驶往美洲的船只，约1070万人在“中间航程”中幸存。维达、罗安达、邦尼等港口为其中心；这一贸易深刻改变了非洲的国家与人口，直至19世纪被禁绝。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Atlantic slave trade

Herbert S. Klein, The Atlantic Slave Trade (2nd ed., 2010)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. V: Africa from the Sixteenth to the Eighteenth Century (ed. B. A. Ogot, 1992)

note: Start and end years are conventions (first direct Africa–Americas voyages c. 1501–1525; last documented voyages 1866–67). Marker placed at Ouidah, a leading embarkation port. Estimates from SlaveVoyages.

story.en:
The trade grew from Portuguese voyages along the Guinea coast into a system that linked African rulers and merchants, European chartered companies and American plantations. Captives, many taken in wars or raids far inland, were marched to coastal forts and barracoons, then packed below deck for a crossing of weeks or months. The SlaveVoyages database estimates that about 12.5 million people embarked and 10.7 million survived the Middle Passage; the peak came in the 18th century.

African voices survive. In 1526 King Afonso I of Kongo wrote to the king of Portugal that traders were seizing his own subjects and nobles. Olaudah Equiano’s 1789 memoir described being kidnapped as a child in Igboland, though some historians question whether he was born in Africa. At Ouidah, a road of memory now leads from the old slave market to the beach and a “Door of No Return”, dedicated in 1995.

Britain and the United States banned the trade in 1807–1808, but ships kept sailing to Brazil until 1850 and to Cuba until 1866–67. Its legacies include depopulation, militarised states and the African diaspora of the Americas.
story.zh:
这一贸易从葡萄牙人沿几内亚海岸的航行发展而来，逐渐形成一个把非洲统治者和商人、欧洲特许公司与美洲种植园连接起来的体系。俘虏多在内陆的战争或劫掠中被抓获，被押送到沿海的堡垒和奴隶棚，再被塞进船舱，经历数周乃至数月的航程。据“奴隶航程”数据库估计，约1250万人被运上船，约1070万人在“中间航道”中幸存；高峰出现在18世纪。

非洲人的声音流传了下来。1526年，刚果国王阿方索一世致信葡萄牙国王，抱怨商人掳掠他的臣民乃至贵族。奥拉达·艾奎亚诺1789年的回忆录描述了自己幼年在伊博地区被绑架的经历，不过也有史家怀疑他是否生于非洲。在维达，如今有一条纪念之路从昔日的奴隶市场通往海滩，尽头是1995年落成的“不归门”。

英国和美国于1807—1808年禁止奴隶贸易，但运奴船直到1850年仍驶往巴西，直到1866—1867年仍驶往古巴。其遗产包括人口流失、军事化的国家以及美洲的非洲离散族群。

summary.en: About 1,100 Black Loyalists from Nova Scotia, freed for serving Britain in the American war, founded Freetown under the abolitionist Sierra Leone Company. It later became the base of the Royal Navy’s anti-slavery squadron and home to tens of thousands of liberated Africans.
summary.zh: 约1100名来自新斯科舍的黑人效忠派（因在美国独立战争中为英国作战而获自由）在废奴主义的塞拉利昂公司支持下建立弗里敦。此后它成为英国皇家海军反奴隶贸易舰队的基地，数万名获释非洲人在此定居。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Freetown
Christopher Fyfe, A History of Sierra Leone (1962)

name.en: Sokoto jihad of Usman dan Fodio
name.zh: 奥斯曼·丹·福迪奥的索科托圣战

summary.en: The Fulani scholar Usman dan Fodio declared jihad against the Hausa king of Gobir, accusing rulers of injustice and syncretism. By 1808 his followers had toppled most Hausa kingdoms, forming the Sokoto Caliphate, the largest state in 19th-century West Africa and a centre of Islamic scholarship.
summary.zh: 富拉尼学者奥斯曼·丹·福迪奥指责豪萨统治者暴虐、信仰混杂，向戈比尔国王宣布圣战。至1808年其追随者推翻大部分豪萨王国，建立索科托哈里发国——19世纪西非最大的国家和伊斯兰学术中心。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Jihad of Usman dan Fodio
Murray Last, The Sokoto Caliphate (1967)
Mervyn Hiskett, The Sword of Truth: The Life and Times of the Shehu Usuman dan Fodio (1973)
Jean Boyd and Beverly B. Mack, The Collected Works of Nana Asmaʾu (1997)

note: QID is the Sokoto jihad proper (Wikidata “Sokoto Revolution”, 1804–1808); Gobir declared war on 21 February 1804, just after the hijra to Gudu. Marker at Sokoto.

story.en:
Usman dan Fodio had preached for some thirty years in the Hausa kingdom of Gobir, criticising heavy taxes, the enslavement of Muslims and rulers who mixed Islam with older rites. When King Yunfa moved against his community at Degel, Usman withdrew with his followers to Gudu in February 1804, a hijra consciously modelled on the Prophet’s flight to Medina. They elected him commander of the faithful, and Gobir declared war.

In June 1804 his outnumbered followers won at Tabkin Kwotto. Flag-bearers who received banners from the shehu then raised revolts across Hausaland, and by 1808 Kano, Katsina and Zaria had fallen and the Gobir capital Alkalawa was stormed, with Yunfa killed.

Usman left government to his son Muhammad Bello, who built Sokoto as capital, and to his brother Abdullahi at Gwandu. His daughter Nana Asmaʾu, a poet in Arabic, Fulfulde and Hausa, organised a network of women teachers. The caliphate of some thirty emirates lasted until the British conquest in 1903, and its sultan remains the spiritual leader of Nigeria’s Muslims.
story.zh:
奥斯曼·丹·福迪奥在豪萨王国戈比尔传道约三十年，批评苛捐杂税、奴役穆斯林以及统治者把伊斯兰教与旧有仪式混杂的做法。国王云法对他在德格尔的团体动手后，奥斯曼于1804年2月率追随者退往古杜，这次“希吉拉”有意效仿先知迁往麦地那。追随者推举他为“信士的长官”，戈比尔随即宣战。

1804年6月，他寡不敌众的追随者在塔布金·夸托取胜。从谢胡手中接过旗帜的各路首领随后在豪萨地区纷纷起事；到1808年，卡诺、卡齐纳和扎里亚相继陷落，戈比尔都城阿卡拉瓦被攻破，云法被杀。

奥斯曼把政务交给儿子穆罕默德·贝洛（他营建索科托为都城）和驻守关杜的弟弟阿卜杜拉希。他的女儿娜娜·阿斯玛乌用阿拉伯语、富拉语和豪萨语写诗，并组织起一个女教师网络。这个由约三十个酋长国组成的哈里发国一直延续到1903年被英国征服，其苏丹至今仍是尼日利亚穆斯林的精神领袖。

summary.en: A period of wars, migrations and state formation in southern Africa accompanied the rise of the Zulu kingdom. New polities such as Moshoeshoe’s Lesotho, the Ndebele and the Gaza emerged; historians debate how far drought, the Delagoa Bay trade and colonial slaving drove the upheaval.
summary.zh: 祖鲁王国崛起期间，南部非洲经历了战争、迁徙与新国家形成的时期。莫舒舒的莱索托、恩德贝莱、加扎等新政权相继出现；干旱、德拉瓜湾贸易与殖民掠奴各在多大程度上推动了这一动乱，史学界仍有争论。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Mfecane
Carolyn Hamilton (ed.), The Mfecane Aftermath: Reconstructive Debates in Southern African History (1995)
J. D. Omer-Cooper, The Zulu Aftermath (1966)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. VI: Africa in the Nineteenth Century until the 1880s (ed. J. F. Ade Ajayi, 1989)

note: Both the concept and its dates are contested (Cobbing critique, 1988).

summary.en: France landed at Sidi Ferruch and took Algiers from its Ottoman dey in 1830. Emir ʿAbd al-Qadir led organised resistance until 1847, and Kabylia rose again in 1871; the long, brutal conquest made Algeria a settler colony annexed to France.
summary.zh: 1830年法国在西迪费鲁什登陆，从奥斯曼的德伊手中夺取阿尔及尔。埃米尔阿卜杜·卡迪尔领导有组织的抵抗直至1847年，卡比利亚于1871年再度起义；漫长而残酷的征服使阿尔及利亚成为并入法国的移民殖民地。

sources.title: Wikipedia: French conquest of Algeria
Benjamin Stora, Algeria 1830–2000: A Short History (2001)
Britannica: ʿAbd al-Qādir
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. VI: Africa in the Nineteenth Century until the 1880s (ed. J. F. Ade Ajayi, 1989)
John Ruedy, Modern Algeria: The Origins and Development of a Nation (2nd ed., 2005)

note: End date conventional: Wikidata gives 1904, many accounts 1903 (Saharan campaigns).

story.en:
The pretext was a quarrel over debts. In 1827, during an argument about unpaid French bills for Algerian wheat, Dey Hussein struck the French consul Pierre Deval with a fly-whisk. Charles X’s government, seeking prestige at home, blockaded Algiers and in June 1830 landed some 34,000 troops at Sidi Ferruch; the dey capitulated on 5 July.

The young emir ʿAbd al-Qadir, proclaimed in 1832, built a state with its own army and administration in the interior and twice forced France to negotiate. Marshal Bugeaud answered with mobile columns that burned crops and villages; in 1845 Colonel Pélissier’s troops suffocated hundreds of people who had taken refuge in the Dahra caves. ʿAbd al-Qadir surrendered in 1847 and later, in exile in Damascus, protected Christians during the massacres of 1860.

Algeria was declared part of France in 1848 and opened to European settlers who took the best land. The great Kabyle revolt of 1871 was crushed, and Saharan campaigns ran into the 1900s.
story.zh:
借口是一场债务纠纷。1827年，在就法国拖欠阿尔及利亚小麦货款发生争吵时，阿尔及尔总督侯赛因用拂尘击打了法国领事皮埃尔·德瓦尔。查理十世政府为在国内博取声望，封锁阿尔及尔，并于1830年6月在西迪费鲁赫登陆约3.4万兵力；总督于7月5日投降。

1832年被拥立的年轻埃米尔阿卜杜·卡迪尔在内陆建立起拥有军队和行政机构的国家，两度迫使法国谈判。比若元帅以机动纵队焚烧庄稼和村庄作为回应；1845年，佩利西耶上校的部队在达赫拉山洞中使数百名避难者窒息而死。阿卜杜·卡迪尔于1847年投降，后来流亡大马士革期间，在1860年的屠杀中保护了基督徒。

1848年阿尔及利亚被宣布为法国领土，向欧洲移民开放，最好的土地落入他们手中。1871年卡比利亚大起义遭到镇压，撒哈拉地区的战事则一直持续到20世纪初。

summary.en: Thousands of Dutch-speaking Boers left the British Cape Colony with their servants and herds, moving onto the highveld and into Natal. Clashes with the Ndebele and Zulu, including Blood River in 1838, led to the Boer republics of Transvaal and Orange Free State.
summary.zh: 数千名讲荷兰语的布尔人携仆从与牲畜离开英属开普殖民地，迁入高地草原与纳塔尔。他们与恩德贝莱人、祖鲁人发生冲突（包括1838年血河之战），最终建立德兰士瓦和奥兰治自由邦两个布尔共和国。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Great Trek
Hermann Giliomee, The Afrikaners: Biography of a People (2003)
Norman Etherington, The Great Treks: The Transformation of Southern Africa, 1815–1854 (2001)
Britannica: Great Trek
Leonard Thompson, A History of South Africa (3rd ed., 2001)

note: Date range follows Wikidata (1836–1852, to the Sand River Convention); many accounts date the main movement 1835–1840s.

story.en:
From the mid-1830s parties of Dutch-speaking farmers, later called Voortrekkers, loaded ox-wagons and left the eastern Cape. They resented British rule, the emancipation of slaves in 1834 and what they saw as poor protection on the frontier. Perhaps 12,000 to 15,000 people, with their servants and livestock, crossed the Orange River over the next decade.

The highveld they entered had been disrupted by the wars of the Mfecane, but it was not empty. Trekkers fought Mzilikazi’s Ndebele, who withdrew north across the Limpopo. In Natal, the Zulu king Dingane had the trek leader Piet Retief and his party killed at uMgungundlovu in February 1838. On 16 December 1838 Andries Pretorius’s laager of wagons beat back a Zulu army at the Ncome River, which ran red and was renamed Blood River.

Britain annexed the trekkers’ republic of Natalia in 1843, but recognised the Transvaal in 1852 and the Orange Free State in 1854. The centenary re-enactment of 1938 became a rallying point for Afrikaner nationalism and, a decade later, apartheid.
story.zh:
从19世纪30年代中期起，一批批说荷兰语的农民（后称“开拓者”）装上牛车离开开普东部。他们不满英国统治、1834年的奴隶解放，以及在他们看来边境防护不力。此后十年间，约一万二千至一万五千人带着仆役和牲畜渡过奥兰治河。

他们进入的高原已被姆菲卡尼战争搅乱，但并非无人之地。开拓者与姆兹利卡齐的恩德贝莱人交战，后者向北退过林波波河。在纳塔尔，祖鲁国王丁冈于1838年2月在乌姆贡贡德洛夫杀死了迁徙领袖皮特·雷蒂夫及其随行人员。1838年12月16日，安德里斯·比勒陀利乌斯以牛车围成的营垒在恩科姆河击退祖鲁大军，河水被染红，此河因而改称“血河”。

英国于1843年吞并了开拓者建立的纳塔利亚共和国，但在1852年和1854年先后承认德兰士瓦和奥兰治自由邦。1938年的百年纪念重演成为阿非利卡民族主义的集结号，十年后种族隔离制度随之而来。

summary.en: Built from 1859 by Ferdinand de Lesseps’s company with the forced labour of tens of thousands of Egyptian peasants, the canal opened under Khedive Ismaʿil, linking the Mediterranean and Red Sea. Egypt’s debts soon led it to sell its shares to Britain (1875).
summary.zh: 运河自1859年由斐迪南·德·雷赛布的公司修建，数万埃及农民被强征服役，在赫迪夫伊斯梅尔治下通航，连通地中海与红海。埃及因债务很快于1875年将其股份售予英国。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Suez Canal
Zachary Karabell, Parting the Desert: The Creation of the Suez Canal (2003)
Britannica: Suez Canal
Britannica: Suez Canal – History

story.en:
Ferdinand de Lesseps, a former French diplomat, won a concession from his friend Saʿid Pasha in 1854 and broke ground at what became Port Said in 1859. For years the digging relied on the corvée: tens of thousands of Egyptian peasants were levied each month to shift sand with picks and baskets, and thousands died of cholera and exhaustion before steam dredgers took over after 1864.

Khedive Ismaʿil turned the opening in November 1869 into a spectacle meant to show Egypt as part of Europe. Empress Eugénie of France led a procession of ships through the canal aboard the imperial yacht L’Aigle, and Ismaʿil built a new opera house in Cairo; Verdi’s Aida, commissioned for it, premiered in 1871.

The costs proved ruinous. In 1875 the bankrupt khedive sold Egypt’s 44 percent stake to Britain, which Prime Minister Disraeli financed with a loan from the Rothschilds. Debt led to European financial control, the ʿUrabi revolt and British occupation in 1882, and the canal stayed a flashpoint until Nasser nationalised it in 1956.
story.zh:
前法国外交官斐迪南·德·雷赛布于1854年从友人赛义德帕夏处获得特许权，1859年在后来的塞得港破土动工。多年来开凿依靠徭役：每月有数以万计的埃及农民被征调，用镐和筐搬运沙土，在1864年后蒸汽挖泥船接手之前，已有数千人死于霍乱和劳累。

赫迪夫伊斯梅尔把1869年11月的通航典礼办成一场盛会，意在展示埃及已是欧洲的一部分。法国皇后欧仁妮乘坐御用游艇“雄鹰号”率船队驶过运河；伊斯梅尔还在开罗新建歌剧院，为此委约的威尔第歌剧《阿依达》于1871年首演。

代价最终是毁灭性的。1875年，濒临破产的赫迪夫把埃及持有的44%股份卖给英国，首相迪斯雷利借罗斯柴尔德家族的贷款完成收购。债务导致欧洲接管埃及财政，引发奥拉比起义和1882年英国占领；直到1956年纳赛尔将其收归国有，运河始终是争端焦点。

summary.en: A Zulu army of about 20,000 under Ntshingwayo kaMahole overwhelmed the camp of a British column invading King Cetshwayo’s kingdom, killing over 1,300 soldiers. It was among the heaviest defeats of a modern army by an African force, though Britain went on to take Ulundi that July.
summary.zh: 恩茨欣瓦约·卡马霍莱率约两万祖鲁大军攻破入侵塞奇瓦约国王领地的英军营地，击毙一千三百余人。这是非洲军队对近代军队取得的最惨重胜利之一，但英军仍于同年7月攻占乌伦迪。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Isandlwana
Jeff Guy, The Destruction of the Zulu Kingdom (1979)
Ian Knight, Zulu Rising: The Epic Story of iSandlwana and Rorke’s Drift (2010)
Britannica: Battle of Isandlwana

story.en:
In January 1879 Lord Chelmsford invaded the Zulu kingdom after King Cetshwayo ignored an ultimatum designed to be refused. Confident that the Zulu would avoid open battle, Chelmsford split his central column on 22 January and rode out with half of it, leaving the camp beneath the crag of Isandlwana unentrenched under Lieutenant-Colonel Henry Pulleine.

A Zulu army of some 20,000, which British scouts had stumbled upon resting in a valley nearby, attacked in its classic “horns of the buffalo” formation: the chest pinned the British line while the horns swept around both flanks. When the over-extended British firing line fell back, the regiments broke into the camp; the old story that it ran out of ammunition is now doubted. A partial eclipse of the sun darkened the sky during the afternoon. More than 1,300 men of the British force died, along with about a thousand or more Zulu.

That night some 150 soldiers held the mission station at Rorke’s Drift, a defence Britain celebrated to soften the shock. Reinforced, Chelmsford burned Cetshwayo’s capital at Ulundi in July, and the kingdom was broken up.
story.zh:
1879年1月，切姆斯福德勋爵在祖鲁国王塞奇瓦约拒绝一份蓄意令其无法接受的最后通牒后入侵祖鲁王国。切姆斯福德自信祖鲁人会回避正面交战，于1月22日把中路纵队一分为二，亲率一半出营，把伊散德尔瓦纳岩峰下未构筑工事的营地交给亨利·普莱恩中校留守。

英军侦察兵在附近一处山谷偶然撞见正在休整的约两万祖鲁大军，后者随即以经典的“水牛角”阵型发起进攻：“胸部”牵制英军正面，两只“角”则从两翼包抄。战线过长的英军前沿后撤之际，祖鲁各团冲入营地；英军因弹药耗尽而溃败的旧说如今受到质疑。午后一次日偏食使天色昏暗。英军方面一千三百余人阵亡，祖鲁一方也死亡一千人以上。

当夜，约150名士兵守住了罗克渡口的传教站，英国大肆宣扬这场防御战以冲淡震惊。获得增援后，切姆斯福德于同年7月焚毁塞奇瓦约的都城乌伦迪，祖鲁王国被肢解。

name.en: ʿUrabi revolt and British occupation of Egypt
name.zh: 奥拉比起义与英国占领埃及

summary.en: Colonel Ahmad ʿUrabi led Egyptian officers and notables against foreign financial control and the Turco-Circassian elite under the slogan “Egypt for the Egyptians”. Britain bombarded Alexandria and defeated ʿUrabi at Tel el-Kebir in 1882, beginning an occupation that lasted until 1956.
summary.zh: 艾哈迈德·奥拉比上校率埃及军官与士绅，以“埃及人的埃及”为口号反对外国财政控制和土耳其—切尔克斯精英。1882年英国炮击亚历山大港，并在泰勒凯比尔击败奥拉比，开始了持续至1956年的占领。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Urabi revolt
Juan R. I. Cole, Colonialism and Revolution in the Middle East: Social and Cultural Origins of Egypt’s ʿUrabi Movement (1993)

summary.en: Fourteen states, with no African representatives, met in Bismarck’s Berlin to regulate European claims in Africa. The General Act recognised Leopold II’s Congo association, declared free trade on the Congo and Niger, and set “effective occupation” as the test of a claim, accelerating partition.
summary.zh: 十四国在俾斯麦主持下于柏林开会，规范欧洲在非洲的领土主张，没有任何非洲代表。总议定书承认利奥波德二世的刚果协会，宣布刚果河与尼日尔河自由通商，并以“有效占领”作为主张依据，加速了瓜分。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Berlin Conference
General Act of the Conference of Berlin (26 February 1885)
S. Förster, W. J. Mommsen & R. Robinson (eds.), Bismarck, Europe and Africa: The Berlin Africa Conference 1884–1885 (1988)
Thomas Pakenham, The Scramble for Africa (1991)
Britannica: Berlin West Africa Conference
S. Förster, W. J. Mommsen and R. Robinson (eds.), Bismarck, Europe and Africa: The Berlin Africa Conference 1884–1885 (1988)

story.en:
Bismarck, who had just declared German protectorates in Togo, Cameroon and South West Africa, convened the conference with France in November 1884 to settle disputes over the Congo basin and the Niger. Delegates of fourteen states, including the United States and the Ottoman Empire, met in his official residence on the Wilhelmstrasse. No African ruler was invited, not even the Sultan of Zanzibar, whose claims on the mainland were at stake.

The conference did not, as often said, carve up the continent on a map. Its General Act of 26 February 1885 did something with longer reach: it set the ground rules. Coastal claims had to be notified to the other powers and backed by “effective occupation”; trade on the Congo and Niger was declared free; the signatories promised to suppress the slave trade and to “watch over” native peoples.

In practice the Act blessed King Leopold II’s private Congo Free State and set off a race to sign treaties and plant garrisons inland. Within thirty years nearly all of Africa was under European rule.
story.zh:
俾斯麦刚刚宣布对多哥、喀麦隆和西南非洲实行保护，便于1884年11月与法国联合召开会议，以解决围绕刚果盆地和尼日尔河的争端。包括美国和奥斯曼帝国在内的十四国代表在他位于威廉大街的官邸开会。没有一位非洲统治者受到邀请，连大陆领地主张直接受影响的桑给巴尔苏丹也被排除在外。

会议并不像常说的那样在地图上瓜分了非洲大陆。1885年2月26日签署的《总议定书》影响更为深远：它制定了游戏规则。沿海领土主张须通告其他列强并以“有效占领”为依据；刚果河与尼日尔河宣布贸易自由；签字国承诺取缔奴隶贸易并“关照”当地人民。

实际上，《总议定书》认可了利奥波德二世私人拥有的刚果自由邦，并引发了深入内陆签约驻军的竞赛。不到三十年，几乎整个非洲都落入欧洲统治之下。

name.en: Mahdist siege and capture of Khartoum
name.zh: 马赫迪军围攻并攻克喀土穆

summary.en: Forces of Muhammad Ahmad, the self-proclaimed Mahdi, besieged the Egyptian-held capital of Sudan for ten months and stormed it on 26 January 1885, killing Governor-General Charles Gordon. The Mahdist state ruled Sudan from Omdurman until 1898.
summary.zh: 自称马赫迪的穆罕默德·艾哈迈德的军队围困埃及控制下的苏丹首府十个月，于1885年1月26日破城，总督查尔斯·戈登被杀。马赫迪国家以恩图曼为中心统治苏丹至1898年。

P. M. Holt, The Mahdist State in the Sudan, 1881–1898 (1958)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. VI: Africa in the Nineteenth Century until the 1880s (ed. J. F. Ade Ajayi, 1989)

summary.en: In barely three decades European powers claimed almost the whole continent through treaties, chartered companies and military conquest. Only Ethiopia, which defeated Italy, and Liberia remained independent, while resistance from Morocco to the Cape was widespread.
summary.zh: 短短三十余年间，欧洲列强通过条约、特许公司和军事征服瓜分了几乎整个非洲大陆。只有击败意大利的埃塞俄比亚和利比里亚保持独立，而从摩洛哥到开普，各地抵抗此起彼伏。

Thomas Pakenham, The Scramble for Africa (1991)

note: Wikidata starts the Scramble in 1885; many historians begin with the French move on Tunisia (1881). Marker at Boma, first capital of the Congo Free State.

story.en:
In 1880 European states held little of Africa beyond Algeria, the Cape, a scatter of coastal forts and Portuguese Angola and Mozambique. France’s protectorate over Tunisia in 1881 and Britain’s occupation of Egypt in 1882 set off a rivalry in which no power wanted to be left out. Explorers and agents raced inland to collect “treaties” from chiefs who often had no idea they were signing away sovereignty, and chartered companies such as Cecil Rhodes’s British South Africa Company and the Royal Niger Company governed vast territories for profit.

The conquests rested on firepower. Hilaire Belloc’s satirical verse of 1898 summed it up: “we have got the Maxim gun, and they have not.” At Omdurman that year machine guns and artillery killed some 10,000 Sudanese in a morning.

Resistance was everywhere: Samori Touré in the western Sudan, the Ndebele and Shona risings of 1896–97, Asante, Maji Maji, the Herero and Nama. By 1914 only Ethiopia, which had beaten Italy at Adwa, and Liberia remained independent, and the borders drawn then largely survive today.
story.zh:
1880年时，欧洲国家在非洲所占的不过是阿尔及利亚、开普、零星的沿海堡垒，以及葡萄牙的安哥拉和莫桑比克。1881年法国对突尼斯实行保护、1882年英国占领埃及，引发了一场谁都不愿落后的角逐。探险家和代理人争相深入内陆，向往往不知自己正在出让主权的酋长们收集“条约”；塞西尔·罗得斯的英国南非公司和皇家尼日尔公司等特许公司为牟利而统治着广袤领土。

征服依靠的是火力。希莱尔·贝洛克1898年的讽刺诗一语道破：“我们有马克沁机枪，而他们没有。”同年在恩图曼，机枪和大炮在一个上午就杀死约一万名苏丹人。

抵抗无处不在：西苏丹的萨摩里·杜尔、1896—1897年恩德贝莱人和绍纳人的起义、阿散蒂、马及马及起义、赫雷罗人和纳马人。到1914年，只有在阿杜瓦打败意大利的埃塞俄比亚和利比里亚保持独立，而当时划定的边界大多沿用至今。

summary.en: Emperor Menelik II and Empress Taytu’s army of perhaps 100,000 decisively defeated an Italian invasion force under General Baratieri. Italy recognised Ethiopian independence in the Treaty of Addis Ababa, and Adwa became an enduring symbol of African resistance to colonialism.
summary.zh: 孟尼利克二世皇帝与泰图皇后率领约十万大军，决定性地击败巴拉蒂耶里将军指挥的意大利入侵军。意大利在《亚的斯亚贝巴条约》中承认埃塞俄比亚独立，阿杜瓦成为非洲反殖民抵抗的不朽象征。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Adwa
Raymond Jonas, The Battle of Adwa: African Victory in the Age of Empire (2011)
Bahru Zewde, A History of Modern Ethiopia, 1855–1991 (2nd ed., 2001)
Britannica: Battle of Adwa

story.en:
The war grew out of a translation. In the 1889 Treaty of Wuchale, the Italian text of Article 17 made Ethiopia an Italian protectorate in foreign affairs, while the Amharic version merely allowed Menelik to use Italy’s diplomats if he wished. Menelik repudiated the treaty, and in 1895 Italian forces from Eritrea pushed into Tigray.

Menelik mobilised an army of perhaps 100,000, many armed with modern rifles bought from France and Russia, and Empress Taytu led her own contingent. Under pressure from Rome to win quickly, General Oreste Baratieri ordered a night advance on 29 February 1896 with about 17,000 men. With poor maps in broken mountain country, his brigades lost contact, and at dawn on 1 March Ethiopian forces destroyed them one by one. More than 6,000 Italian and Eritrean askari soldiers were killed and some 3,000 captured.

Crispi’s government fell, and the Treaty of Addis Ababa in October recognised Ethiopia’s full independence. Adwa, still a public holiday in Ethiopia, became a symbol for pan-Africanists and Black communities worldwide.
story.zh:
这场战争源于一处翻译分歧。1889年《乌查利条约》第17条的意大利文本把埃塞俄比亚的外交置于意大利保护之下，而阿姆哈拉文本只规定孟尼利克在愿意时可借助意大利外交官。孟尼利克宣布废除条约，1895年意大利军队从厄立特里亚攻入提格雷。

孟尼利克动员了约十万大军，许多士兵装备了从法国和俄国购买的新式步枪，皇后泰图则率领她自己的部队。迫于罗马要求速胜的压力，奥雷斯特·巴拉蒂耶里将军于1896年2月29日下令约一万七千人夜间推进。在崎岖山地中，各旅地图粗陋，彼此失去联络；3月1日拂晓，埃塞俄比亚军队将其逐一歼灭。六千余名意大利士兵和厄立特里亚土著兵阵亡，约三千人被俘。

克里斯皮政府随即倒台，同年10月的《亚的斯亚贝巴条约》承认埃塞俄比亚完全独立。阿杜瓦战役纪念日至今仍是埃塞俄比亚的公共假日，它也成为泛非主义者和全世界黑人社群的象征。

name.zh: 南非战争（第二次布尔战争）

summary.en: Britain fought the Transvaal and Orange Free State over control of the gold-rich interior. Its scorched-earth tactics and concentration camps killed tens of thousands of Boer and Black African civilians; the Treaty of Vereeniging (1902) led to the Union of South Africa in 1910.
summary.zh: 英国与德兰士瓦和奥兰治自由邦为争夺富含黄金的内陆而战。英军的焦土战术与集中营造成数万布尔人和非洲黑人平民死亡；1902年《弗里尼欣和约》之后，1910年成立南非联邦。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Second Boer War
Thomas Pakenham, The Boer War (1979)
Peter Warwick, Black People and the South African War, 1899–1902 (1983)
Britannica: South African War
Elizabeth van Heyningen, The Concentration Camps of the Anglo-Boer War: A Social History (2013)

story.en:
The discovery of gold on the Witwatersrand in 1886 made Paul Kruger’s South African Republic the richest territory in Africa and drew in tens of thousands of foreign miners, the uitlanders, whom Kruger denied the vote. After the failed Jameson Raid of 1895–96 and months of brinkmanship by Britain’s Alfred Milner, Kruger issued an ultimatum, and war began in October 1899.

Boer commandos besieged Ladysmith, Kimberley and Mafeking and inflicted three defeats on the British in “Black Week” of December 1899. Massive reinforcements under Lord Roberts took Bloemfontein and Pretoria in 1900, but the Boers turned to guerrilla war. Kitchener replied by burning farms and herding civilians into camps. The British campaigner Emily Hobhouse exposed conditions there: some 26,000 Boer women and children died, and at least 14,000 Black Africans died in separate camps that drew far less notice.

The Treaty of Vereeniging in May 1902 annexed both republics but left the question of the Black franchise to a later self-governing white government, a bargain that shaped the Union of 1910.
story.zh:
1886年威特沃特斯兰德发现金矿，使保罗·克鲁格的南非共和国成为非洲最富庶的地区，也吸引了数万名外国矿工（称“外侨”），而克鲁格拒绝给予他们选举权。1895—1896年詹姆森突袭失败后，英国的阿尔弗雷德·米尔纳又进行了数月边缘政策，克鲁格发出最后通牒，战争于1899年10月爆发。

布尔突击队围困莱迪史密斯、金伯利和马弗京，并在1899年12月的“黑色星期”中三次击败英军。罗伯茨勋爵率大批援军于1900年攻占布隆方丹和比勒陀利亚，布尔人却转入游击战。基奇纳以焚烧农庄、把平民赶进集中营作为回应。英国社会活动家艾米莉·霍布豪斯揭露了营中惨状：约二万六千名布尔妇女儿童死亡，另有至少一万四千名黑人死于很少受到关注的另设营地。

1902年5月的《弗里尼欣条约》吞并了两个共和国，却把黑人选举权问题留给日后的白人自治政府决定，这一妥协塑造了1910年成立的南非联邦。

summary.en: When the British governor demanded to sit on the Golden Stool, the sacred symbol of Asante nationhood, Queen Mother Yaa Asantewaa of Ejisu led an uprising that besieged the British fort at Kumasi. The rising was crushed and Asante annexed, but the Stool itself was never surrendered.
summary.zh: 英国总督要求坐上阿散蒂民族的神圣象征“金凳子”，埃吉苏王太后雅阿·阿散蒂瓦随即领导起义，围攻库马西的英军堡垒。起义被镇压、阿散蒂遭吞并，但金凳子始终未被交出。

sources.title: Wikipedia: War of the Golden Stool
A. Adu Boahen, Yaa Asantewaa and the Asante–British War of 1900–1 (2003)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. VII: Africa under Colonial Domination 1880–1935 (ed. A. Adu Boahen, 1985)

name.zh: 赫雷罗人和纳马人种族灭绝

summary.en: After the Herero and Nama rose against German rule in South West Africa, General von Trotha issued an extermination order; survivors were driven into the Omaheke desert or concentration camps. Most Herero and about half the Nama died. Germany acknowledged the events as genocide in 2021.
summary.zh: 赫雷罗人和纳马人起义反抗德属西南非洲统治后，冯·特罗塔将军下达灭绝令，幸存者被驱入奥马赫科沙漠或集中营。大多数赫雷罗人和约半数纳马人死亡。德国于2021年承认其为种族灭绝。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Herero and Nama genocide
David Olusoga & Casper W. Erichsen, The Kaiser’s Holocaust (2010)
Jürgen Zimmerer & Joachim Zeller (eds.), Genocide in German South-West Africa (2008)
David Olusoga and Casper W. Erichsen, The Kaiser’s Holocaust (2010)
Britannica: Herero and Nama genocide

note: Marker at the Waterberg, site of the decisive battle of August 1904 (approximate).

story.en:
German settlers in South West Africa had been taking Herero cattle and land for years when, in January 1904, the Herero under Samuel Maharero rose and killed about 120 Germans, mostly male settlers. Berlin sent General Lothar von Trotha, who surrounded the Herero at the Waterberg in August. The encirclement was left open to the east, and the Herero, with their families and herds, fled into the waterless Omaheke sandveld.

On 2 October 1904 von Trotha proclaimed that every Herero within the German border, armed or unarmed, would be shot, and patrols sealed the desert’s waterholes. Thousands died of thirst. The Nama under Hendrik Witbooi rose that autumn and fought a guerrilla war until 1908. Survivors of both peoples were sent to concentration camps such as Shark Island at Lüderitz, where most prisoners died, and skulls were shipped to Germany for racial research.

The Herero fell from perhaps 80,000 to about 15,000, and around half the Nama perished. Germany returned remains from 2011 onward and in 2021 called the events genocide, offering €1.1 billion in aid, an offer many Herero and Nama leaders rejected as inadequate.
story.zh:
德国移民多年来不断夺取赫雷罗人的牛群和土地。1904年1月，赫雷罗人在萨穆埃尔·马哈雷罗领导下起义，杀死约120名德国人，多为男性移民。柏林派出洛塔尔·冯·特罗塔将军，他于8月在瓦特贝格包围赫雷罗人。包围圈东面留有缺口，赫雷罗人携家带口、赶着牛群逃入缺水的奥马赫凯沙地。

1904年10月2日，冯·特罗塔宣布德国边界内的每个赫雷罗人，无论有无武器，一律枪决，巡逻队封锁了沙漠中的水源，成千上万人渴死。同年秋，亨德里克·维特布伊领导的纳马人起义，游击战一直持续到1908年。两族幸存者被送往吕德里茨的鲨鱼岛等集中营，大多数囚犯死在那里，头骨还被运往德国供种族研究。

赫雷罗人从约八万人锐减到约一万五千人，纳马人约半数死亡。德国自2011年起陆续归还遗骸，2021年承认这些事件为种族灭绝，并提出提供11亿欧元援助，但许多赫雷罗和纳马领袖认为这远远不够而予以拒绝。

summary.en: Peoples of southern German East Africa, resisting forced cotton cultivation and taxes, rose together, many trusting sacred water (maji) from the prophet Kinjikitile to turn bullets. German famine tactics left perhaps 75,000–300,000 dead.
summary.zh: 德属东非南部各族因反抗强制种植棉花和苛税而联合起义，许多人相信先知金吉基提勒所赐的圣水（“马及”）能化解子弹。德军的饥荒战术造成约7.5万至30万人死亡。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Maji Maji Rebellion
John Iliffe, A Modern History of Tanganyika (1979)
G. C. K. Gwassa & John Iliffe (eds.), Records of the Maji Maji Rising (1967)

note: Marker in the Matumbi Hills where the rising began (approximate); death toll estimates vary widely.

summary.en: The Djenné masons’ guild under master builder Ismaila Traoré raised the present mud-brick mosque on the site of the medieval original. Re-plastered by the whole town each year, it is the largest earthen building in the world and an emblem of Sudano-Sahelian architecture.
summary.zh: 杰内泥瓦匠行会在建筑大师伊斯梅拉·特拉奥雷主持下，于中世纪原寺旧址上建起现今的泥砖清真寺。全城居民每年为之重新抹泥，它是世界上最大的土建筑，也是苏丹—萨赫勒建筑风格的象征。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Great Mosque of Djenné
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Old Towns of Djenné
Jean-Louis Bourgeois, “The History of the Great Mosques of Djenné”, African Arts 20/3 (1987)

name.zh: 意大利入侵埃塞俄比亚

summary.en: Mussolini’s Italy invaded Ethiopia, using poison gas against soldiers and civilians, and took Addis Ababa in May 1936. Haile Selassie’s appeal to the League of Nations went unanswered, but Ethiopian patriots kept fighting until liberation with British help in 1941.
summary.zh: 墨索里尼的意大利入侵埃塞俄比亚，对军民使用毒气，1936年5月攻占亚的斯亚贝巴。海尔·塞拉西向国际联盟的呼吁未获回应，但埃塞俄比亚爱国者坚持抗战，1941年在英国协助下光复。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Second Italo-Ethiopian War
Bahru Zewde, A History of Modern Ethiopia, 1855–1991 (2nd ed., 2001)
Haile Selassie I, Appeal to the League of Nations (30 June 1936)
Haile Selassie, Appeal to the League of Nations, Geneva, 30 June 1936
Ian Campbell, The Addis Ababa Massacre: Italy’s National Shame (2017)

note: Wikidata ends the war in February 1937 (last regular resistance); most accounts date the conventional war 1935–36.

story.en:
Mussolini wanted to avenge Adwa and found an empire. A skirmish at the oasis of Walwal on the Somali frontier in December 1934 served as pretext, and on 3 October 1935 Italian armies invaded from Eritrea and Italian Somaliland. The League of Nations voted sanctions but left oil off the list, and Britain kept the Suez Canal open to Italian troopships.

Ethiopian armies fought with rifles and courage against tanks and aircraft. From December, Italian planes sprayed mustard gas on soldiers, villages and the waters of Lake Ashenge, in breach of the Geneva Protocol. After the defeat at Maychew in March 1936, Haile Selassie went into exile, and Marshal Badoglio entered Addis Ababa on 5 May.

On 30 June 1936 the emperor addressed the League in Geneva while Italian journalists jeered; he warned that collective security was dying and that small states would be next. Occupation brought the massacre in Addis Ababa of February 1937 after an attempt on Viceroy Graziani. Patriot guerrillas, women among them, held out until British and Ethiopian forces restored the emperor on 5 May 1941.
story.zh:
墨索里尼一心为阿杜瓦雪耻并建立帝国。1934年12月索马里边境瓦尔瓦尔绿洲的一场冲突成为借口，1935年10月3日意大利军队从厄立特里亚和意属索马里兰同时入侵。国际联盟虽表决实施制裁，却把石油排除在外，英国也继续让意大利运兵船通过苏伊士运河。

埃塞俄比亚军队凭着步枪和勇气对抗坦克与飞机。自12月起，意大利飞机违反《日内瓦议定书》，向士兵、村庄乃至阿申格湖的湖水喷洒芥子气。1936年3月在梅丘战败后，海尔·塞拉西流亡海外，巴多格里奥元帅于5月5日进入亚的斯亚贝巴。

1936年6月30日，皇帝在日内瓦向国联发表演说，意大利记者在场起哄；他警告说集体安全正在消亡，下一个就会轮到其他小国。占领期间，1937年2月总督格拉齐亚尼遇刺未遂后，亚的斯亚贝巴发生大屠杀。爱国游击队（其中也有妇女）坚持抗战，直到1941年5月5日英国和埃塞俄比亚军队护送皇帝复位。

summary.en: The Free Officers led by Gamal Abdel Nasser and Muhammad Naguib seized power in a bloodless coup, forcing King Farouk to abdicate. The monarchy was abolished in 1953, land reform followed, and Nasser emerged as leader of Arab nationalism and the non-aligned world.
summary.zh: 以纳赛尔和纳吉布为首的“自由军官组织”发动不流血政变，迫使法鲁克国王退位。1953年废除君主制，随后推行土地改革，纳赛尔成为阿拉伯民族主义和不结盟运动的领袖。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Egyptian revolution of 1952
Joel Gordon, Nasser’s Blessed Movement: Egypt’s Free Officers and the July Revolution (1992)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. VIII: Africa since 1935 (ed. A. A. Mazrui, 1993)
Britannica: Egyptian Revolution of 1952

story.en:
By 1952 King Farouk was discredited by corruption, defeat in the 1948 Palestine war and Britain’s continued garrison on the Suez Canal. In January rioters burned much of modern central Cairo on “Black Saturday”. A secret group of young army officers, the Free Officers, had been planning for years under Lieutenant-Colonel Gamal Abdel Nasser, with the popular General Muhammad Naguib as their public face.

In the night of 22–23 July they seized army headquarters and the radio station almost without bloodshed, and in the morning Anwar Sadat read their proclamation on the air. On 26 July Farouk abdicated in favour of his infant son and sailed from Alexandria into exile aboard the royal yacht al-Mahrousa, saluted by the officers who had deposed him.

A land reform law in September broke up the great estates. The monarchy was abolished in June 1953 with Naguib as president, but Nasser outmanoeuvred him and took full power in 1954. Under Nasser, Egypt nationalised the Suez Canal in 1956 and became the centre of Arab nationalism.
story.zh:
到1952年，法鲁克国王因腐败、1948年巴勒斯坦战争的失败以及英国在苏伊士运河区继续驻军而威信扫地。同年1月的“黑色星期六”，暴乱者焚毁了开罗现代市中心的大片街区。一个由青年军官组成的秘密团体“自由军官组织”在贾迈勒·阿卜杜勒·纳赛尔中校领导下已筹划多年，深孚众望的穆罕默德·纳吉布将军则充当其公开代表。

7月22日至23日夜间，他们几乎未流血便控制了陆军总部和广播电台，次日清晨由安瓦尔·萨达特在电台宣读声明。7月26日，法鲁克宣布让位于襁褓中的儿子，乘王室游艇“马哈鲁萨号”从亚历山大流亡海外，推翻他的军官们还向他鸣礼致意。

9月颁布的土地改革法拆分了大地产。1953年6月废除君主制，纳吉布出任总统，但纳赛尔在权力斗争中胜出，于1954年掌握全部权力。在纳赛尔领导下，埃及于1956年将苏伊士运河收归国有，成为阿拉伯民族主义的中心。

summary.en: The Kenya Land and Freedom Army, mainly Kikuyu, fought British colonial rule and settler land seizure in the central highlands. Britain declared an emergency and detained some tens of thousands in camps where abuse was systematic; the struggle hastened Kenyan independence in 1963.
summary.zh: 以基库尤人为主的“肯尼亚土地与自由军”在中部高原反抗英国殖民统治和移民夺地。英国宣布紧急状态，将数以万计的人关入系统性施虐的拘留营；这一斗争加速了肯尼亚于1963年独立。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Mau Mau rebellion
Caroline Elkins, Imperial Reckoning: The Untold Story of Britain’s Gulag in Kenya (2005)
David Anderson, Histories of the Hanged (2005)

note: Marker at Nyeri in the central highlands.

summary.en: The National Liberation Front (FLN) launched coordinated attacks on 1 November 1954. France answered with mass troop deployments, torture and resettlement camps; after hundreds of thousands of deaths the Évian Accords led to Algerian independence on 5 July 1962.
summary.zh: 民族解放阵线于1954年11月1日发动协同袭击。法国以大规模派兵、酷刑和强制安置营回应；在数十万人死亡后，《埃维昂协议》促成阿尔及利亚于1962年7月5日独立。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Algerian War
Alistair Horne, A Savage War of Peace: Algeria 1954–1962 (1977)
Benjamin Stora, Algeria 1830–2000: A Short History (2001)
Britannica: Algerian War

story.en:
In the early hours of 1 November 1954, the “Red All Saints’ Day”, the newly formed FLN set off some seventy bombings and attacks across Algeria. France, which regarded Algeria as three départements of the Republic and home to about a million European settlers, poured in conscripts until some 400,000 troops were deployed.

In the Battle of Algiers of 1957, General Massu’s paratroopers broke the FLN’s urban network in the Casbah through mass arrests and systematic torture, which the communist journalist Henri Alleg exposed in his banned book La Question (1958). Settler and army anger at Paris brought down the Fourth Republic in May 1958 and returned Charles de Gaulle to power. To the settlers’ fury he moved toward self-determination; the diehard OAS answered with bombings in Algeria and France.

The Évian Accords of March 1962 ended the fighting, and Algeria became independent on 5 July. Nearly a million pieds-noirs left within months, and many harkis who had served France were killed. Estimates of Algerian deaths run from about 300,000 to the official Algerian figure of 1.5 million.
story.zh:
1954年11月1日凌晨，即“红色万圣节”，新成立的民族解放阵线在阿尔及利亚各地发动约七十起爆炸和袭击。法国视阿尔及利亚为共和国的三个省，那里居住着约一百万欧洲移民，于是不断增派义务兵，最终部署兵力约四十万。

在1957年的阿尔及尔战役中，马叙将军的伞兵通过大规模逮捕和系统性酷刑摧毁了民族解放阵线在卡斯巴的城市网络；共产党记者亨利·阿莱格在1958年遭禁的《问题》一书中揭露了酷刑。移民和军队对巴黎的愤怒导致第四共和国于1958年5月垮台，戴高乐重新执政。令移民愤慨的是，他逐步走向民族自决；顽固派秘密军组织则在阿尔及利亚和法国制造爆炸。

1962年3月的《埃维昂协议》结束了战事，阿尔及利亚于7月5日独立。数月之内近百万“黑脚”法裔离开，许多曾为法国效力的“哈基”遭到杀害。阿尔及利亚死亡人数的估计从约三十万到阿尔及利亚官方所称的一百五十万不等。

summary.en: The Gold Coast became independent as Ghana under Kwame Nkrumah, one of the first sub-Saharan colonies to end European rule. At midnight Nkrumah declared that Ghana’s independence was meaningless unless linked to the total liberation of Africa; Accra became a hub of pan-Africanism.
summary.zh: 黄金海岸在克瓦米·恩克鲁玛领导下独立为加纳，是撒哈拉以南最早摆脱欧洲统治的殖民地之一。午夜时分恩克鲁玛宣告，除非与整个非洲的解放相联系，加纳的独立便毫无意义；阿克拉由此成为泛非主义中心。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Dominion of Ghana
Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana: The Autobiography of Kwame Nkrumah (1957)
Britannica: Ghana: Independence
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. VIII: Africa since 1935 (ed. A. A. Mazrui, 1993)
Britannica: Kwame Nkrumah

note: QID is the Dominion of Ghana (1957–1960), the state created on independence day.

story.en:
Kwame Nkrumah returned to the Gold Coast in 1947 after twelve years in the United States and Britain, and in 1949 broke away to found the Convention People’s Party with the slogan “Self-Government Now”. Jailed for sedition after a campaign of “positive action” strikes, he won the 1951 election from his cell and was released to lead the government under the British governor.

At midnight on 5–6 March 1957, before a vast crowd at the Old Polo Grounds in Accra, Nkrumah and his ministers, in white caps embroidered “PG” for “prison graduate”, announced that Ghana was free for ever. He declared that its independence would mean nothing unless it was tied to the liberation of the whole continent. The new state took its name from the medieval Sahelian empire, and its flag carried a black star.

Accra became a capital of pan-Africanism. In 1958 Nkrumah hosted the All-African People’s Conference, attended by young leaders such as Patrice Lumumba, and Ghana backed liberation movements until his overthrow in 1966.
story.zh:
1947年，在美国和英国度过十二年后，克瓦米·恩克鲁玛回到黄金海岸；1949年他另立门户，创建人民大会党，口号是“立即自治”。因发动“积极行动”罢工而以煽动罪入狱后，他在狱中赢得1951年大选，获释后在英国总督之下领导政府。

1957年3月5日至6日午夜，在阿克拉老马球场的人山人海前，恩克鲁玛和部长们头戴绣有“PG”（意为“出狱者”）字样的白色便帽，宣布加纳永远自由。他宣称，加纳的独立若不与整个非洲大陆的解放联系在一起，便毫无意义。新国家以中世纪萨赫勒地区的古帝国为名，国旗上缀着一颗黑星。

阿克拉成为泛非主义的中心。1958年恩克鲁玛主办全非人民大会，帕特里斯·卢蒙巴等青年领袖出席；直到1966年恩克鲁玛被推翻，加纳一直支持各地的解放运动。

summary.en: Seventeen African states, including Nigeria, the Congo and most of French West and Equatorial Africa, gained independence in 1960. In December the UN General Assembly adopted Resolution 1514 declaring colonialism a denial of human rights.
summary.zh: 1960年，包括尼日利亚、刚果以及法属西非和赤道非洲大部在内的十七个非洲国家获得独立。同年12月，联合国大会通过第1514号决议，宣布殖民主义是对基本人权的否定。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Year of Africa
UN General Assembly Resolution 1514 (XV), Declaration on the Granting of Independence to Colonial Countries and Peoples (14 Dec 1960)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. VIII: Africa since 1935 (ed. A. A. Mazrui, 1993)
UN General Assembly Resolution 1514 (XV), 14 December 1960
Britannica: Wind of Change speech

note: Marker placed at Lagos (Nigeria, independent 1 October 1960) as a symbolic location.

story.en:
The year opened with Cameroon’s independence on 1 January and closed with Mauritania’s on 28 November. In between came Togo, Madagascar, Somalia, the Belgian Congo, Nigeria and almost all of French West and Equatorial Africa, from Senegal and Mali to Chad and Gabon: seventeen new states in all, most admitted to the United Nations that September.

The mood had been set in February, when the British prime minister Harold Macmillan told the all-white parliament in Cape Town that a “wind of change” was blowing through the continent. Seven weeks later police killed 69 protesters at Sharpeville, a reminder that settler regimes in South Africa, Rhodesia and the Portuguese colonies were not bending.

Independence also brought instant crisis in the Congo, where Lumumba’s defiant speech before King Baudouin on 30 June was followed within days by mutiny and secession. On 14 December the General Assembly adopted Resolution 1514 by 89 votes to none, with nine abstentions, declaring that subjecting peoples to alien domination denied fundamental human rights.
story.zh:
这一年以1月1日喀麦隆独立开始，以11月28日毛里塔尼亚独立结束。其间独立的有多哥、马达加斯加、索马里、比属刚果、尼日利亚，以及从塞内加尔、马里到乍得、加蓬几乎整个法属西非和赤道非洲，总共十七个新国家，其中大多数于当年9月加入联合国。

基调早在2月就已定下：英国首相哈罗德·麦克米伦在开普敦对全由白人组成的议会说，“变革之风”正吹遍整个非洲大陆。七周后，警察在沙佩维尔打死69名抗议者，提醒世人南非、罗得西亚和葡萄牙殖民地的移民政权并不打算让步。

独立也让刚果立即陷入危机：6月30日卢蒙巴在博杜安国王面前发表措辞强硬的演说，几天之内便发生兵变和分离。12月14日，联合国大会以89票赞成、0票反对、9票弃权通过第1514号决议，宣布使人民受外国奴役是对基本人权的否定。

summary.en: South African police opened fire on a crowd protesting the pass laws at Sharpeville, killing 69 people. The government banned the ANC and PAC, which turned to armed struggle; 21 March is now Human Rights Day in South Africa and the UN day against racial discrimination.
summary.zh: 南非警察向沙佩维尔抗议通行证法的人群开枪，打死69人。政府随即取缔非国大和泛非大，两者转向武装斗争；3月21日现为南非人权日和联合国消除种族歧视国际日。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Sharpeville massacre
Tom Lodge, Sharpeville: An Apartheid Massacre and Its Consequences (2011)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. VIII: Africa since 1935 (ed. A. A. Mazrui, 1993)

summary.en: Days after independence from Belgium, the Congo faced an army mutiny and the Belgian-backed secessions of Katanga and South Kasai. Prime Minister Lumumba was deposed and murdered in 1961; UN intervention, Cold War rivalry and rebellions ended with Mobutu’s coup in 1965.
summary.zh: 刚果脱离比利时独立数日后即遭遇军队哗变，以及比利时支持的加丹加和南开赛分裂。卢蒙巴总理于1961年被推翻并遇害；联合国干预、冷战角力和多次叛乱最终以1965年蒙博托政变告终。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Congo Crisis
Georges Nzongola-Ntalaja, The Congo from Leopold to Kabila: A People’s History (2002)
Ludo De Witte, The Assassination of Lumumba (2001)
Britannica: Patrice Lumumba

note: Wikidata ends the crisis in 1966; most accounts close it with Mobutu’s coup of November 1965.

story.en:
At the independence ceremony on 30 June 1960, King Baudouin praised the “genius” of his great-uncle Leopold II. Prime Minister Patrice Lumumba, not scheduled to speak, answered with a blistering account of the humiliations and violence of colonial rule. Five days later soldiers of the Force Publique mutinied against their Belgian officers, Belgian troops intervened, and on 11 July Moïse Tshombe declared Katanga, with its copper mines, independent under Belgian protection.

The United Nations sent peacekeepers but refused to subdue Katanga, so Lumumba turned to the Soviet Union for help. In September President Kasa-Vubu dismissed him and the army chief Joseph-Désiré Mobutu took power. Lumumba was handed to his Katangese enemies and shot on 17 January 1961 with Belgian officers present; his body was dissolved in acid. In September 1961 UN Secretary-General Dag Hammarskjöld died in a plane crash near Ndola.

UN forces ended Katanga’s secession in 1963, but the Simba rebellion followed. On 24 November 1965 Mobutu seized power for good, ruling for 32 years. In 2022 Belgium returned a tooth, the only known remains of Lumumba, to his family.
story.zh:
1960年6月30日的独立仪式上，博杜安国王称颂其叔祖利奥波德二世的“天才”。原本未安排发言的总理帕特里斯·卢蒙巴随即起身，痛陈殖民统治下的屈辱与暴力。五天后，公安军士兵哗变反抗比利时军官，比利时军队介入；7月11日，莫伊兹·冲伯在比利时庇护下宣布盛产铜矿的加丹加独立。

联合国派出维和部队却拒绝平定加丹加，卢蒙巴于是转向苏联求援。9月，总统卡萨武布将他解职，陆军参谋长约瑟夫-德西雷·蒙博托掌权。卢蒙巴被交给加丹加的敌人，1961年1月17日在比利时军官在场的情况下遭枪杀，遗体被强酸溶解。1961年9月，联合国秘书长达格·哈马舍尔德在恩多拉附近坠机身亡。

联合国部队于1963年结束了加丹加的分离，但辛巴叛乱接踵而至。1965年11月24日，蒙博托再次夺权并从此执政32年。2022年，比利时把卢蒙巴唯一已知的遗骸——一颗牙齿——归还给他的家人。

summary.en: Thirty-two independent African states signed the OAU Charter in Addis Ababa, hosted by Haile Selassie. The organisation backed liberation movements against colonial and white-minority rule while upholding inherited borders; 25 May is celebrated as Africa Day.
summary.zh: 三十二个独立非洲国家在海尔·塞拉西主持下于亚的斯亚贝巴签署《非洲统一组织宪章》。该组织支持反对殖民和白人少数统治的解放运动，同时维护殖民时期遗留的边界；5月25日被定为“非洲日”。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Organisation of African Unity
Charter of the Organization of African Unity (Addis Ababa, 25 May 1963)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. VIII: Africa since 1935 (ed. A. A. Mazrui, 1993)
Britannica: Organization of African Unity
African Union: OAU Charter, Addis Ababa, 25 May 1963

story.en:
By 1963 independent Africa was split into rival camps. The radical Casablanca group, led by Ghana, Guinea, Mali and Egypt, wanted rapid political union; the larger Monrovia group, including Nigeria and most former French colonies, preferred cooperation between sovereign states. Emperor Haile Selassie invited both to Addis Ababa, and in May heads of state from thirty-two countries met in the new Africa Hall.

Kwame Nkrumah arrived with copies of his book Africa Must Unite and urged a continental government with a common army and currency. Most leaders refused to surrender their new sovereignty. The charter signed on 25 May instead pledged non-interference, respect for territorial integrity and the liberation of the territories still under colonial or white-minority rule. A Liberation Committee based in Dar es Salaam funnelled money and arms to movements in southern Africa.

In 1964 members agreed to keep the frontiers inherited from colonialism, a choice that limited wars between states but left many internal conflicts unresolved. Morocco walked out in 1984 over Western Sahara. The OAU gave way to the African Union in 2002, and 25 May is still marked as Africa Day.
story.zh:
到1963年，独立的非洲分裂为对立的阵营。以加纳、几内亚、马里和埃及为首的激进派“卡萨布兰卡集团”主张迅速实现政治统一；包括尼日利亚和大多数前法国殖民地在内、规模更大的“蒙罗维亚集团”则倾向于主权国家之间的合作。皇帝海尔·塞拉西邀请双方前往亚的斯亚贝巴，5月，三十二国的国家元首在新落成的非洲大厦聚会。

克瓦米·恩克鲁玛带着他的新书《非洲必须统一》与会，力主建立拥有共同军队和货币的大陆政府。多数领导人不愿交出刚刚获得的主权。5月25日签署的宪章转而承诺不干涉内政、尊重领土完整，并致力于解放仍处于殖民统治或白人少数统治下的地区。设在达累斯萨拉姆的解放委员会向南部非洲的解放运动输送资金和武器。

1964年，成员国同意保留殖民时代遗留的边界，这一决定限制了国家间战争，却使许多内部冲突悬而未决。1984年摩洛哥因西撒哈拉问题退出。2002年非洲统一组织由非洲联盟取代，5月25日至今仍被定为“非洲日”。

name.zh: 尼日利亚内战（比夫拉战争）
