summary.en: After massacres of Igbo in the north, the Eastern Region seceded as the Republic of Biafra under Odumegwu Ojukwu. A federal blockade caused mass famine; estimates of deaths, mostly civilian, range from about one to two million before Biafra surrendered in January 1970.
summary.zh: 北方发生针对伊博人的屠杀后，东区在奥朱古领导下宣布独立为比夫拉共和国。联邦封锁造成大饥荒；至1970年1月比夫拉投降，估计约一百万至两百万人死亡，多为平民。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Nigerian Civil War
John de St. Jorre, The Nigerian Civil War (1972)
Chinua Achebe, There Was a Country: A Personal History of Biafra (2012)
Britannica: Biafra
Michael Gould, The Struggle for Modern Nigeria: The Biafran War 1967–1970 (2012)

note: Marker at Enugu, first capital of Biafra.

story.en:
Nigeria’s First Republic collapsed in 1966. A coup in January by mostly Igbo junior officers killed the northern and western premiers; a northern counter-coup in July killed the Igbo head of state, General Aguiyi-Ironsi. Over the following months mobs in northern cities massacred thousands of Igbo and other easterners, and perhaps a million refugees fled home to the Eastern Region.

Talks between the military governor of the East, Lieutenant-Colonel Odumegwu Ojukwu, and the federal leader Yakubu Gowon at Aburi in Ghana broke down, and on 30 May 1967 Ojukwu proclaimed the Republic of Biafra. Federal forces took Enugu in October and then tightened a land and sea blockade. As Biafra shrank, starvation spread; photographs of children with kwashiorkor shocked the world, and church agencies flew food in at night from São Tomé to a road strip at Uli.

Biafra surrendered in January 1970. Gowon declared “no victor, no vanquished” and avoided mass reprisals, but the trauma endured. French doctors who had worked in Biafra went on in 1971 to found Médecins Sans Frontières.
story.zh:
尼日利亚第一共和国于1966年崩溃。1月，以伊博族为主的下级军官发动政变，杀死北部区和西部区总理；7月北方军官反政变，杀死伊博族国家元首阿吉伊-伊龙西将军。此后数月，北方城市的暴民屠杀了数千名伊博人和其他东部人，约百万难民逃回东区。

东区军事长官奥杜梅古·奥朱古中校与联邦领导人雅库布·戈翁在加纳阿布里的谈判破裂，1967年5月30日奥朱古宣布成立比夫拉共和国。联邦军队于10月攻占埃努古，随后收紧陆海封锁。随着比夫拉控制区不断缩小，饥荒蔓延；患夸希奥科病儿童的照片震惊世界，教会救援机构夜间从圣多美向乌利的一段公路跑道空运食品。

比夫拉于1970年1月投降。戈翁宣布“没有胜利者，也没有失败者”，避免了大规模报复，但创伤长久未愈。曾在比夫拉工作的法国医生们于1971年创立了无国界医生组织。

summary.en: Thousands of Black schoolchildren in Soweto marched against compulsory Afrikaans instruction; police fired on them, killing Hector Pieterson among many others. Unrest spread nationwide and a new generation joined the liberation movements; 16 June is now Youth Day.
summary.zh: 索韦托数千名黑人学生游行反对强制以阿非利卡语授课，警察向他们开枪，赫克托·彼得森等多人遇难。动荡蔓延全国，新一代青年投身解放运动；6月16日现为南非青年节。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Soweto uprising
Baruch Hirson, Year of Fire, Year of Ash: The Soweto Revolt (1979)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. VIII: Africa since 1935 (ed. A. A. Mazrui, 1993)

name.en: Genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda
name.zh: 卢旺达图西族种族灭绝

summary.en: After President Habyarimana’s plane was shot down, Hutu extremist militias and soldiers killed some 800,000 people, mostly Tutsi and also moderate Hutu, in about 100 days. The UN withdrew most peacekeepers; the killing ended when the Rwandan Patriotic Front took Kigali in July.
summary.zh: 哈比亚利马纳总统座机被击落后，胡图极端民兵与士兵在约一百天内杀害约八十万人，主要是图西族，也有温和派胡图族。联合国撤走大部分维和人员；7月卢旺达爱国阵线攻占基加利，屠杀才告结束。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Rwandan genocide
Alison Des Forges, Leave None to Tell the Story: Genocide in Rwanda (Human Rights Watch, 1999)
Report of the Independent Inquiry into the Actions of the United Nations during the 1994 Genocide in Rwanda (1999)
Roméo Dallaire, Shake Hands with the Devil (2003)

story.en:
On the evening of 6 April 1994 a plane carrying President Juvénal Habyarimana of Rwanda and President Cyprien Ntaryamira of Burundi was shot down on its approach to Kigali. Within hours Hutu Power extremists in the army, the Presidential Guard and the Interahamwe militia set up roadblocks, killed the moderate prime minister Agathe Uwilingiyimana and began working through prepared lists. Radio RTLM urged listeners to hunt down the “cockroaches”, its word for Tutsi.

Neighbours killed neighbours with machetes and clubs; churches where Tutsi sought refuge became sites of massacre, and sexual violence was used on a huge scale. The UN commander, General Roméo Dallaire, had warned in January of plans for extermination. After ten Belgian peacekeepers were murdered, the Security Council cut his force to about 270.

The Rwandan Patriotic Front under Paul Kagame took Kigali on 4 July, and some two million Hutu fled, many into Zaire, carrying the conflict into the Congo wars. The UN tribunal at Arusha delivered the first international conviction for genocide in 1998, and community gacaca courts later heard nearly two million cases.
story.zh:
1994年4月6日傍晚，载有卢旺达总统朱韦纳尔·哈比亚利马纳和布隆迪总统西普里安·恩塔里亚米拉的飞机在降落基加利时被击落。数小时内，军队、总统卫队和“联攻派”民兵中的胡图极端分子设立路障，杀害温和派总理阿加特·乌维林吉伊马纳，并按事先拟好的名单展开屠杀。千山自由广播电视台煽动听众追杀“蟑螂”，即对图西人的蔑称。

邻居用砍刀和棍棒杀害邻居；图西人避难的教堂成为屠杀现场，性暴力被大规模使用。联合国维和部队指挥官罗密欧·达莱尔将军早在1月就警告过灭绝计划。十名比利时维和士兵遇害后，安理会把他的部队削减到约270人。

保罗·卡加梅领导的卢旺达爱国阵线于7月4日攻占基加利，约二百万胡图人出逃，许多人进入扎伊尔，把冲突带入了后来的刚果战争。设在阿鲁沙的联合国法庭于1998年作出国际上首例种族灭绝罪判决，后来社区“加卡卡”法庭又审理了近两百万起案件。

summary.en: After negotiations that ended apartheid, South Africans of all races voted for the first time; the ANC won 62.6 percent. Nelson Mandela was inaugurated as president at the Union Buildings in Pretoria on 10 May 1994, heading a government of national unity.
summary.zh: 在终结种族隔离的谈判之后，南非各种族民众首次共同投票，非国大获得62.6%的选票。1994年5月10日，纳尔逊·曼德拉在比勒陀利亚联合大厦宣誓就任总统，领导民族团结政府。

sources.title: Wikipedia: 1994 South African general election
Nelson Mandela, Long Walk to Freedom (1994)
Britannica: South Africa: The end of apartheid
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. VIII: Africa since 1935 (ed. A. A. Mazrui, 1993)
South African History Online: The 1994 election

story.en:
The vote followed four years of talks after Nelson Mandela’s release, punctuated by violence that killed thousands, including the assassination of the Communist leader Chris Hani in 1993. The Inkatha Freedom Party joined the ballot only a week before polling, so its candidates were added to the papers on stickers, and white right-wingers set off bombs in the days before.

From 26 to 29 April some 19 million people voted, most for the first time in their lives. Queues stretched for kilometres across townships and farmland, and elderly voters waited for hours in the sun. Mandela cast his ballot at Ohlange High School in Inanda, near the grave of John Dube, the ANC’s first president.

The ANC won 62.6 percent, just short of the two-thirds needed to write the constitution alone. On 10 May Mandela was sworn in at the Union Buildings in Pretoria, with F. W. de Klerk and Thabo Mbeki as deputy presidents, while air force jets trailed the colours of the new flag overhead. 27 April is celebrated as Freedom Day.
story.zh:
这次选举是在纳尔逊·曼德拉获释后长达四年的谈判之后举行的，其间暴力冲突夺去数千人生命，包括1993年南非共产党领导人克里斯·哈尼遇刺。因卡塔自由党在投票前一周才决定参选，其候选人只能以贴纸形式补印到选票上；白人右翼分子则在投票前几天制造了爆炸。

4月26日至29日，约一千九百万人参加投票，大多数人是生平第一次。投票队伍在城镇和农田间绵延数公里，老人们在烈日下等候数小时。曼德拉在伊南达的奥兰格中学投票，那里靠近非国大首任主席约翰·杜布的墓地。

非国大赢得62.6%的选票，略低于单独制定宪法所需的三分之二。5月10日，曼德拉在比勒陀利亚的联合大厦宣誓就任总统，德克勒克和塔博·姆贝基任副总统，空军喷气机在空中拉出新国旗的彩色烟带。4月27日被定为“自由日”。

summary.en: The African Union replaced the OAU at a summit in Durban, with a mandate for deeper integration, a Pan-African Parliament and a Peace and Security Council. Unlike its predecessor, its Constitutive Act allows intervention in member states in cases of genocide and war crimes.
summary.zh: 非洲联盟在德班峰会上取代非洲统一组织，以深化一体化为宗旨，设立泛非议会和和平与安全理事会。与前身不同，其《组织法》允许在发生种族灭绝和战争罪时干预成员国。

sources.title: Wikipedia: African Union
Constitutive Act of the African Union (Lomé, 2000)
Corinne A. A. Packer & Donald Rukare, “The New African Union and Its Constitutive Act”, American Journal of International Law 96/2 (2002)

note: Wikidata’s inception date (9 September 1999) is the Sirte Declaration; the AU was formally launched in Durban on 9 July 2002.

summary.en: The self-immolation of street vendor Mohamed Bouazizi in Sidi Bouzid sparked nationwide protests that forced President Ben Ali to flee on 14 January 2011, igniting the Arab Spring. Tunisia’s National Dialogue Quartet received the 2015 Nobel Peace Prize for guiding a democratic transition.
summary.zh: 西迪布济德街头小贩穆罕默德·布瓦吉吉自焚，引发全国抗议，迫使本·阿里总统于2011年1月14日出逃，点燃“阿拉伯之春”。突尼斯全国对话四方机制因引导民主转型而获2015年诺贝尔和平奖。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Tunisian revolution
Britannica: Jasmine Revolution
Nobel Peace Prize 2015: National Dialogue Quartet
The Nobel Peace Prize 2015: National Dialogue Quartet

story.en:
On 17 December 2010 Mohamed Bouazizi, a 26-year-old fruit seller in the town of Sidi Bouzid, had his cart and scales confiscated by municipal inspectors. Refused a hearing at the governor’s office, he doused himself with fuel outside it and set himself alight. Protests spread from the impoverished interior, filmed on mobile phones and shared on Facebook and by satellite channels, despite police bullets and censorship.

Bouazizi died on 4 January 2011. Lawyers, the UGTT trade union and students joined the demonstrations, and on 14 January crowds filled Avenue Habib Bourguiba in Tunis. That evening President Zine El Abidine Ben Ali, in power since 1987, flew to Saudi Arabia. Within weeks protests had toppled Egypt’s Hosni Mubarak and spread across the Arab world.

Tunisia was the uprisings’ one lasting democratic outcome for a decade. When the transition stalled in 2013 after political assassinations, four civil-society groups brokered a national dialogue and a new constitution in 2014, earning the 2015 Nobel Peace Prize. In 2021 President Kais Saied suspended parliament and began ruling by decree.
story.zh:
2010年12月17日，西迪布济德镇26岁的水果小贩穆罕默德·布瓦吉吉的推车和秤被市政检查员没收。他到省政府申诉被拒，便在门外浇上燃油自焚。抗议从贫困的内陆地区蔓延开来，人们用手机拍摄，通过脸书和卫星电视传播，警察的子弹和审查都未能阻止。

布瓦吉吉于2011年1月4日去世。律师、突尼斯总工会和学生加入示威，1月14日人群挤满突尼斯市的哈比卜·布尔吉巴大街。当晚，自1987年起执政的总统本·阿里飞往沙特阿拉伯。几周之内，抗议推翻了埃及的穆巴拉克，并蔓延到整个阿拉伯世界。

此后十年间，突尼斯是这场起义浪潮中唯一延续下来的民主成果。2013年接连发生政治暗杀、转型陷入僵局时，四个公民社会团体促成全国对话并于2014年通过新宪法，因此获得2015年诺贝尔和平奖。2021年，总统凯斯·赛义德冻结议会，开始以法令治国。

name.zh: 伊本·海什木著《光学之书》

summary.en: Working in Fatimid Cairo, Ibn al-Haytham wrote the Kitab al-Manazir, arguing that vision results from light entering the eye and testing his claims with controlled experiments. Translated into Latin around 1200, it shaped European optics from Roger Bacon to Kepler.
summary.zh: 伊本·海什木在法蒂玛王朝治下的开罗撰写《光学之书》，主张视觉源于光线进入眼睛，并以可控实验检验自己的论断。约1200年该书被译为拉丁文，影响了从罗吉尔·培根到开普勒的欧洲光学。

sources.title: Britannica: Kitab al-manazir
Britannica: Ibn al-Haytham
Wikipedia: Book of Optics
A. I. Sabra (trans.), The Optics of Ibn al-Haytham, Books I–III (1989)

note: Composed c. 1011–1021, mostly after the death of the caliph al-Hakim; exact dates are uncertain.

story.en:
Medieval biographers, beginning with Ibn al-Qifti, tell how Ibn al-Haytham, a scholar from Basra, boasted that the Nile’s floods could be regulated. The Fatimid caliph al-Hakim summoned him to Egypt, but on surveying the river near Aswan he saw the scheme was impossible. Fearing the notoriously volatile caliph, he is said to have feigned madness and lived confined until al-Hakim’s death in 1021. The story may be embellished, but it places the composition of his great work in Cairo.

In the seven books of the Kitab al-Manazir he rejected the old idea that the eye sends out rays and argued that vision occurs when light from every point of an object enters the eye. He backed his claims with systematic experiments using darkened rooms, tubes and screens, studied reflection and refraction, and explained optical illusions through the psychology of perception.

Translated into Latin around 1200 as De aspectibus, and printed by Friedrich Risner in 1572, the book was studied by Roger Bacon, Witelo and Kepler. Historians count it among the most important works in the history of physics before Newton.
story.zh:
从伊本·基夫提开始，中世纪传记作家都讲述过这样的故事：巴士拉学者伊本·海赛姆夸口说可以调节尼罗河的洪水。法蒂玛王朝哈里发哈基姆把他召到埃及，但他在阿斯旺附近考察河流后发现计划根本不可行。据说他畏惧这位喜怒无常的哈里发，便装疯卖傻，一直被软禁到1021年哈基姆去世。故事或许有所渲染，但它说明他的巨著是在开罗写成的。

在七卷本的《光学之书》中，他否定了眼睛发出射线的旧说，主张视觉是物体上每一点发出的光进入眼睛的结果。他以暗室、管筒和屏幕进行系统的实验来验证观点，研究了反射与折射，并从知觉心理学的角度解释了视错觉。

此书约在1200年译为拉丁文《论视觉》，1572年由弗里德里希·里斯纳刊印，罗吉尔·培根、维特洛和开普勒都曾研读。史家把它列为牛顿以前物理学史上最重要的著作之一。

name.zh: 跨撒哈拉黄金与食盐贸易

summary.en: Camel caravans linked the Maghreb with the West African Sahel, exchanging salt, textiles and horses for gold, ivory and slaves. Sijilmasa, founded in 757, was a leading northern terminus; the trade financed Ghana, Mali and Songhai and carried Islam and Arabic literacy south.
summary.zh: 骆驼商队连接马格里布与西非萨赫勒地区，以食盐、纺织品和马匹换取黄金、象牙和奴隶。757年建立的西吉尔马萨是主要的北端枢纽；这一贸易支撑了加纳、马里和桑海帝国，并把伊斯兰教和阿拉伯文读写带往南方。

sources.title: The Met, Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History: The Trans-Saharan Gold Trade (7th–14th Century)
Wikipedia: Sijilmasa
Wikipedia: Trans-Saharan trade
N. Levtzion and J. F. P. Hopkins (eds.), Corpus of Early Arabic Sources for West African History (1981): al-Bakri, Ibn Battuta
Ralph A. Austen, Trans-Saharan Africa in World History (2010)

note: Span is conventional: from the founding of Sijilmasa (757) to the Moroccan conquest of Songhai (1591), after which Atlantic trade eclipsed the caravans. Marker at Sijilmasa.

story.en:
The trade depended on the camel, which became common in the Sahara in the first centuries CE, and on the desert-wise Berber peoples who guided caravans across some two months of sand and gravel plains. Northbound loads carried gold, ivory, kola nuts and enslaved people; southbound came salt, copper, cloth, horses and books.

Arab geographers left vivid sketches. Al-Bakri, compiling his geography in Córdoba in 1068, wrote that the king of Ghana kept every gold nugget for himself and left only gold dust to the people, so that the metal would not become cheap. Ibn Battuta, crossing in 1352, stayed at the salt mine of Taghaza, where even the houses and the mosque were built of salt blocks roofed with camel skins, and the water was brackish.

West African gold supplied much of the medieval Mediterranean’s coinage, from Fatimid dinars to Genoese and Castilian gold. The caravans also carried Islam, Arabic writing and scholarship to the Sahel cities of Awdaghust, Walata, Timbuktu and Gao. Their importance faded after the Moroccan invasion of 1591 and the rise of the Atlantic trade.
story.zh:
这一贸易依赖骆驼——公元最初几个世纪骆驼在撒哈拉普及——以及熟悉沙漠的柏柏尔人，他们引导驼队穿越约两个月路程的沙海与砾石平原。北上的货物有黄金、象牙、可乐果和被奴役的人；南下的则有盐、铜、布匹、马匹和书籍。

阿拉伯地理学家留下了生动的描述。1068年在科尔多瓦编撰地理书的贝克里写道，加纳国王把所有金块据为己有，只把金砂留给百姓，以免黄金贬值。1352年穿越沙漠的伊本·白图泰在塔加扎盐矿停留，那里连房屋和清真寺都用盐块砌成、用驼皮作顶，饮水也是咸的。

西非黄金为中世纪地中海世界提供了大量铸币原料，从法蒂玛王朝的第纳尔到热那亚和卡斯蒂利亚的金币。驼队还把伊斯兰教、阿拉伯文字和学术带到奥达戈斯特、瓦拉塔、廷巴克图和加奥等萨赫勒城市。1591年摩洛哥入侵和大西洋贸易兴起之后，它的重要性逐渐衰退。

summary.en: Under Mali and Songhai rule, scholars of the Sankore, Djinguereber and Sidi Yahya mosques built family libraries of Arabic and Ajami manuscripts on law, theology, astronomy, medicine and history. Hundreds of thousands survive; many were smuggled to Bamako during the 2012 occupation.
summary.zh: 在马里和桑海统治下，桑科雷、津加里贝尔和西迪·叶海亚清真寺的学者建立家族图书馆，收藏以阿拉伯文和阿贾米文书写的法学、神学、天文、医学和历史手稿。存世手稿数以十万计，2012年城市被占领期间许多被秘密转移到巴马科。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Timbuktu
Britannica: Timbuktu
Wikipedia: Timbuktu Manuscripts
Leo Africanus, Description of Africa (1550), book VII: Timbuktu
Joshua Hammer, The Bad-Ass Librarians of Timbuktu (2016)

note: Span is conventional: the scholarly peak from the mid-15th century to the Moroccan conquest of 1591. Most surviving manuscripts were copied later, in the 16th–19th centuries.

story.en:
Timbuktu’s wealth lay as much in books as in gold. Scholarly families such as the Aqit, to whom Ahmad Baba belonged, taught law, grammar, theology and astronomy in the mosques of Sankore, Djinguereber and Sidi Yahya, and copied or bought manuscripts brought by caravan from Fez and Cairo. Leo Africanus, visiting in the early 16th century, remarked that books from North Africa were sold there at greater profit than any other merchandise.

The Moroccan conquest broke the scholarly community: in 1594 Ahmad Baba was taken in chains to Marrakesh and later lamented that he had lost some 1,600 volumes, the smallest library, he said, of anyone in his family. Yet families went on copying and hiding books for centuries, often in trunks and mud-walled storerooms.

When jihadist groups occupied Timbuktu in 2012, the librarian Abdel Kader Haidara and his network smuggled an estimated 350,000 manuscripts south to Bamako in footlockers, by road and river. Retreating fighters in January 2013 set fire to the Ahmed Baba Institute, destroying some 4,000 manuscripts, but most of the city’s written heritage survived.
story.zh:
廷巴克图的财富既在黄金，也在书籍。艾哈迈德·巴巴所属的阿基特家族等学者世家，在桑科雷、津加里贝尔和西迪·叶海亚清真寺讲授法学、语法、神学和天文学，并抄写或购买驼队从非斯和开罗运来的手稿。16世纪初到访的利奥·阿非利加努斯说，这里出售北非书籍比出售任何其他货物都更赚钱。

摩洛哥的征服打散了学者群体：1594年艾哈迈德·巴巴被戴上镣铐押往马拉喀什，他后来哀叹失去了约1600卷藏书，并说这在他家族中还是最小的藏书。然而数百年间，各家族仍不断抄写书籍，并把它们藏在箱子和泥墙储藏室里。

2012年圣战组织占领廷巴克图时，图书馆员阿卜杜勒·卡迪尔·海达拉及其网络用铁皮箱经公路和河道把约35万份手稿偷运到南方的巴马科。2013年1月撤退的武装分子纵火焚烧艾哈迈德·巴巴研究所，约四千份手稿被毁，但这座城市的文字遗产大部分得以保全。

name.en: Saint Catherine's Monastery built at Sinai
name.zh: 西奈圣凯瑟琳修道院建成

summary.en: Justinian I had a fortified monastery built at the foot of Mount Sinai around the traditional site of the Burning Bush. Never destroyed, it is among the oldest continuously inhabited Christian monasteries, and its library holds one of the largest collections of early manuscripts and icons.
summary.zh: 查士丁尼一世在西奈山麓传统认定的燃烧荆棘之处修建了一座设防修道院。它从未被毁，是持续有人居住的最古老基督教修道院之一，其图书馆收藏着数量极多的早期抄本和圣像。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Saint Catherine Area
Britannica: Saint Catherine's Monastery
Wikipedia: Saint Catherine's Monastery

note: Built between 548 and 565: the church's roof-beam inscriptions commemorate Justinian and the late empress Theodora (d. 548).

summary.en: A sudden release of carbon dioxide from the volcanic crater lake of Nyos in Cameroon flowed down the surrounding valleys at night, suffocating about 1,700 people and thousands of cattle. The rare limnic eruption led to degassing pipes being installed in the lake from 2001.
summary.zh: 喀麦隆火山口湖尼奥斯湖夜间突然释放大量二氧化碳，气体沿周围山谷下沉，令约1700人和数千头牲畜窒息死亡。这次罕见的湖底喷发促使人们自2001年起在湖中安装排气管。

sources.title: G. W. Kling et al., "The 1986 Lake Nyos Gas Disaster in Cameroon, West Africa", Science 236 (1987)
Britannica: Lake Nyos
Wikipedia: Lake Nyos disaster

name.zh: 首例人体心脏移植手术

summary.en: At Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town, Christiaan Barnard's team transplanted the heart of a young road-accident victim, Denise Darvall, into Louis Washkansky, who lived for 18 days. The operation made heart transplantation a worldwide clinical goal.
summary.zh: 在开普敦格罗特·舒尔医院，克里斯蒂安·巴纳德的团队将车祸遇难的年轻女子丹妮丝·达瓦尔的心脏移植给路易斯·沃什坎斯基，后者存活了18天。这次手术使心脏移植成为全球医学界追求的临床目标。

sources.title: Britannica: Christiaan Barnard
C. N. Barnard, "The operation. A human cardiac transplant", South African Medical Journal 41 (1967) (PubMed)
Wikipedia: Louis Washkansky
D. K. C. Cooper, ‘Christiaan Barnard and his contributions to heart transplantation’, Journal of Heart and Lung Transplantation 20 (2001)

note: No Wikidata item exists for the operation itself; the QID is omitted rather than borrowing the surgeon's or patient's item.

story.en:
On the afternoon of 2 December 1967, 25-year-old Denise Darvall and her mother were struck by a car as they crossed a road in Cape Town. Her mother died at the scene, and Denise was brought to Groote Schuur Hospital with irreparable brain injuries. Her father, Edward Darvall, agreed that her heart and kidneys could be donated.

In the early hours of 3 December a team of about thirty led by Christiaan Barnard, who had trained in transplant techniques in the United States, removed the 53-year-old grocer Louis Washkansky’s failing heart and replaced it with hers. When the new heart was shocked into rhythm, Barnard reportedly said in Afrikaans, “Dit gaan werk!” (“It’s going to work!”). Washkansky was soon sitting up and talking to reporters, but drugs given to suppress rejection left him vulnerable, and he died of pneumonia eighteen days later.

Barnard became a world celebrity. His second patient, Philip Blaiberg, lived for nineteen months with the heart of a Coloured man, an irony much noted in apartheid South Africa. Survival rates stayed poor until the immunosuppressant ciclosporin arrived in the 1980s.
story.zh:
1967年12月2日下午，25岁的丹尼丝·达瓦尔和母亲在开普敦过马路时被汽车撞倒。母亲当场身亡，丹尼丝被送到格罗特舒尔医院时脑部已受到不可逆的损伤。她的父亲爱德华·达瓦尔同意捐献她的心脏和肾脏。

12月3日凌晨，曾在美国学习移植技术的克里斯蒂安·巴纳德率领约三十人的团队，摘除了53岁杂货商路易斯·沃什坎斯基衰竭的心脏，换上了她的心脏。新心脏经电击恢复跳动时，据说巴纳德用阿非利卡语高喊：“能成功！”沃什坎斯基不久便能坐起来接受记者采访，但抑制排异的药物削弱了他的抵抗力，十八天后他死于肺炎。

巴纳德成了世界名人。他的第二位病人菲利普·布莱伯格靠一位“有色人”的心脏活了十九个月，这一讽刺在种族隔离时代的南非引起广泛议论。直到20世纪80年代免疫抑制剂环孢素问世，心脏移植的存活率才大为提高。

name.en: Cornelius Balbus campaigns against the Garamantes
name.zh: 科尔内利乌斯·巴尔布斯远征加拉曼特人

summary.en: The proconsul of Africa, Lucius Cornelius Balbus, led a Roman column deep into the Fezzan and took Garama, capital of the Garamantes, a Saharan people who farmed oases with underground channels. He celebrated a triumph in Rome in 19 BCE, the last ever held by a general outside the imperial family.
summary.zh: 阿非利加行省总督卢基乌斯·科尔内利乌斯·巴尔布斯率罗马军队深入费赞，攻占加拉曼特人的都城加拉马。加拉曼特人是以地下暗渠灌溉绿洲的撒哈拉民族。巴尔布斯于公元前19年在罗马举行凯旋式，这是皇室以外将领最后一次获此殊荣。

sources.title: Pliny the Elder, Natural History 5.35–37
David J. Mattingly (ed.), The Archaeology of Fazzan, vols. 1–4 (2003–2013)
Britannica: Garamantes
Wikipedia: Garamantes

note: The campaign is usually dated c. 20 BCE; the triumph (Fasti Triumphales) is dated 27 March 19 BCE.

story.en:
The Garamantes puzzled Greek and Roman writers. Herodotus described them hunting “cave-dwelling Ethiopians” from four-horse chariots; Roman authors treated them as raiders of the coastal cities. Archaeology in the Fezzan since the 1990s has shown something else: a Saharan state of walled towns, cemeteries of tens of thousands of graves and foggaras, hand-dug tunnels that tapped fossil groundwater and watered wheat, barley and dates in the middle of the desert.

Around 20 BCE the proconsul Lucius Cornelius Balbus marched south from Sabratha and took Garama itself. Pliny the Elder lists the names of the towns and peoples paraded in his triumph in 19 BCE. Balbus, from Gades in Spain, was the first man born outside Italy to hold a triumph, and the last who was not of the imperial house.

Rome never ruled the Fezzan. Instead the Garamantes became trading partners, exchanging slaves, carbuncles and ivory for wine, glass and fine pottery. Their oases declined from the 4th century as the groundwater ran down.
story.zh:
加拉曼特人让希腊罗马作家困惑不已。希罗多德说他们驾着四马战车追猎“穴居的埃塞俄比亚人”，罗马作家则把他们视为侵扰沿海城市的劫掠者。1990年代以来费赞的考古发掘揭示了另一幅图景：这是一个撒哈拉国家，有带城墙的城镇、埋葬数以万计死者的墓地，还有人工开凿的地下暗渠（foggara），引取古地下水，在沙漠中心灌溉小麦、大麦和椰枣。

约公元前20年，阿非利加总督卢基乌斯·科尔内利乌斯·巴尔布斯从萨布拉塔南下，攻占加拉马。老普林尼记下了公元前19年凯旋式上展示的城镇和部族名称。巴尔布斯出生于西班牙的加德斯，是第一位出生于意大利以外而获凯旋式的人，也是最后一位不属皇室的凯旋者。

罗马从未统治费赞。加拉曼特人转而成为贸易伙伴，用奴隶、红宝石和象牙换取葡萄酒、玻璃和精美陶器。4世纪起，随着地下水枯竭，他们的绿洲逐渐衰落。

summary.en: Kushite armies led by the kandake Amanirenas and Prince Akinidad raided Roman Egypt at Syene and Philae. The prefect Gaius Petronius struck back up the Nile as far as Napata, but Augustus finally granted Kush’s envoys peace at Samos and dropped his demand for tribute.
summary.zh: 库施军队在坎达克（女王）阿玛尼雷纳斯和王子阿基尼达德率领下袭击罗马埃及的赛伊尼和菲莱。埃及总督盖乌斯·佩特罗尼乌斯沿尼罗河反击，直抵纳帕塔，但奥古斯都最终在萨摩斯与库施使节议和，并放弃了纳贡要求。

label.zh: 库施人洗劫赛伊尼与象岛
佩特罗尼乌斯在普塞尔基斯击败库施军
罗马军攻占普里米斯（卡斯尔伊布里姆）
佩特罗尼乌斯夷平纳帕塔

label.en: Amanirenas besieges the Roman garrison at Primis
label.zh: 阿玛尼雷纳斯围攻普里米斯的罗马守军

label.en: Peace agreed with Augustus on Samos
label.zh: 在萨摩斯与奥古斯都议和

sources.title: Strabo, Geography 17.1.54
Cassius Dio, Roman History 54.5
László Török, The Kingdom of Kush: Handbook of the Napatan-Meroitic Civilization (1997)
British Museum: Bronze head of Augustus (the Meroë Head)
Wikipedia: Amanirenas

note: Dates follow Strabo and Cassius Dio and are approximate (c. 25–21/20 BCE). Strabo calls the queen “Candace”; her identification with Amanirenas rests on Meroitic inscriptions.

story.en:
In about 25 BCE, while the Roman prefect of Egypt was campaigning in Arabia, a Kushite army crossed the frontier at the First Cataract. It sacked Syene, Elephantine and Philae and carried off bronze statues of Augustus. Strabo calls its leader “Candace”, a one-eyed and “masculine” queen. Kushite inscriptions name her Amanirenas.

The prefect Gaius Petronius answered with 10,000 infantry and 800 cavalry. He beat the Kushites at Pselchis, stormed Primis and razed the royal city of Napata. When the queen counter-attacked the garrison at Primis, Petronius returned. In the end the Kushite envoys were sent to Augustus himself on Samos, and he granted all they asked, including the cancellation of tribute. The frontier then held for three centuries.

One of the captured statues survived. In 1910 the archaeologist John Garstang found a bronze head of Augustus buried beneath the steps of a temple at Meroë, where everyone who entered would tread on the emperor. It is now in the British Museum.
story.zh:
约公元前25年，罗马埃及总督正在阿拉伯作战，一支库施军队越过第一瀑布边境，洗劫赛伊尼、象岛和菲莱，掳走奥古斯都的青铜雕像。斯特拉波称其首领为“坎迪斯”，一位独眼而“具男子气概”的女王；库施铭文称她为阿玛尼雷纳斯。

总督盖乌斯·佩特罗尼乌斯率一万步兵、八百骑兵反击，在普塞尔基斯击败库施军，攻下普里米斯，夷平王城纳帕塔。女王反攻普里米斯守军时，佩特罗尼乌斯再度回援。最终库施使节被送到萨摩斯面见奥古斯都本人，他答应了全部请求，包括免除贡赋。此后边境安定了三个世纪。

一尊被掳走的雕像幸存下来。1910年，考古学家约翰·加斯唐在麦罗埃一座神庙的台阶下发现了奥古斯都的青铜头像：每位进入神庙的人都会踏过皇帝的头。它现藏于大英博物馆。

name.zh: 珀培图阿与费利西塔斯殉道

summary.en: The young noblewoman Vibia Perpetua, her pregnant slave Felicity and several companions were killed in the amphitheatre of Carthage. The Passion of Perpetua includes her own prison diary, one of the earliest surviving texts written by a Christian woman.
summary.zh: 年轻的贵族妇女维比娅·珀培图阿、她怀孕的女奴费利西塔斯及几位同伴在迦太基圆形剧场殉难。《珀培图阿受难记》收录了她本人的狱中日记，是现存最早的基督教女性著作之一。

sources.title: The Passion of Saints Perpetua and Felicity (c. 203)
Joyce E. Salisbury, Perpetua’s Passion: The Death and Memory of a Young Roman Woman (1997)
Britannica: Saints Perpetua and Felicity
Wikipedia: Perpetua and Felicity

story.en:
Vibia Perpetua was 22, well educated and nursing an infant son when she was arrested at Thuburbo Minus with other catechumens, probably under an edict of Septimius Severus against conversion. In prison she kept a diary. It records her pagan father begging her on his knees to give up her faith, and her reply: as a water jug can be called nothing but a jug, she could be called nothing but a Christian. She also wrote down visions, among them a bronze ladder to heaven guarded by a dragon.

Felicity, a slave, gave birth in prison three days before the games. On 7 March 203 the prisoners were sent into the arena of Carthage. A wild cow was set on the women, and a gladiator finished them with the sword. The editor adds that Perpetua herself guided his trembling hand to her throat.

The Passion was read aloud in African churches. Augustine preached on it two centuries later, warning his congregation not to rank it with Scripture.
story.zh:
维比娅·珀培图阿22岁，受过良好教育，正在哺育襁褓中的儿子。她与其他慕道者在图布尔博米努斯被捕，可能是因为塞普蒂米乌斯·塞维鲁禁止改宗的敕令。她在狱中写下日记：信奉异教的父亲跪地哀求她放弃信仰，她回答说，水罐只能叫水罐，她也只能叫基督徒。她还记下了异象，其中有一架由巨龙把守、通往天国的铜梯。

女奴费利西塔斯在竞技前三天于狱中分娩。203年3月7日，囚徒们被押入迦太基竞技场。一头野牛被放出冲撞两位女子，最后由角斗士持剑了结。编者补记说，珀培图阿亲手把颤抖的剑引向自己的咽喉。

这篇受难记在非洲教会中被诵读。两个世纪后奥古斯丁还为此布道，并提醒会众不要把它与《圣经》等量齐观。

name.en: Pachomius founds communal monasticism at Tabennisi
name.zh: 帕科米乌斯在塔本尼西创立集体修道制

summary.en: A former conscript, Pachomius gathered monks into a walled community at Tabennisi in Upper Egypt, with a written rule, shared work, meals and prayer. His federation of monasteries, for men and for women, became the model for cenobitic monasticism across the Christian world.
summary.zh: 曾被征召入伍的帕科米乌斯在上埃及的塔本尼西把修士聚集到有围墙的团体中，订立成文会规，共同劳作、用餐与祈祷。他建立的男女修道院联合体成为整个基督教世界集体修道制度的范本。

sources.title: The Bohairic and Greek Lives of Pachomius, trans. Armand Veilleux, Pachomian Koinonia (1980)
Philip Rousseau, Pachomius: The Making of a Community in Fourth-Century Egypt (1985)
Britannica: Saint Pachomius
Wikipedia: Pachomius the Great

note: The foundation is dated between c. 320 and 325; the site of Tabennisi near Nag Hammadi is approximate.

story.en:
Egypt gave Christianity two ways of leaving the world. Antony, the famous hermit, went alone into the desert. Pachomius, a young Copt conscripted into the army of Constantine’s rivals, took another path. According to his Lives, Christians in Thebes brought food to the conscripts locked up there, and he vowed to serve others as they had served him.

Around 323, at the deserted village of Tabennisi on the Nile, he began to organise monks into a koinonia, a community. Monks lived in houses grouped by trade, wore the same habit, ate together, worked at basket-weaving and farming, and obeyed a superior and a written rule. Pachomius’s sister Mary founded a women’s house nearby.

By his death in 346 there were nine monasteries. His rule was translated into Latin by Jerome in 404, and through John Cassian and later Benedict its ideas shaped the monasteries of medieval Europe.
story.zh:
埃及为基督教提供了两种出世之道。著名隐士安东尼独自走进沙漠；而帕科米乌斯走了另一条路。这位年轻的科普特人曾被君士坦丁的对手征召入伍。据其传记记载，底比斯的基督徒给关押在那里的新兵送饭，他便立誓要像他们那样服侍他人。

约323年，他在尼罗河畔废弃的塔本尼西村开始把修士组织成“共同体”。修士们按手艺分屋居住，穿同样的会衣，一同进餐，编篮务农，服从院长和成文会规。帕科米乌斯的姐姐玛丽在附近创建了女修院。

到346年他去世时，已有九座修道院。404年哲罗姆把他的会规译成拉丁文，经约翰·卡西安以及后来的本笃，这些理念塑造了中世纪欧洲的修道院。

name.en: Ezana’s campaign on the Nile and the end of Meroë
name.zh: 埃扎纳的尼罗河远征与麦罗埃的终结

summary.en: A Ge’ez inscription of King Ezana describes an Aksumite army marching to the confluence of the Nile and the Atbara, defeating the Noba and burning towns of the Kasu. By then the Meroitic kingdom of Kush had already been weakened by the loss of trade to Aksum, and its royal burials ended soon after.
summary.zh: 阿克苏姆国王埃扎纳的一块吉兹语碑文记载，阿克苏姆军队进军至尼罗河与阿特巴拉河汇流处，击败诺巴人，焚烧卡苏人的城镇。当时库施的麦罗埃王国已因贸易被阿克苏姆夺走而衰弱，其王陵此后不久便告终止。

sources.title: Inscription of Ezana, RIE 189 (Deutsche Aksum-Expedition)
Stuart Munro-Hay, Aksum: An African Civilisation of Late Antiquity (1991), ch. 4
László Török, The Kingdom of Kush (1997)
Wikipedia: Kingdom of Kush

note: The date (c. 350) and whether Meroë itself was still a royal capital at the time are debated.

name.zh: 汪达尔战争：贝利撒留收复北非

summary.en: Justinian sent Belisarius with about 15,000 men to overthrow the Vandal king Gelimer. Two victories, at Ad Decimum and Tricamarum, ended the Vandal kingdom within six months and returned Carthage and the African provinces to the Roman Empire.
summary.zh: 查士丁尼派贝利撒留率约一万五千人推翻汪达尔国王盖利默。阿德底斯慕姆和特里卡梅伦两场胜利在六个月内终结了汪达尔王国，迦太基及北非诸行省重归罗马帝国。

label.zh: 在卡普特瓦达登陆
经哈德鲁梅图姆北上
阿德底斯慕姆大捷（9月13日）
进入迦太基（9月15日）
特里卡梅伦大捷（12月）
盖利默在帕普亚山投降

sources.title: Procopius, History of the Wars, Books III–IV (The Vandalic War)
Andy Merrills and Richard Miles, The Vandals (2010)
Britannica: Vandal
Wikipedia: Vandalic War

note: Mount Papua’s exact location in the Edough massif west of Hippo is uncertain; the route stop is approximate.

story.en:
In 530 the Vandal king Hilderic, who favoured the Catholics and had good relations with Constantinople, was deposed by his cousin Gelimer. Justinian took this as a pretext. Many of his advisers remembered the disaster of the great expedition of 468 and argued against it, but he sent Belisarius in 533 with about 15,000 men in 500 transports. Procopius, his secretary, sailed with him.

Luck ran Belisarius’s way. Gelimer’s brother had taken the best Vandal troops to put down a revolt in Sardinia. At Ad Decimum, ten miles from Carthage, Gelimer’s plan to trap the Romans fell apart when his brother Ammatas attacked too early and was killed, and Gelimer stopped to bury him. Belisarius entered Carthage on 15 September and, Procopius says, ate the dinner prepared for the Vandal king.

After defeat at Tricamarum Gelimer fled into the mountains. He surrendered in 534. Procopius reports that he asked for a lyre to sing of his misfortune, a sponge for his eyes and a loaf of bread. He walked in Belisarius’s triumph in Constantinople.
story.zh:
530年，亲近天主教徒、与君士坦丁堡交好的汪达尔国王希尔德里克被堂兄盖利默废黜。查士丁尼以此为借口出兵。许多大臣记得468年大远征的惨败而反对，他仍于533年派贝利撒留率约一万五千人、五百艘运输船出征，秘书普罗科匹厄斯随行。

运气站在贝利撒留一边。盖利默的弟弟带着汪达尔精锐去撒丁岛平叛。在距迦太基十罗马里的阿德底斯慕姆，盖利默设下的包围计划因其弟阿马塔斯过早出击阵亡而落空，盖利默又停下来为他收尸。贝利撒留于9月15日进入迦太基，据普罗科匹厄斯说，他吃掉了为汪达尔国王准备的晚餐。

特里卡梅伦战败后，盖利默逃入山中，534年投降。普罗科匹厄斯记载，他讨要一把里拉琴来吟唱自己的不幸，一块海绵擦拭泪眼，还有一条面包。他后来在君士坦丁堡的凯旋式上走在贝利撒留之前。

name.zh: 传教士使努比亚诸王国皈依基督教

summary.en: Rival missions from Constantinople brought Christianity to the three Nubian kingdoms: the priest Julian, sent by Empress Theodora, reached Nobatia in 543; Makuria accepted the Chalcedonian creed of Justinian around 569; and Longinus baptised the king of Alodia in 580. Nubia remained Christian for nearly a thousand years.
summary.zh: 来自君士坦丁堡的对立传教团把基督教带到努比亚三国：543年，狄奥多拉皇后派遣的教士尤利安抵达诺巴蒂亚；约569年，马库里亚接受查士丁尼支持的卡尔西顿信条；580年，朗吉努斯为阿洛迪亚国王施洗。努比亚此后信奉基督教近千年。

sources.title: John of Ephesus, Ecclesiastical History, Part III, Book IV
William Y. Adams, Nubia: Corridor to Africa (1977)
Derek A. Welsby, The Medieval Kingdoms of Nubia (2002)
Wikipedia: Christian Nubia

note: Dates follow John of Ephesus; the conversion of Makuria (c. 569) is less well documented.

story.en:
According to John of Ephesus, a Miaphysite bishop who knew the people involved, the conversion of Nubia began as a race between husband and wife. Justinian supported the Chalcedonian creed, while the Empress Theodora protected its Miaphysite opponents. When she heard that the emperor was sending envoys to Nobatia, she sent her own priest, Julian, and warned the governor of Upper Egypt that he would lose his head if the emperor’s party arrived first. The governor delayed them, and Julian baptised the Nobatian king in 543.

Makuria, further south, took the imperial creed instead around 569. In 580 the bishop Longinus slipped past Makurian opposition to reach Alodia, at the confluence of the Niles, and baptised its king.

The result was a Christian Nubia with cathedrals at Faras, Old Dongola and Soba. The paintings of Faras, saved by Polish archaeologists before Lake Nasser flooded the site in the 1960s, show bishops and kings of Nubia side by side with Christ and the saints.
story.zh:
据认识当事人的米亚菲西派主教以弗所的约翰记载，努比亚的皈依起初是一场夫妻之间的竞赛。查士丁尼支持卡尔西顿信条，皇后狄奥多拉则庇护其反对者米亚菲西派。她听说皇帝要派使节去诺巴蒂亚，便派出自己的教士尤利安，并警告上埃及总督：若皇帝的使团先到，他就人头落地。总督拖住了皇帝的人，尤利安于543年为诺巴蒂亚国王施洗。

更南面的马库里亚约在569年接受了帝国的信条。580年，主教朗吉努斯绕过马库里亚的阻挠，抵达青白尼罗河汇流处的阿洛迪亚，为其国王施洗。

于是出现了一个基督教的努比亚，法拉斯、老栋古拉和索巴建起了大教堂。1960年代纳赛尔湖淹没法拉斯之前，波兰考古学家抢救出那里的壁画，画中努比亚的主教和国王与基督和圣徒并肩而立。

name.zh: 伊德里斯一世建立非斯

summary.en: Idris ibn Abdallah, a descendant of the Prophet who had fled the Abbasids, founded a town on the right bank of the Fez river in 789; his son Idris II added a second town on the left bank in 809. Settlers from Kairouan and Córdoba gave the two quarters their names and made Fez the intellectual capital of Morocco.
summary.zh: 先知后裔伊德里斯·本·阿卜杜拉逃离阿拔斯王朝后，于789年在非斯河右岸建城；其子伊德里斯二世于809年在左岸另建新城。来自凯鲁万和科尔多瓦的移民为两个城区命名，使非斯成为摩洛哥的学术之都。

sources.title: Britannica: Fès
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Medina of Fez
Roger Le Tourneau, Fez in the Age of the Marinides (1961)
Wikipedia: Fez, Morocco

note: Sources give 789 for the first foundation and 808/809 for the second; some historians attribute both foundations to Idris II.

name.en: Ziyadat Allah I rebuilds the Great Mosque of Kairouan
name.zh: 齐亚达特·安拉一世重建凯鲁万大清真寺

summary.en: The Aghlabid emir Ziyadat Allah I demolished and rebuilt the mosque first founded by ʿUqba ibn Nafiʿ in 670, giving it the form it largely keeps today: a hypostyle prayer hall on reused Roman columns and a massive three-storey minaret, the oldest standing minaret in the western Islamic world.
summary.zh: 阿格拉布王朝埃米尔齐亚达特·安拉一世拆除并重建了乌格巴·本·纳菲于670年始建的清真寺，奠定了其今日的基本格局：以重新利用的罗马石柱支撑的多柱礼拜大厅，以及一座三层巨型宣礼塔，它是伊斯兰世界西部现存最古老的宣礼塔。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Kairouan
Jonathan M. Bloom, Architecture of the Islamic West: North Africa and the Iberian Peninsula, 700–1800 (2020)
Qantara Mediterranean Heritage: Great Mosque of Kairouan
Wikipedia: Great Mosque of Kairouan

note: Wikidata dates the building to its first foundation (670); this record marks the 836 reconstruction.

story.en:
Kairouan began as a military camp. ʿUqba ibn Nafiʿ chose the site in 670, a day’s ride from the coast and the Byzantine fleet, and laid out a simple mosque at its centre. As the camp became the capital of Ifriqiya, the mosque was rebuilt again and again.

The Aghlabid emir Ziyadat Allah I pulled it down in 836 and started again on a grand scale. The prayer hall rests on more than 400 columns taken from Roman and Byzantine ruins, so that capitals of different styles stand side by side. The square minaret, three tiers high, became the model for minarets across the Maghreb and al-Andalus.

Around 862 his successor Abu Ibrahim Ahmad decorated the mihrab with lustre-painted tiles, many of them apparently brought from Iraq, and a carved wooden minbar, the oldest surviving minbar still in its original place. Pilgrims long said that seven visits to Kairouan were worth one to Mecca.
story.zh:
凯鲁万起初是一座军营。670年，乌格巴·本·纳菲选定此地，距海岸和拜占庭舰队一日路程，并在营地中央建起一座简朴的清真寺。随着军营成为伊夫里基叶的首府，清真寺一再重建。

836年，阿格拉布王朝埃米尔齐亚达特·安拉一世将其拆除，以宏大规模重建。礼拜大厅由四百多根取自罗马和拜占庭遗址的石柱支撑，风格各异的柱头并列其间。三层方形宣礼塔成为马格里布和安达卢斯各地宣礼塔的范本。

约862年，其继任者阿布·易卜拉欣·艾哈迈德用虹彩釉面砖装饰米哈拉布，其中许多似乎来自伊拉克；又添置了一座木雕敏拜尔，是至今仍在原位的最古老敏拜尔。朝圣者长期流传，七次拜谒凯鲁万抵得上一次麦加朝觐。

summary.en: In the 9th–10th centuries, metalworkers at Igbo-Ukwu in south-eastern Nigeria cast intricate leaded-bronze vessels and ornaments by the lost-wax method, and a dignitary was buried with them and with more than 100,000 glass beads. They are the oldest known bronze castings in West Africa.
summary.zh: 9至10世纪，尼日利亚东南部伊格博-乌库的金属工匠用失蜡法铸造了精美的含铅青铜器皿和饰品，一位显贵与这些器物及十万余颗玻璃珠一同下葬。这是西非已知最早的青铜铸件。

sources.title: Thurstan Shaw, Igbo-Ukwu: An Account of Archaeological Discoveries in Eastern Nigeria (1970)
Metropolitan Museum of Art, Heilbrunn Timeline: Igbo-Ukwu (ca. 9th century)
Wikipedia: Archaeology of Igbo-Ukwu

note: Radiocarbon dates cluster in the 9th–10th centuries; the date is approximate. The QID is the Igbo-Ukwu archaeological site, which has no separate item for the bronzes.

story.en:
In 1938 a man named Isaiah Anozie was digging a water cistern in his compound at Igbo-Ukwu when he struck bronze. Most of what he found was given away or sold before a colonial officer saw it. The archaeologist Thurstan Shaw excavated the site properly in 1959–60 and 1964 and found three deposits: a store of ritual objects, a pit of discarded items and a burial chamber in which a richly dressed man had been seated on a stool, surrounded by bronzes, ivory tusks and tens of thousands of beads.

The bronzes astonished art historians: a water pot wrapped in cast rope, shells and calabashes rendered in metal and covered in tiny granules, insects resting on their surfaces. Radiocarbon dating placed them around the 9th and 10th centuries, centuries before Ife or Benin.

The metal came from local ores, but some beads came from as far as Egypt or India, a sign that this forest community was already tied into long-distance trade.
story.zh:
1938年，伊赛亚·阿诺齐在伊格博-乌库自家院子里挖蓄水池时挖到了青铜器。在殖民地官员见到之前，大部分已被送人或卖掉。考古学家瑟斯坦·肖于1959至1960年和1964年进行了正式发掘，发现三处埋藏：一处储存礼器，一处丢弃杂物的坑，还有一座墓室，一位盛装男子端坐凳上，四周环绕着青铜器、象牙和数以万计的珠子。

这些青铜器令艺术史学者惊叹：一只被铸造绳索缠绕的水罐，以金属仿制的贝壳和葫芦，表面布满细小颗粒，还有昆虫停在器物上。放射性碳测年将其定在9至10世纪，比伊费和贝宁早了数百年。

金属来自当地矿石，但有些珠子远自埃及或印度，说明这个森林社群当时已融入长途贸易。

name.en: Banu Hilal invade Ifriqiya: Battle of Haydaran
name.zh: 巴努希拉勒入侵伊夫里基叶：海达兰之战

summary.en: After the Zirid emir al-Muʿizz ibn Badis broke with the Fatimids, Cairo encouraged the Arab Banu Hilal and Banu Sulaym tribes to move west. They routed the Zirid army at Haydaran in 1052 and in 1057 forced al-Muʿizz to abandon Kairouan for the coastal fortress of Mahdia.
summary.zh: 齐里王朝埃米尔穆伊兹·本·巴迪斯与法蒂玛王朝决裂后，开罗鼓动阿拉伯部落巴努希拉勒和巴努苏莱姆西迁。他们于1052年在海达兰击溃齐里军队，1057年迫使穆伊兹放弃凯鲁万，退守沿海要塞马赫迪耶。

sources.title: Ibn Khaldun, Kitab al-ʿIbar (History of the Berbers), trans. de Slane
Michael Brett, “Fitnat al-Qayrawan: A Study of Traditional Arabic Historiography” (PhD thesis, 1970)
Britannica: Hilal, Banu
Wikipedia: Banu Hilal

note: Haydaran is placed near Gabès, following Wikidata; the exact site is uncertain. The scale of the destruction described by Ibn Khaldun is debated by modern historians.

story.en:
In the 1040s the Zirid emir al-Muʿizz ibn Badis, ruler of Ifriqiya in the name of the Fatimid caliphs, stopped naming them in the Friday prayer and recognised the Abbasids of Baghdad instead. The Fatimid vizier al-Yazuri could not afford an army. Instead, the chronicles say, he gave the Banu Hilal and Banu Sulaym, Bedouin tribes troublesome in Upper Egypt, a gold coin and a camel each and told them that Ifriqiya was theirs.

At Haydaran in 1052 a much larger Zirid army, with many Arab contingents who may have changed sides, broke before the tribesmen. In 1057 al-Muʿizz left Kairouan for Mahdia, and the old capital was plundered.

Ibn Khaldun, writing three centuries later, compared the Hilalians to a swarm of locusts that turned the Maghreb into desert. Historians now think the decline was slower and more complicated. But the migration permanently changed the region: it spread Arabic among the rural population, and the epic of the Taghriba, the Hilalian wanderings, is still sung in Egypt and Tunisia.
story.zh:
1040年代，以法蒂玛哈里发名义统治伊夫里基叶的齐里王朝埃米尔穆伊兹·本·巴迪斯不再在聚礼中为他们祈祷，转而承认巴格达的阿拔斯王朝。法蒂玛维齐尔亚祖里无力派兵。据编年史记载，他给了在上埃及闹事的贝都因部落巴努希拉勒和巴努苏莱姆每人一枚金币和一头骆驼，告诉他们伊夫里基叶归他们所有。

1052年在海达兰，人数多得多的齐里军队（其中许多阿拉伯部队可能临阵倒戈）在部落民面前崩溃。1057年穆伊兹离开凯鲁万前往马赫迪耶，故都遭到洗劫。

三个世纪后的伊本·赫勒敦把希拉勒人比作一群蝗虫，使马格里布沦为荒漠。今天的史学家认为衰落过程更缓慢、更复杂。但这次迁徙永久改变了该地区：阿拉伯语在乡村人口中传播开来，讲述希拉勒人漂泊的史诗《塔格里巴》至今仍在埃及和突尼斯传唱。

name.en: Al-Bakri describes the kingdom of Ghana

summary.en: In his Book of Routes and Realms, the Andalusian geographer al-Bakri described Ghana’s capital as two towns six miles apart: a merchants’ town with twelve mosques and the king’s town with his palace and sacred groves. It is the fullest eyewitness-based account of the empire at its height.
summary.zh: 安达卢斯地理学家巴克里在《道里邦国志》中描述加纳都城由相距六英里的两座城镇组成：一座是有十二座清真寺的商人之城，一座是有王宫和圣林的国王之城。这是关于鼎盛时期加纳帝国最详尽、以亲历者见闻为基础的记载。

sources.title: al-Bakri, Kitab al-Masalik wa-l-Mamalik (1068), in N. Levtzion and J. F. P. Hopkins (eds.), Corpus of Early Arabic Sources for West African History (1981)
Nehemia Levtzion, Ancient Ghana and Mali (1973)
Britannica: Ghana, ancient kingdom
Wikipedia: Abu Abdullah al-Bakri

note: Al-Bakri never left al-Andalus; he compiled the account from merchants and from the lost work of Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Warraq. Identification of the capital with Koumbi Saleh is probable but not certain.

story.en:
Abu ʿUbayd al-Bakri never crossed the Sahara. He worked in Córdoba and Almería from merchants’ reports and older books, but his account of Ghana in 1068 is so detailed that historians treat it as the best picture of the empire.

The king, Tunka Manin, he says, sat in a domed pavilion surrounded by horses wearing gold-embroidered cloth, by pages holding gold-mounted shields and swords, and by the sons of vassal kings with gold braided in their hair. Dogs of excellent pedigree guarded the door, wearing collars of gold and silver. Subjects who approached him fell to their knees and sprinkled dust on their heads; Muslims clapped their hands instead.

Al-Bakri also explains the economics. Every nugget found in the mines belonged to the king, and the people could keep only gold dust, so that the metal would not become too plentiful and lose its value. Salt entering the country paid one dinar a donkey-load, and leaving it, two. Within a few decades the Almoravids had shaken this kingdom, and power in the region passed to Sosso and then to Mali.
story.zh:
阿布·乌拜德·巴克里从未穿越撒哈拉。他在科尔多瓦和阿尔梅里亚根据商人的报告和早期著作写作，但他在1068年对加纳的记述极为详尽，史学家视之为关于这个帝国的最佳图景。

他说，国王坦卡·马宁坐在一座圆顶亭中，四周是披着金线绣布的马匹，手持镶金盾剑的侍从，还有发间编着金饰的诸侯之子。门口由血统名贵的猎犬守卫，戴着金银项圈。臣民觐见时双膝跪地，往头上撒土；穆斯林则以拍手代替。

巴克里还解释了其中的经济逻辑：矿中发现的每块金块都归国王所有，百姓只能保留金砂，以免黄金过多而贬值。运盐入境每驴驮交一第纳尔，出境交两第纳尔。几十年内，穆拉比特人动摇了这个王国，区域霸权先后转到索索和马里手中。

name.en: Mai Hummay of Kanem adopts Islam
name.zh: 加涅姆国王胡迈皈依伊斯兰教

summary.en: According to the Girgam, the royal chronicle of Kanem–Bornu, Hummay (Humé) ibn Abd al-Jalil was converted by the scholar Muhammad ibn Mani and became the first Muslim king of Kanem, founding the Sayfawa line that would rule around Lake Chad until 1846.
summary.zh: 据加涅姆-博尔努王室编年史《吉尔甘》记载，胡迈（胡梅）·本·阿卜杜勒·贾利勒受学者穆罕默德·本·马尼感化，成为加涅姆首位穆斯林国王，开创了统治乍得湖周边直至1846年的赛法瓦王朝。

sources.title: The Mahram of Humé, in H. R. Palmer, The Bornu Sahara and Sudan (1936)
Dierk Lange, A Sudanic Chronicle: The Borno Expeditions of Idris Alauma (1987)
Britannica: Kanem-Bornu
Wikipedia: Hummay

note: The conversion is dated c. 1068–1085 in different king lists. The site of the early capital Njimi is unknown; the marker is approximate.

summary.en: Between the 12th and 15th centuries, artists at Ile-Ife, the sacred city of the Yoruba, made naturalistic heads in copper alloy and terracotta, probably portraits of Ooni (kings) and their court. Their discovery in the 20th century overturned European assumptions about African art.
summary.zh: 12至15世纪，约鲁巴人的圣城伊莱-伊费的艺术家用铜合金和陶土制作写实头像，很可能是奥尼（国王）及其宫廷成员的肖像。20世纪这些头像的发现颠覆了欧洲人对非洲艺术的成见。

sources.title: British Museum: Ife head (Af1939,34.1)
Henry John Drewal and Enid Schildkrout, Dynasty and Divinity: Ife Art in Ancient Nigeria (2009)
Metropolitan Museum of Art, Heilbrunn Timeline: Ife (from ca. 350 B.C.)
Wikipedia: Ife Heads

note: Most castings are dated to the 14th–early 15th centuries; terracottas span the 12th–15th. The date marks the peak.

story.en:
In 1910 the German ethnographer Leo Frobenius dug at Ile-Ife and found a bronze head of the sea god Olokun. He was so struck by its classical calm that he decided it must be the work of a lost Greek colony, the “Atlantis” of his imagination. He was wrong. Colonial officials made him give the head back, and the one now kept in Ife is thought to be a later copy; what became of the original is unknown.

In 1938 builders digging foundations in the Wunmonije compound, near the Ooni’s palace, unearthed thirteen copper-alloy heads, and others followed. Life-size, with fine vertical lines over the faces and holes along the hairline where beads or a veil may have hung, they are among the most naturalistic portraits made anywhere in the medieval world. Analysis showed that some are almost pure copper, which is very hard to cast.

For the Yoruba, Ife is where the world was created and where kingship began. The heads, probably used in funerary rites for kings, are now treasured in the National Museum in Ife and the British Museum.
story.zh:
1910年，德国民族学家莱奥·弗罗贝纽斯在伊莱-伊费发掘，发现一尊海神奥洛昆的青铜头像。其古典式的宁静令他震撼，他断定这必定出自一个失落的希腊殖民地，即他想象中的“亚特兰蒂斯”。他错了。殖民当局迫使他交还头像，而如今保存在伊费的那尊被认为是后来的复制品，原件下落不明。

1938年，工人在奥尼王宫附近的温莫尼杰院落挖地基，挖出十三尊铜合金头像，其后又有更多发现。这些头像与真人等大，脸上有细密的竖纹，发际线有一排小孔，可能曾挂珠串或面纱，是中世纪世界最写实的肖像之一。分析显示有些几乎是纯铜，铸造难度极高。

在约鲁巴人看来，伊费是创世之地和王权的起源。这些头像可能用于国王的葬礼仪式，今藏于伊费国家博物馆和大英博物馆。

name.en: Yekuno Amlak founds the Solomonic dynasty
name.zh: 耶库诺·阿姆拉克建立所罗门王朝

summary.en: Yekuno Amlak, a lord from Amhara, overthrew the last Zagwe king and took the throne, claiming descent from Solomon and the Queen of Sheba through the old kings of Aksum. His line ruled Ethiopia, with interruptions, until 1974.
summary.zh: 来自阿姆哈拉的领主耶库诺·阿姆拉克推翻扎格维王朝末代国王登上王位，自称经阿克苏姆古王系承袭所罗门王与示巴女王的血统。他的家族断续统治埃塞俄比亚直至1974年。

sources.title: Taddesse Tamrat, Church and State in Ethiopia, 1270–1527 (1972)
Harold G. Marcus, A History of Ethiopia (1994)
Britannica: Ethiopia: The Solomonic dynasty
Wikipedia: Yekuno Amlak

note: The year 1270 is conventional. Accounts of the role of the monks Iyasus Moʾa and Tekle Haymanot, and of the land grant said to have rewarded the church, come from later hagiographies.

story.en:
The Zagwe kings had built the churches of Lalibela, but they were never fully accepted as legitimate: they could not claim descent from the kings of Aksum. Yekuno Amlak, a regional lord in Amhara, made that claim his banner. After defeating and killing the Zagwe king, traditionally named Yetbarak, in about 1270, he presented his victory as the restoration of the house of Solomon.

According to later church tradition, he was helped by two monks, Iyasus Moʾa of the monastery on Lake Hayq and Tekle Haymanot, founder of Debre Libanos, and in return promised a third of the kingdom’s land to the church. Historians doubt the details but agree that the alliance between the new dynasty and the monasteries was real and lasting.

The Kebra Nagast, compiled some decades later, gave the dynasty its founding legend: Menelik, son of Solomon and Sheba, had brought the Ark of the Covenant to Aksum. Ethiopian emperors carried the title “Elect of God, Conquering Lion of the Tribe of Judah” until Haile Selassie was deposed in 1974.
story.zh:
扎格维诸王建造了拉利贝拉的教堂，却始终未被完全视为正统，因为他们无法自称阿克苏姆诸王的后裔。阿姆哈拉的地方领主耶库诺·阿姆拉克正是打出了这面旗帜。约1270年，他击败并杀死扎格维国王（传统上称为耶特巴拉克），宣称自己的胜利是所罗门王室的复辟。

据后来的教会传统，他得到了两位修士的帮助：海克湖修道院的伊亚苏斯·莫阿和德卜雷利巴诺斯修道院的创建者特克勒·海马诺特，作为回报，他许诺把王国三分之一的土地献给教会。史学家对细节存疑，但都认为新王朝与修道院的联盟真实而持久。

数十年后编成的《国王的荣耀》为王朝提供了开国神话：所罗门与示巴之子孟尼利克把约柜带到了阿克苏姆。埃塞俄比亚皇帝一直使用“上帝的选民、犹大支派的雄狮”称号，直到1974年海尔·塞拉西被废黜。

name.zh: 马穆鲁克埃及的黑死病

summary.en: Plague reached Alexandria in autumn 1347 on ships from the Black Sea and spread up the Nile. At its peak in Cairo in late 1348 chroniclers counted thousands of deaths a day. Egypt may have lost a quarter to a third of its people, and repeated outbreaks undermined Mamluk agriculture for a century.
summary.zh: 1347年秋，瘟疫随来自黑海的船只抵达亚历山大港并沿尼罗河扩散。1348年底开罗疫情最烈时，编年史家记录每天死亡数千人。埃及可能失去了四分之一到三分之一的人口，此后反复暴发的瘟疫使马穆鲁克王朝的农业衰退长达一个世纪。

sources.title: Michael W. Dols, The Black Death in the Middle East (1977)
al-Maqrizi, Kitab al-Suluk li-Maʿrifat Duwal al-Muluk
Stuart J. Borsch, The Black Death in Egypt and England: A Comparative Study (2005)
Wikipedia: Black Death in the Middle East
Ross E. Dunn, The Adventures of Ibn Battuta (1986), ch. 12

note: Mortality figures from the Mamluk chroniclers (up to 20,000 a day in Cairo) are probably exaggerated; modern estimates vary widely. This is the Egyptian part of the pandemic recorded as ev-black-death in data/europe; Wikidata has only a broader item for the Middle East (Q92159855), so no QID is set.

story.en:
The pandemic that Europe remembers as the Black Death, followed in this atlas’s own entry for it, reached Egypt by sea. In the autumn of 1347 a ship from the Black Sea put in at Alexandria; according to al-Maqrizi, almost everyone aboard was dead or dying. Within months the disease had spread through the Delta to Cairo, then perhaps the largest city west of China.

The chroniclers describe the capital in late 1348: biers ran short, so bodies were carried on planks and doors; prayers for the dead were said over dozens at once; the government ordered the Quran recited in public. Al-Maqrizi, writing later, gives 10,000 to 20,000 deaths a day, an exaggeration of a genuine catastrophe. Two great writers of the age lived through it: Ibn Battuta crossed plague-stricken Syria and Egypt in 1348 on his way home, and in Tunis the young Ibn Khaldun lost both his parents.

The consequences lasted longer in Egypt than in Europe. Stuart Borsch argues that the Mamluk system, in which absentee military lords drew rents from villages and kept up the irrigation canals, could not adjust to the loss of peasants. Canals silted, fields went out of cultivation, and the plague returned roughly every decade for a century.
story.zh:
这场被欧洲人称为“黑死病”的大流行（本图集另有专门条目）经海路传到埃及。1347年秋，一艘来自黑海的船驶抵亚历山大港；据马克里兹记载，船上的人几乎全都死去或垂死。数月之内，疫病经三角洲传入开罗，这座城市当时可能是中国以西最大的城市。

编年史家描述了1348年底的都城：棺架不够用，尸体只能放在木板和门板上抬运；一次为数十名死者举行殡礼；政府下令公开诵读《古兰经》。后来写作的马克里兹给出每天死亡一万至两万人的数字，这是对真实灾难的夸大。那个时代的两位大作家亲历了这场瘟疫：1348年伊本·白图泰在归途中穿越疫病肆虐的叙利亚和埃及，而在突尼斯，年轻的伊本·赫勒敦失去了双亲。

这场灾难在埃及的后果比欧洲更持久。斯图尔特·博尔施认为，马穆鲁克体制由不在地的军事领主从村庄收租并维护灌溉渠道，无法适应农民锐减的局面。渠道淤塞，田地荒芜，此后一个世纪瘟疫大约每十年卷土重来一次。

name.en: Sunni Ali takes Timbuktu and Djenné
name.zh: 索尼·阿里攻取廷巴克图与杰内

summary.en: The Songhai king Sunni Ali drove the Tuareg out of Timbuktu in 1468 and, after a long siege, took Djenné around 1473, turning Gao’s kingdom into the largest state of the western Sudan. The Timbuktu chroniclers, hostile to him, remembered him as a tyrant who persecuted scholars.
summary.zh: 桑海国王索尼·阿里于1468年把图阿雷格人逐出廷巴克图，约1473年经长期围攻夺取杰内，使加奥王国成为西苏丹最大的国家。对他心怀敌意的廷巴克图编年史家把他记作迫害学者的暴君。

sources.title: ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Saʿdi, Tarikh al-Sudan (c. 1655), trans. J. O. Hunwick, Timbuktu and the Songhay Empire (1999)
Britannica: Sonni ʿAlī
Wikipedia: Sonni Ali

note: Al-Saʿdi says the siege of Djenné lasted seven years, seven months and seven days, a formulaic figure; the fall is dated c. 1473.

story.en:
Timbuktu had been under Tuareg control since about 1433, and its leading scholars had made their peace with the Tuareg chief Akil. When Sunni Ali’s cavalry approached in 1468, Akil fled, taking many of the city’s scholars with him to Walata. Sunni Ali’s troops sacked the town, and the king, who suspected the remaining jurists of collaboration, had some of them killed.

That is why the 17th-century chronicles written in Timbuktu treat him so harshly. Al-Saʿdi calls him “the great tyrant” and says he was a Muslim in name only, mixing Islam with the old Songhai cults of the river. Songhai oral tradition, by contrast, remembers Si (Sunni) as a sorcerer-king who could never be defeated.

Djenné, protected by the waters of the flood plain, held out much longer; the chroniclers’ “seven years, seven months and seven days” mark the siege as legendary. When Sunni Ali drowned or died on campaign in 1492, he left a large empire but a quarrel with the Muslim elite that his general Askia Muhammad exploited the next year.
story.zh:
廷巴克图自约1433年起受图阿雷格人控制，城中的主要学者已与图阿雷格首领阿基勒相安无事。1468年索尼·阿里的骑兵逼近时，阿基勒出逃，带走许多学者前往瓦拉塔。索尼·阿里的军队洗劫城镇，国王怀疑留下的法学家通敌，处死了其中一些人。

因此，17世纪在廷巴克图写成的编年史对他极为严厉。萨迪称他为“大暴君”，说他只是名义上的穆斯林，把伊斯兰教与桑海人古老的河神崇拜混在一起。而桑海口头传统则把西（索尼）记作战无不胜的巫王。

杰内有泛滥平原的河水保护，坚守得更久；编年史中“七年七月零七天”的说法把这次围城变成了传奇。1492年索尼·阿里在征战中溺亡或去世，留下一个大帝国，也留下了与穆斯林精英的嫌隙，次年他的将领阿斯基亚·穆罕默德便利用了这一点。

name.en: Portuguese build São Jorge da Mina (Elmina)
name.zh: 葡萄牙人修建圣乔治·达米纳城堡（埃尔米纳）

summary.en: Diogo de Azambuja landed with prefabricated stone and timber and built the castle of São Jorge da Mina on the Gold Coast, the first European fortress in sub-Saharan Africa. Built for the gold trade, it later became a major holding point for enslaved Africans under the Portuguese and, from 1637, the Dutch.
summary.zh: 迪奥戈·德·阿赞布雅带着预制的石料和木材登陆黄金海岸，修建了圣乔治·达米纳城堡，这是撒哈拉以南非洲第一座欧洲要塞。它原为黄金贸易而建，后来在葡萄牙人和1637年起的荷兰人手中成为关押被奴役非洲人的主要据点。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Forts and Castles, Volta, Greater Accra, Central and Western Regions
John Vogt, Portuguese Rule on the Gold Coast, 1469–1682 (1979)
Britannica: Elmina
Wikipedia: Elmina Castle

story.en:
Portuguese traders had been buying gold on this stretch of coast since 1471. To keep Castilian and other rivals away, King João II sent Diogo de Azambuja in December 1481 with about a dozen ships, nine caravels and two transports by one count, carrying some 600 soldiers and craftsmen and pre-cut building stone, lime and timber, everything needed to raise a fortress quickly.

According to the Portuguese chronicler Rui de Pina, the local ruler, whom the Portuguese called Caramansa, received Azambuja with ceremony but warned that friends who met only occasionally stayed friends longer than neighbours. When the masons began to quarry a rock the people held sacred, there was fighting, settled with gifts. The walls rose in about three weeks in January 1482.

For a century Elmina sent Lisbon a large share of the crown’s gold. The Dutch West India Company took it in 1637, and over the next two centuries its dungeons held enslaved people waiting for the ships, who left through what visitors now call the Door of No Return. The Dutch handed the castle to Britain in 1872; it is now a UNESCO World Heritage site and museum.
story.zh:
自1471年起，葡萄牙商人就在这段海岸收购黄金。为阻止卡斯蒂利亚等对手染指，国王若昂二世于1481年12月派迪奥戈·德·阿赞布雅率约十二艘船出发（一说九艘卡拉维尔帆船和两艘运输船），载有约六百名士兵和工匠以及预先切割的石料、石灰和木材，即迅速建起要塞所需的一切。

据葡萄牙编年史家鲁伊·德·皮纳记载，当地统治者（葡萄牙人称之为卡拉曼萨）以隆重礼仪接待阿赞布雅，但告诫说，偶尔相见的朋友比做邻居的朋友交情更长久。石匠开采一块当地人视为神圣的岩石时爆发冲突，最后以馈赠平息。1482年1月，城墙在约三周内建成。

一个世纪里，埃尔米纳为里斯本输送了王室黄金的很大一部分。1637年荷兰西印度公司夺取城堡，此后两个世纪，其地牢关押着等待运奴船的被奴役者，他们从今人所说的“不归之门”离开。1872年荷兰将城堡移交英国，如今它是联合国教科文组织世界遗产和博物馆。

name.en: King Nzinga a Nkuwu of Kongo is baptised
name.zh: 刚果国王恩津加·恩库武受洗

summary.en: A Portuguese embassy with priests and masons reached Mbanza Kongo, and the manikongo Nzinga a Nkuwu was baptised as João I. His son Afonso, baptised at the same time, would make Catholicism the religion of the Kongo court and state.
summary.zh: 一支带有教士和石匠的葡萄牙使团抵达姆班扎刚果，刚果国王恩津加·恩库武受洗，教名若昂一世。同时受洗的儿子阿方索后来使天主教成为刚果宫廷和国家的宗教。

sources.title: John K. Thornton, A History of West Central Africa to 1850 (2020)
Anne Hilton, The Kingdom of Kongo (1985)
Britannica: Kongo kingdom
Wikipedia: João I of Kongo

note: Nzinga a Nkuwu later drifted away from the new faith; Afonso became its champion.

name.zh: 阿尔梅达洗劫基卢瓦与蒙巴萨

summary.en: On his way to become the first viceroy of Portuguese India, Francisco de Almeida took Kilwa in July 1505, installed a puppet sultan and began a fort, then stormed and burned Mombasa in August. The attacks broke Kilwa’s control of the Sofala gold trade and opened a century of Portuguese domination of the Swahili coast.
summary.zh: 弗朗西斯科·德·阿尔梅达在前往出任葡属印度首任总督的途中，于1505年7月攻占基卢瓦，扶植傀儡苏丹并开始修筑要塞，8月又攻破并焚烧蒙巴萨。这些袭击打破了基卢瓦对索法拉黄金贸易的控制，开启了葡萄牙主宰斯瓦希里海岸的一个世纪。

label.zh: 攻占基卢瓦（7月24日）
攻破并焚烧蒙巴萨（8月）

label.en: Fleet sails past Malindi, Portugal’s ally
label.zh: 舰队经过葡萄牙盟友马林迪
抵达印度安吉迪瓦岛

sources.title: Hans Mayr’s account of the voyage of Francisco de Almeida (1505), in G. S. P. Freeman-Grenville, The East African Coast: Select Documents (1962)
Mark Horton and John Middleton, The Swahili (2000)
Wikipedia: Francisco de Almeida

story.en:
Francisco de Almeida sailed from Lisbon in March 1505 with more than twenty ships and orders to secure the East African ports for Portugal’s new sea route. A German on board, Hans Mayr, wrote one of the few eyewitness accounts. At Kilwa, he reports, the sultan stalled for time and then fled; the Portuguese plundered the city, crowned a rival as sultan under Portuguese protection and began building a fort.

Mombasa resisted. Its people had heard what had happened at Kilwa, and they fought from the streets and rooftops. The Portuguese set the town on fire and took it house by house. Mayr estimates some 1,500 dead in the streets and houses, mentions many prisoners, women and children among them, and describes the loot loaded onto the ships.

The raids did not bring Portugal the gold of Zimbabwe it hoped for: traders simply moved to other routes. But they ended Kilwa’s greatness, and Mombasa remained hostile for most of the century, until the Portuguese built Fort Jesus there in 1593.
story.zh:
1505年3月，弗朗西斯科·德·阿尔梅达率二十余艘船从里斯本出发，奉命为葡萄牙新开辟的海路控制东非港口。船上的德国人汉斯·迈尔留下了为数不多的亲历记述。他说，在基卢瓦，苏丹先是拖延，随后出逃；葡萄牙人洗劫城市，在葡萄牙保护下立其对手为苏丹，并动工修建要塞。

蒙巴萨进行了抵抗。居民已听说基卢瓦的遭遇，在街巷和屋顶上奋战。葡萄牙人纵火焚城，逐屋攻占。迈尔估计街巷和房屋中约有一千五百人死亡，提到大批俘虏，其中有妇女和儿童，并描述了装上船的战利品。

这些袭击并未给葡萄牙带来期望中的津巴布韦黄金：商人们只是改走其他路线。但它们终结了基卢瓦的辉煌，而蒙巴萨在这个世纪的大部分时间里一直与葡萄牙为敌，直到1593年葡萄牙人在那里修建耶稣堡。

name.en: Afonso I of Kongo protests the slave trade to Portugal
name.zh: 刚果国王阿方索一世向葡萄牙抗议奴隶贸易

summary.en: In letters to King João III, Afonso I complained that Portuguese merchants were seizing free Kongolese, even nobles and his own kin, and selling them as slaves. He set up a royal committee to inspect every captive sold to the Portuguese. The letters are among the earliest African-authored documents on the Atlantic slave trade.
summary.zh: 阿方索一世在致国王若昂三世的信中抱怨，葡萄牙商人掳掠自由的刚果人，甚至贵族和他的亲属，把他们当作奴隶出售。他设立王室委员会检查每一名卖给葡萄牙人的俘虏。这些信件是非洲人撰写的关于大西洋奴隶贸易的最早文献之一。

sources.title: António Brásio (ed.), Monumenta Missionaria Africana, vol. 1 (1952): letters of Afonso I, 6 July and 18 October 1526
John K. Thornton, “Afonso I Mvemba a Nzinga, King of Kongo”, in Africa and the West: A Documentary History (2010)
Britannica: Afonso I
Wikipedia: Afonso I of Kongo

note: Afonso did not oppose slavery or the sale of war captives as such; he objected to the unregulated kidnapping of free subjects.

story.en:
Afonso Mvemba a Nzinga had ruled Kongo for about two decades when he dictated the letters of 1526. He was a committed Catholic who read Portuguese, built churches and sent his son Henrique to Lisbon, where he became the first bishop from sub-Saharan Africa. He wanted priests, teachers, physicians and ships from Portugal. What he got, he complained, were merchants.

In the letter of 6 July 1526 Afonso tells João III that traders were spreading through the country, tempting his vassals with goods and seizing free people, including noblemen’s sons and members of his own family, and selling them. The kingdom, he warns, was being depopulated, and he asked the king to send no more merchants or goods, only priests and teachers.

He could not stop the trade, which brought his own nobility wealth too. Instead he created a committee of three officials to certify that every captive offered for sale had been lawfully enslaved. The letters show an African king trying, and failing, to control the Atlantic trade on his own terms at its very beginning.
story.zh:
1526年口述这些信件时，阿方索·姆文巴·恩津加已统治刚果约二十年。他是虔诚的天主教徒，能读葡萄牙文，修建教堂，并把儿子恩里克送到里斯本，恩里克后来成为撒哈拉以南非洲第一位主教。他希望从葡萄牙得到教士、教师、医生和船只，可他抱怨说，来的却是商人。

在1526年7月6日的信中，阿方索告诉若昂三世，商人散布全国，用货物诱惑他的封臣，掳走自由人，包括贵族子弟和他自己的家人，然后卖掉。他警告说王国正在人口流失，请求国王不要再派商人和货物，只派教士和教师。

他无法阻止这项贸易，因为他自己的贵族也从中获利。于是他设立由三名官员组成的委员会，核验每名出售的俘虏是否被合法奴役。这些信件表明，在大西洋贸易刚刚兴起之时，一位非洲国王曾试图按自己的条件加以控制，却未能成功。

name.en: Omani siege of Fort Jesus, Mombasa
name.zh: 阿曼人围攻蒙巴萨耶稣堡

summary.en: An Omani army besieged the Portuguese in Fort Jesus for 33 months, from March 1696 to December 1698. Plague and hunger killed most of the defenders before the fort fell, ending Portuguese power north of Mozambique and opening the era of Omani rule on the Swahili coast.
summary.zh: 阿曼军队从1696年3月到1698年12月围困耶稣堡中的葡萄牙人长达33个月。瘟疫和饥饿使大部分守军死亡，要塞最终陷落，葡萄牙在莫桑比克以北的势力就此终结，斯瓦希里海岸进入阿曼统治时代。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Fort Jesus, Mombasa
James Kirkman, Fort Jesus: A Portuguese Fortress on the East African Coast (1974)
C. R. Boxer and Carlos de Azevedo, Fort Jesus and the Portuguese in Mombasa, 1593–1729 (1960)
Wikipedia: Siege of Fort Jesus

story.en:
Fort Jesus was designed by the Milanese architect Giovanni Battista Cairati and begun in 1593, an Italian Renaissance fortress laid out roughly like a human body seen from above, with bastions for head, arms and legs. It was meant to guard the coast against the Ottomans. Its real enemy turned out to be Oman, whose Yaʿrubi imams had expelled the Portuguese from Muscat in 1650 and now carried the war to Africa.

The Omanis arrived in March 1696. Inside were the small Portuguese garrison, and loyal Swahili families from Mombasa and the neighbouring towns. Plague broke out. Relief fleets from Goa came twice and were too small. By December 1698, according to the Portuguese accounts, the garrison had shrunk to its captain, nine soldiers and a priest, and the Omanis scaled the walls on the night of 12–13 December. A relief fleet from Goa arrived a week later to find the fort lost.

The fall made Oman the master of the coast from Mombasa to Kilwa. The Portuguese briefly retook the fort in 1728–29. Today it is a museum, where graffiti scratched into the plaster by soldiers of every side can still be seen.
story.zh:
耶稣堡由米兰建筑师乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·凯拉蒂设计，1593年动工，是一座意大利文艺复兴式要塞，俯瞰大致呈人体形状，棱堡构成头、手臂和双腿。它原为防御奥斯曼人而建，真正的敌人却是阿曼：亚里巴王朝的伊玛目于1650年把葡萄牙人逐出马斯喀特，此时又把战火引向非洲。

阿曼人于1696年3月到来。堡内有人数不多的葡萄牙守军，以及来自蒙巴萨和邻近城镇的效忠斯瓦希里家族。瘟疫爆发。果阿的援军两度到来，但兵力太少。据葡萄牙方面记载，到1698年12月，守军只剩下指挥官、九名士兵和一名神父；12月12日至13日夜间，阿曼人攀上城墙。一周后果阿的援军赶到，要塞已经失守。

要塞陷落使阿曼成为从蒙巴萨到基卢瓦海岸的主人。葡萄牙人在1728至1729年曾短暂夺回。如今这里是博物馆，各方士兵刻在灰泥上的涂鸦依然可见。

summary.en: Sent by her brother Ngola Mbandi to negotiate with the Portuguese governor João Correia de Sousa, Njinga secured a peace treaty, refused to accept vassal status for Ndongo and was baptised Ana de Sousa. Later accounts say that, offered no chair, she sat on the back of a kneeling attendant.
summary.zh: 恩津加受兄长恩戈拉·姆班迪派遣与葡萄牙总督若昂·科雷亚·德·索萨谈判，订立和约，拒绝让恩东戈成为附庸，并受洗，教名安娜·德·索萨。后世记载称，对方未给她设座，她便坐在一名跪伏侍从的背上。

sources.title: Linda M. Heywood, Njinga of Angola: Africa’s Warrior Queen (2017)
Antonio Cavazzi da Montecuccolo, Istorica descrizione de’ tre regni Congo, Matamba et Angola (1687)
Wikipedia: Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba

note: The chair anecdote first appears in later 17th-century accounts (Cavazzi, Cadornega) and may be embellished.

name.en: Moulay Ismail makes Meknes his imperial capital
name.zh: 穆莱·伊斯梅尔以梅克内斯为帝都

summary.en: The Alaouite sultan Moulay Ismail, who reigned for 55 years, made Meknes his capital and filled it with walls, gates, granaries and stables on a vast scale. He ruled through a standing army of enslaved and conscripted Black soldiers, the ʿAbid al-Bukhari, and unified Morocco more firmly than any ruler before him.
summary.zh: 在位55年的阿拉维王朝苏丹穆莱·伊斯梅尔以梅克内斯为都，大规模修建城墙、城门、粮仓和马厩。他依靠由被奴役和被征召的黑人士兵组成的常备军“布哈里奴隶军”进行统治，对摩洛哥的统一程度超过以往任何君主。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic City of Meknes
Chouki El Hamel, Black Morocco: A History of Slavery, Race, and Islam (2013)
Britannica: Ismāʿīl
Wikipedia: Ismail Ibn Sharif

note: Wikidata dates the city itself (founded in the 10th century); this record marks its elevation to capital in 1672.

story.en:
Moulay Ismail came to the throne in 1672 and chose Meknes, a modest town, over Fez and Marrakesh, whose elites he distrusted. For decades it was a building site. European captives, taken by the corsairs of Salé, worked alongside local labourers on walls that ran for some 40 kilometres, on the great gate of Bab Mansour, on granaries cooled by thick walls and on stables said to hold 12,000 horses.

His power rested on the ʿAbid al-Bukhari, a slave army created by registering Black Moroccans, free and enslaved, and swearing them on a copy of al-Bukhari’s hadith collection to serve the sultan. Chouki El Hamel shows how this forced enrolment of free Black Muslims provoked protests from the scholars of Fez. The army reached tens of thousands of men.

European visitors told stories of his cruelty and of his hundreds of children; such figures were part of his legend. He exchanged embassies with Louis XIV and took back Tangier from the English in 1684 and Larache from Spain in 1689. After his death in 1727 Morocco fell into thirty years of succession wars.
story.zh:
穆莱·伊斯梅尔于1672年即位，他不信任非斯和马拉喀什的精英，便选了一座不起眼的城镇梅克内斯为都。此后数十年这里都是一座大工地。萨莱海盗掳来的欧洲俘虏与当地劳工一起修建约40公里长的城墙、宏伟的曼苏尔门、以厚墙降温的粮仓，以及据说能容纳一万二千匹马的马厩。

他的权力依靠“布哈里奴隶军”。这支奴隶军由登记在册的摩洛哥黑人组成，无论自由人还是奴隶，都要手按布哈里的圣训集宣誓效忠苏丹。舒基·哈梅尔指出，强行征召自由的黑人穆斯林曾引起非斯学者的抗议。这支军队人数达数万。

欧洲来访者讲述他的残暴和数以百计的子女；这些数字已成为他传说的一部分。他与路易十四互派使节，1684年从英国人手中收复丹吉尔，1689年从西班牙收复拉腊什。1727年他去世后，摩洛哥陷入三十年的王位继承战争。

name.zh: 达荷美征服阿拉达与维达

summary.en: King Agaja of Dahomey took Allada in 1724 and the coastal kingdom of Hueda, with its slave port of Ouidah, in 1727. The conquest gave the inland kingdom direct access to European traders and made Ouidah one of the busiest ports of the Atlantic slave trade.
summary.zh: 达荷美国王阿加贾于1724年攻占阿拉达，1727年征服沿海王国胡埃达及其奴隶港维达。此次征服使这个内陆王国得以直接与欧洲商人交易，维达也成为大西洋奴隶贸易最繁忙的港口之一。

sources.title: Robin Law, Ouidah: The Social History of a West African Slaving “Port”, 1727–1892 (2004)
Edna G. Bay, Wives of the Leopard: Gender, Politics, and Culture in the Kingdom of Dahomey (1998)
Britannica: Agaja
Wikipedia: Agaja

story.en:
Agaja became king of Dahomey around 1718, when it was an inland kingdom on the Abomey plateau, cut off from the coast by Allada and Hueda, whose rulers grew rich as middlemen in the trade in captives. In 1724 his army overran Allada. In February 1727 it crossed into Hueda, whose king fled; the capital Savi was sacked and Ouidah, with its European forts, came under Dahomey.

Some historians have argued that Agaja wanted to end the slave trade; the evidence, Robin Law concludes, shows rather that he wanted to control it. Dahomey became one of the main suppliers of the trade for the next century and a half, and Ouidah its port.

Dahomey’s armies were famous for the corps of women soldiers whom Europeans called Amazons and Fon speakers called the agojie or mino. Their origins are debated, but by the 18th century they formed part of the palace guard. Agaja himself could not escape a stronger neighbour: the cavalry of Oyo invaded repeatedly from 1726 and forced Dahomey to pay tribute until the 1820s.
story.zh:
约1718年阿加贾成为达荷美国王时，达荷美还是阿波美高原上的内陆王国，被阿拉达和胡埃达隔绝于海岸之外，这两国的统治者充当俘虏贸易的中间商而致富。1724年，他的军队攻占阿拉达。1727年2月又攻入胡埃达，其国王出逃，都城萨维遭洗劫，设有欧洲堡垒的维达落入达荷美之手。

有史学家认为阿加贾想终止奴隶贸易；罗宾·劳的结论是，证据显示他更想控制这项贸易。此后一个半世纪，达荷美成为奴隶贸易的主要供应者之一，维达则是其港口。

达荷美军队以女兵队闻名，欧洲人称之为“亚马孙女战士”，丰语称为“阿戈杰”或“米诺”。其起源尚有争议，但到18世纪她们已是宫廷卫队的一部分。阿加贾自己也难敌更强的邻国：奥约骑兵自1726年起屡次入侵，迫使达荷美纳贡直至1820年代。

name.en: Zemene Mesafint, the Era of the Princes
name.zh: 王子时代（扎梅内·梅萨芬特）

summary.en: After the warlord Ras Mikael Sehul had Emperor Iyoas killed in 1769, real power in Ethiopia passed to regional lords, above all the Yejju Oromo dynasty of regents at Debre Tabor, while emperors in Gondar became puppets. The era ended when Kassa Hailu crowned himself Tewodros II in 1855.
summary.zh: 1769年军阀米卡埃尔·塞胡尔公爵杀死皇帝伊约阿斯后，埃塞俄比亚的实权落入地方领主手中，尤其是驻德卜雷塔博尔的耶久奥罗莫摄政家族，贡德尔的皇帝沦为傀儡。1855年卡萨·海卢自加冕为特沃德罗斯二世，这一时代告终。

sources.title: Shiferaw Bekele, “The Chronicle of Täklä Giyorgis I (1779–1800)” and studies of the Zemene Mesafint
Bahru Zewde, A History of Modern Ethiopia, 1855–1991 (2nd ed., 2001)
Britannica: Ethiopia: The Zemene Mesafint
Wikipedia: Zemene Mesafint

story.en:
The name comes from the Book of Judges: “In those days there was no king in Israel, and every man did what was right in his own eyes.” Ethiopian chroniclers applied it to the decades after 1769, when the governor of Tigray, Ras Mikael Sehul, had the young emperor Iyoas strangled and set up a puppet in his place.

From then on emperors were made and unmade by regional lords. One of them, Tekle Giyorgis I, was deposed and restored so many times that he was nicknamed “the end of the government”. The most lasting power belonged to the Yejju Oromo family of Ras Ali I, which ruled central Ethiopia as regents from Debre Tabor.

It was a time of civil war but also of church learning and of strong regional states such as Shewa and Tigray. It ended when Kassa Hailu, a frontier chief from Qwara, defeated the regents and the lords of Gojjam and Tigray one after another and was crowned Tewodros II in 1855, determined to rebuild a united empire.
story.zh:
这个名称出自《士师记》：“那时以色列中没有王，各人任意而行。”埃塞俄比亚编年史家用它来指1769年以后的几十年：那一年提格雷总督米卡埃尔·塞胡尔公爵下令勒死年轻的皇帝伊约阿斯，另立傀儡。

从此皇帝由地方领主立废。其中一位特克勒·吉约吉斯一世被废黜又复位多次，人称“政权的终结”。最持久的势力属于耶久奥罗莫人阿里一世公爵的家族，他们以摄政身份从德卜雷塔博尔统治埃塞俄比亚中部。

这是内战频仍的时代，也是教会学术繁荣、绍阿和提格雷等地方强国兴起的时代。来自夸拉的边地首领卡萨·海卢先后击败摄政和戈贾姆、提格雷的领主，于1855年加冕为特沃德罗斯二世，决心重建统一的帝国，这一时代遂告结束。

summary.en: French soldiers rebuilding a fort near Rashid (Rosetta) in the Nile Delta found a broken stela of 196 BCE inscribed with the same decree in hieroglyphic, Demotic and Greek. Surrendered to Britain in 1801, it gave Jean-François Champollion the key to deciphering hieroglyphs in 1822.
summary.zh: 在尼罗河三角洲拉希德（罗塞塔）附近重建堡垒的法国士兵发现了一块公元前196年的残碑，上面以圣书体、世俗体和希腊文刻着同一道诏令。它于1801年被移交英国，并为让-弗朗索瓦·商博良在1822年破译象形文字提供了钥匙。

sources.title: British Museum: The Rosetta Stone (EA 24)
Richard Parkinson, Cracking Codes: The Rosetta Stone and Decipherment (1999)
Jean-François Champollion, Lettre à M. Dacier (1822)
Wikipedia: Rosetta Stone

note: Wikidata dates the object itself (196 BCE); this record marks its discovery in July 1799.

story.en:
In July 1799, during Napoleon’s occupation of Egypt, soldiers strengthening an old fort near the port of Rashid, which Europeans called Rosetta, pulled out a slab of dark granodiorite with three bands of writing. The officer in charge, Pierre-François Bouchard, saw that the bottom band was Greek and realised the stone might hold a translation of the hieroglyphs above. The scholars Napoleon had brought to Egypt made ink copies and casts.

When the French army surrendered in 1801, the treaty handed the stone to Britain, and it has been in the British Museum since 1802. The Greek text turned out to be a decree of 196 BCE honouring the young Ptolemy V.

The Englishman Thomas Young identified several signs, but the breakthrough came from Jean-François Champollion, who knew Coptic, the last stage of the Egyptian language. In September 1822 he showed that hieroglyphs combined sound signs with signs for ideas. According to a family story, Champollion ran into his brother’s office shouting “Je tiens l’affaire!” (“I’ve got it!”) and fainted. Egypt has repeatedly asked for the stone’s return.
story.zh:
1799年7月，拿破仑占领埃及期间，士兵在拉希德港（欧洲人称罗塞塔）附近加固一座旧堡垒时，挖出一块刻有三段文字的深色花岗闪长岩石板。负责的军官皮埃尔-弗朗索瓦·布沙尔看出最下面一段是希腊文，意识到这块石碑可能刻有上方象形文字的译文。拿破仑带到埃及的学者们制作了墨拓和模型。

1801年法军投降时，条约把石碑交给英国，自1802年起它一直存放在大英博物馆。希腊文原来是公元前196年表彰年幼的托勒密五世的一道诏令。

英国人托马斯·杨辨认出若干符号，但真正的突破来自通晓埃及语最后阶段科普特语的让-弗朗索瓦·商博良。1822年9月，他证明象形文字结合了表音符号和表意符号。据家族流传的说法，商博良冲进哥哥的办公室高喊“我搞定了！”随即晕倒。埃及多次要求归还石碑。

name.en: Sayyid Said moves his court to Zanzibar
name.zh: 赛义德·赛义德迁都桑给巴尔

summary.en: Sayyid Said bin Sultan, ruler of Oman, made Zanzibar his main residence and capital. Clove plantations worked by enslaved Africans and caravans to the Great Lakes for ivory and captives turned the island into the commercial centre of East Africa; on his death in 1856 Zanzibar became a separate sultanate.
summary.zh: 阿曼统治者赛义德·赛义德·本·苏丹把桑给巴尔作为主要驻地和首都。由被奴役非洲人耕作的丁香种植园，以及前往大湖地区获取象牙和俘虏的商队，使该岛成为东非的商业中心；1856年他去世后，桑给巴尔成为独立的苏丹国。

sources.title: Abdul Sheriff, Slaves, Spices and Ivory in Zanzibar (1987)
Britannica: Saʿīd ibn Sulṭān
Wikipedia: Said bin Sultan

note: Sayyid Said spent long periods in Zanzibar from 1828; the transfer of the court is usually dated 1832 or 1840.

summary.en: Settlers of the American Colonization Society’s colony, formerly enslaved and free Black Americans, adopted a declaration of independence and a constitution modelled on that of the United States. Joseph Jenkins Roberts became the first president of Africa’s first modern republic.
summary.zh: 美国殖民协会所建殖民地的定居者（曾受奴役和自由的美国黑人）通过了独立宣言和仿照美国宪法的宪法。约瑟夫·詹金斯·罗伯茨成为非洲第一个近代共和国的首任总统。

sources.title: Amos J. Beyan, African American Settlements in West Africa: John Brown Russwurm and the American Civilizing Efforts (2005)
Britannica: Liberia: History
Wikipedia: Liberian Declaration of Independence

story.en:
The colony began in 1822 at Cape Mesurado, where agents of the American Colonization Society pressed local Dei and Bassa rulers into selling land. The society’s motives were mixed: some members opposed slavery, others simply wanted free Black people out of the United States. The settlers called their town Monrovia, after President James Monroe.

By the 1840s the colony was in trouble. British traders refused to pay customs duties to a private American society, and the United States would not take responsibility. On 26 July 1847 a convention in Monrovia declared independence. The declaration, drafted by Hilary Teague, spoke of settlers who had been “originally inhabitants of the United States” and had come to Africa to escape oppression. Britain recognised the republic in 1848; the United States only in 1862, during the Civil War.

The new state reproduced a painful hierarchy. For more than a century the Americo-Liberian minority, a few per cent of the population, monopolised power over the indigenous majority, until the coup of 1980.
story.zh:
殖民地始于1822年的梅苏拉多角，美国殖民协会的代理人迫使当地代伊人和巴萨人统治者出让土地。协会的动机复杂：有些成员反对奴隶制，有些人只是想把自由黑人迁出美国。定居者以詹姆斯·门罗总统之名把城镇命名为蒙罗维亚。

到1840年代，殖民地陷入困境。英国商人拒绝向一个美国私人协会缴纳关税，美国又不愿承担责任。1847年7月26日，蒙罗维亚的制宪会议宣布独立。由希拉里·蒂格起草的宣言说，定居者“原是美利坚合众国的居民”，为逃避压迫来到非洲。英国于1848年承认这个共和国，美国则迟至1862年南北战争期间才承认。

新国家复制了令人痛心的等级制度。一个多世纪里，仅占人口百分之几的美裔利比里亚人垄断了对本土多数民众的统治，直至1980年政变。

summary.en: To free British envoys and missionaries imprisoned by Emperor Tewodros II, General Robert Napier led some 13,000 soldiers from India across the Ethiopian highlands. His troops stormed the mountain fortress of Magdala on 13 April 1868; Tewodros shot himself, and the British carried off crown regalia and hundreds of manuscripts.
summary.zh: 为解救被皇帝特沃德罗斯二世囚禁的英国使节和传教士，罗伯特·纳皮尔将军率约一万三千名印度驻军穿越埃塞俄比亚高原。1868年4月13日部队攻陷马格达拉山地要塞，特沃德罗斯开枪自尽，英军掠走王冠礼器和数以百计的手稿。

label.en: Battle of Arogee and storming of Magdala
label.zh: 阿罗吉之战与攻陷马格达拉

sources.title: Henry M. Stanley, Coomassie and Magdala (1874)
Richard Pankhurst, “The Napier Expedition and the Loot from Maqdala”, Présence Africaine 133–134 (1985)
Britannica: Tewodros II
Wikipedia: British Expedition to Abyssinia

story.en:
Tewodros II had written to Queen Victoria in 1862 proposing an alliance against the Ottomans and Egypt. The letter was left unanswered in the Foreign Office. Feeling insulted, and angered by missionaries he suspected of spying, the emperor imprisoned the British consul Charles Cameron and, later, the envoy sent to free him.

Britain’s answer was an expensive show of logistics. Napier landed at Zula on the Red Sea with Indian and British troops, thousands of mules and camels and 44 elephants to carry the heavy guns, and built a railway and a pier. The army marched about 600 kilometres into the highlands. Many regional lords, at war with Tewodros, let it pass.

On Good Friday, 10 April 1868, Ethiopian troops charging down from Magdala were cut down at Arogee by breech-loading rifles. Tewodros released the hostages, and when the fortress was stormed three days later he shot himself, reportedly with a pistol that Victoria had once sent him as a gift. The soldiers auctioned the loot on the spot. Ethiopia has sought the return of the Maqdala treasures ever since, and a few have come home.
story.zh:
1862年，特沃德罗斯二世致信维多利亚女王，提议结盟对抗奥斯曼帝国和埃及。这封信在外交部被搁置未复。皇帝感到受辱，又怀疑传教士从事间谍活动，便囚禁了英国领事查尔斯·卡梅伦，后来又扣押了前来营救他的使节。

英国的回应是一场代价高昂的后勤展示。纳皮尔率印度和英国军队在红海边的祖拉登陆，带着数千头骡子和骆驼以及44头驮运重炮的大象，修建了铁路和码头。军队向高原挺进约600公里。许多与特沃德罗斯交战的地方领主任其通过。

1868年4月10日耶稣受难日，从马格达拉冲下山的埃塞俄比亚军队在阿罗吉被后装步枪击溃。特沃德罗斯释放了人质；三天后要塞被攻破，他开枪自尽，据说用的是维多利亚女王曾赠给他的一把手枪。士兵们当场拍卖战利品。埃塞俄比亚此后一直要求归还马格达拉宝物，已有少数回归。

summary.en: The discovery of diamonds on Colesberg Kopje in 1871 drew tens of thousands of diggers to Griqualand West and created the town of Kimberley around the mine later called the Big Hole. Britain annexed the fields, and by 1888 Cecil Rhodes had merged the claims into De Beers Consolidated Mines.
summary.zh: 1871年在科尔斯伯格小丘发现钻石，数万名采掘者涌向西格里夸兰，在后来被称为“大洞”的矿坑周围形成了金伯利镇。英国吞并了钻石矿区，到1888年塞西尔·罗得斯已把各矿权合并为戴比尔斯联合矿业公司。

sources.title: William H. Worger, South Africa’s City of Diamonds: Mine Workers and Monopoly Capitalism in Kimberley, 1867–1895 (1987)
Britannica: Kimberley
Wikipedia: Big Hole

note: Wikidata gives the mine’s working dates; the rush began in July 1871 with the “New Rush” on Colesberg Kopje.

story.en:
The first diamond, a pebble picked up by a farmer’s child near the Orange River in 1867, was a curiosity. Then in 1869 a herder sold the 83-carat “Star of South Africa”, and in July 1871 diggers found diamonds on a low hill called Colesberg Kopje. Within months the hill had vanished. In its place a pit of thousands of tiny claims, criss-crossed by ropes and buckets, sank ever deeper, and a tin-roofed town of tens of thousands grew around it.

The ground was claimed by the Griqua chief Nicolaas Waterboer and by the Boer republics, but in 1871 Britain annexed it as Griqualand West. As the pit deepened, small diggers sold out to companies, and by 1888 Cecil Rhodes, backed by the Rothschilds, had bought out his rival Barney Barnato to form De Beers.

Kimberley set the pattern of South African mining: African migrant workers on short contracts, housed in closed compounds and searched for stolen stones, and white men with capital and the vote. The Big Hole was worked by hand to a depth of about 240 metres before it closed in 1914.
story.zh:
第一颗钻石是1867年一位农民的孩子在奥兰治河边捡到的卵石，只是件新奇玩意儿。1869年，一名牧人卖出83克拉的“南非之星”；1871年7月，采掘者在一座名为科尔斯伯格小丘的矮山上发现钻石。几个月内这座山就消失了，取而代之的是一个由数千块小矿区组成、绳索与吊桶纵横交错、越挖越深的矿坑，周围冒出一座有数万人口的铁皮屋顶城镇。

格里夸首领尼古拉斯·沃特博尔和布尔共和国都声称拥有这片土地，但英国于1871年将其吞并为西格里夸兰。随着矿坑加深，小采掘者把矿权卖给公司；到1888年，得到罗斯柴尔德家族支持的塞西尔·罗得斯收购了对手巴尼·巴纳托的产业，组建戴比尔斯。

金伯利奠定了南非采矿业的模式：签短期合同的非洲流动劳工住在封闭的营地中，被搜身以防偷钻；掌握资本和选票的则是白人。“大洞”在1914年关闭前靠人力挖到约240米深。

name.en: Ottomans take Tunis and end the Hafsids
name.zh: 奥斯曼攻占突尼斯，哈夫斯王朝终结

summary.en: A great Ottoman fleet under Koca Sinan Pasha and Uluç Ali stormed the Spanish fortress of La Goulette and the citadel of Tunis in August–September 1574. The last Hafsid sultan was taken to Istanbul, and Tunisia became an Ottoman province, ending forty years of Habsburg intervention.
summary.zh: 1574年8至9月，科贾·锡南帕夏和乌卢奇·阿里率领的奥斯曼大舰队攻克西班牙的拉古莱特要塞和突尼斯城堡。末代哈夫斯苏丹被押往伊斯坦布尔，突尼斯成为奥斯曼行省，哈布斯堡王朝长达四十年的干预就此结束。

sources.title: Andrew C. Hess, The Forgotten Frontier: A History of the Sixteenth-Century Ibero-African Frontier (1978)
Britannica: Ḥafṣid dynasty
