name.en: Amara Dunqas founds the Funj sultanate of Sennar
name.zh: 阿马拉·敦卡斯建立森纳尔芬吉苏丹国

summary.en: According to Sudanese tradition, the Funj leader Amara Dunqas founded Sennar on the Blue Nile in 1504, after his people and the Arab Abdallab had destroyed Soba, capital of the last Christian Nubian kingdom of Alodia. The Funj sultanate dominated the middle Nile for three centuries.
summary.zh: 据苏丹传统，芬吉人首领阿马拉·敦卡斯于1504年在青尼罗河畔建立森纳尔，此前芬吉人与阿拉伯阿卜达拉布人摧毁了最后一个基督教努比亚王国阿洛迪亚的都城索巴。芬吉苏丹国主宰尼罗河中游达三个世纪。

sources.title: Jay Spaulding, The Heroic Age in Sinnar (1985)
P. M. Holt and M. W. Daly, A History of the Sudan (6th ed., 2011)
Britannica: Funj Sultanate
Wikipedia: Funj Sultanate

note: The date 1504 comes from the 19th-century Funj Chronicle; the fall of Soba may have been earlier and the Funj origins are debated.

summary.en: The Kano Chronicle credits Sarki Muhammad Rumfa with extending the city walls, building the Gidan Rumfa palace, founding the Kurmi market and introducing Islamic law and court ceremony. The Maghrebi scholar al-Maghili wrote a treatise on government for him.
summary.zh: 据《卡诺编年史》记载，萨尔基（国王）穆罕默德·伦法扩建城墙，修建伦法王宫，开设库尔米市场，并引入伊斯兰法和宫廷礼仪。马格里布学者马吉利为他撰写了一部论治国的著作。

name.en: Witwatersrand gold rush and the founding of Johannesburg
name.zh: 威特沃特斯兰德淘金热与约翰内斯堡的建立

summary.en: Gold-bearing reef was found on the farm Langlaagte in 1886, and the South African Republic proclaimed public diggings that September. Johannesburg grew from a mining camp to a city of about 100,000 in ten years; the reef became the world’s largest gold field and the struggle over it led to the South African War.
summary.zh: 1886年在兰拉赫特农场发现含金矿脉，南非共和国于当年9月宣布开放公共采掘区。约翰内斯堡十年间从矿营发展为约十万人口的城市；这条矿脉成为世界最大的金矿区，围绕它的争夺最终引发了南非战争。

sources.title: Charles van Onselen, New Babylon, New Nineveh: Everyday Life on the Witwatersrand, 1886–1914 (1982)
Britannica: Johannesburg
South African History Online: The discovery of gold
Wikipedia: Witwatersrand Gold Rush

story.en:
In early 1886 an Australian prospector named George Harrison, working on the farm Langlaagte, recognised gold-bearing conglomerate in an outcrop of rock. He sold his claim for a few pounds and disappeared from history. The reef he found, it turned out, ran underground for scores of kilometres. In September the government of Paul Kruger’s South African Republic declared the area public diggings, and a triangle of unclaimed land between farms was laid out as Johannesburg.

The gold was plentiful but low-grade and deep, so it could be mined only by big companies with capital, much of it from Kimberley’s diamond magnates, and by huge numbers of cheap workers. African men from across southern Africa came on contracts and lived in compounds; by 1899 about 100,000 worked the mines. White immigrants, the Uitlanders, soon outnumbered the Boer citizens of the republic, who denied them the vote.

That quarrel, and British determination to control the richest gold field on earth, led to the Jameson Raid of 1895 and the war of 1899. Johannesburg, Egoli to its African residents, “the place of gold”, became the economic heart of the continent.
story.zh:
1886年初，在兰拉赫特农场干活的澳大利亚探矿者乔治·哈里森在一处露头岩石中认出了含金砾岩。他以几英镑卖掉矿权，从此消失于历史。后来发现，他找到的矿脉在地下绵延数十公里。当年9月，保罗·克留格尔领导的南非共和国政府宣布该地区为公共采掘区，几座农场之间一块无人认领的三角形土地被规划为约翰内斯堡。

这里的黄金储量丰富但品位低、埋藏深，只有拥有资本的大公司（其中许多资本来自金伯利的钻石巨头）雇用大量廉价劳工才能开采。来自南部非洲各地的非洲男子签约而来，住在封闭营地；到1899年约有十万人在矿上劳作。白人移民即“外侨”的人数很快超过了共和国的布尔公民，后者却拒绝给他们投票权。

这一争端，加上英国控制世界最富金矿的决心，导致了1895年的詹姆森袭击和1899年的战争。约翰内斯堡，非洲居民口中的“伊戈利”（黄金之地），成为非洲大陆的经济心脏。

name.en: Atrocities in the Congo Free State

summary.en: In the Congo Free State, the personal possession of King Leopold II of Belgium, the forced collection of wild rubber was enforced by hostage-taking, flogging, mutilation and killing. International protest, led by E. D. Morel and Roger Casement, forced Belgium to annex the territory in 1908. The death toll is unknown but ran into the millions by most estimates.
summary.zh: 在比利时国王利奥波德二世的私人领地刚果自由邦，强制采集野生橡胶以扣押人质、鞭打、断肢和杀戮来推行。在埃德蒙·莫雷尔和罗杰·凯斯门特领导的国际抗议下，比利时于1908年被迫接管该地。死亡人数无从确知，但多数估计达数百万。

sources.title: Roger Casement, Report on the Administration of the Congo Free State (1904)
Adam Hochschild, King Leopold’s Ghost (1998)
Jean-Luc Vellut, “La violence armée dans l’État indépendant du Congo”, Cultures et développement 16 (1984)
Britannica: Congo Free State
Wikipedia: Atrocities in the Congo Free State

note: No census was taken; estimates of population loss range from about one million to ten million and are disputed. The marker is Coquilhatville (Mbandaka), centre of the Équateur rubber district.

story.en:
At the Berlin Conference of 1884–85 the powers recognised a vast territory in the Congo basin as the property not of Belgium but of its king, Leopold II, who promised free trade and the suppression of the slave trade. When the bicycle and the motor car created a world market for rubber in the 1890s, the Free State and its concession companies turned to the wild rubber vines of the rainforest.

Villages were given quotas. Soldiers of the Force Publique held women and children hostage until the men brought in rubber, and they were required to account for their cartridges, sometimes with severed hands. In May 1904, at Baringa, the missionary Alice Seeley Harris photographed a man named Nsala looking at the hand and foot of his five-year-old daughter, killed by company sentries. Such photographs, shown in lantern lectures across Britain and the United States, made the Congo one of the first great international human-rights campaigns.

The British consul Roger Casement’s report of 1904 confirmed the missionaries’ accounts. Belgium took over the colony in 1908, and Leopold burned the Free State’s archives before handing it over.
story.zh:
在1884至1885年的柏林会议上，列强承认刚果盆地一大片土地不属于比利时，而属于其国王利奥波德二世个人，他承诺实行自由贸易并镇压奴隶贸易。1890年代自行车和汽车创造了橡胶的世界市场，自由邦及其特许公司便把目光投向雨林中的野生橡胶藤。

各村被分派定额。公安军士兵扣押妇女儿童作为人质，直到男人交来橡胶；他们还须为消耗的子弹交代用途，有时以砍下的手作为凭证。1904年5月，传教士爱丽丝·西利·哈里斯在巴林加拍下一张照片：名叫恩萨拉的男子凝视着他五岁女儿的一只手和一只脚，女孩被公司哨兵杀害。这些照片在英美各地的幻灯演讲中展出，使刚果问题成为最早的大规模国际人权运动之一。

英国领事罗杰·凯斯门特1904年的报告证实了传教士的叙述。比利时于1908年接管该殖民地，利奥波德在移交前烧毁了自由邦的档案。

summary.en: After an unauthorised British party led by James Phillips was ambushed on its way to Benin City in January 1897, a punitive force under Admiral Harry Rawson captured and burned the city in February. Oba Ovonramwen was exiled, and thousands of brass plaques, ivories and sculptures, the Benin Bronzes, were looted and sold to museums worldwide.
summary.zh: 1897年1月，詹姆斯·菲利普斯率领、未获批准前往贝宁城的英国队伍遭伏击后，哈里·罗森海军上将指挥的惩罚性部队于2月攻占并焚烧了该城。奥巴奥文拉姆文被流放，数以千计的黄铜饰板、象牙雕刻和雕塑，即“贝宁青铜器”，被掠走并卖给世界各地的博物馆。

sources.title: Dan Hicks, The Brutish Museums: The Benin Bronzes, Colonial Violence and Cultural Restitution (2020)
Barnaby Phillips, Loot: Britain and the Benin Bronzes (2021)
Britannica: Benin Bronzes
Wikipedia: Benin Expedition of 1897

story.en:
In January 1897 the acting consul-general James Phillips set out for Benin City with a small party and porters, intending to see the Oba during the Ague festival, when no foreigners were to be received. Commanders of the Oba ambushed the column; Phillips and most of the British were killed. Within weeks the Admiralty had assembled about 1,200 marines and sailors.

The force fought its way through the forest and entered the city on 18 February 1897. Three days later a fire swept through it, destroying the palace. Officers and men collected the contents of the royal compound: more than 900 cast plaques that had once covered the palace pillars, recording centuries of court history, commemorative heads, carved tusks and coral regalia. Many were sold in London to pay for the expedition. Oba Ovonramwen surrendered in August and was exiled to Calabar, where he died in 1914.

The Benin Bronzes are now scattered across more than 150 museums. Since 2021 Germany, the Smithsonian, several British universities and others have returned objects or transferred ownership to Nigeria.
story.zh:
1897年1月，代理总领事詹姆斯·菲利普斯带着一小队人和挑夫前往贝宁城，打算在阿圭节期间觐见奥巴，而节期内按规矩不接待外人。奥巴的将领伏击了这支队伍，菲利普斯和大部分英国人被杀。几周之内，海军部集结了约一千二百名海军陆战队员和水兵。

部队在森林中一路激战，于1897年2月18日进城。三天后一场大火席卷全城，烧毁王宫。军官和士兵搜罗了王宫的藏品：九百多块曾覆盖宫殿柱子、记录数百年宫廷历史的铸造饰板，纪念头像、雕花象牙和珊瑚礼器。许多在伦敦被拍卖以支付远征费用。奥巴奥文拉姆文于8月投降，被流放到卡拉巴尔，1914年死于该地。

贝宁青铜器如今散布在一百五十多家博物馆。自2021年起，德国、史密森学会、多所英国大学等已向尼日利亚归还文物或移交所有权。

summary.en: A French expeditionary force landed at Mahajanga in 1895 and marched on Antananarivo, losing thousands of men to malaria and dysentery but only about two dozen in battle. The capital surrendered after a brief bombardment on 30 September 1895; France annexed the island in 1896 and abolished the Merina monarchy in 1897.
summary.zh: 1895年法国远征军在马哈赞加登陆，向塔那那利佛进军，途中数千人死于疟疾和痢疾，阵亡者仅二十余人。经短暂炮击后，首都于1895年9月30日投降；法国于1896年吞并该岛，1897年废除梅里纳君主制。

note: The QID is the second Madagascar expedition (1894–95); this record also covers the annexation of 1896 and the abolition of the monarchy in 1897, hence the end year.

story.en:
The Merina kingdom had Protestant churches, schools, a printing press and an army trained by British officers, and its prime minister Rainilaiarivony, married in turn to three queens, had kept the French at bay since the war of 1883–85. In 1894 France demanded a full protectorate. When the government in Antananarivo refused, Paris sent about 15,000 soldiers and many thousands of porters.

The expedition became a byword for military disaster. The army had to build a road through swamp and forest from the coast, and fever cut it down: some 6,000 men died of disease, while only about twenty to twenty-five were killed in fighting. In September General Duchesne sent a flying column ahead, and after a few shells landed near the queen’s palace, Ranavalona III raised a white flag.

Resistance did not end. The menalamba, “red shawl” rebels, rose in 1895–96 against both the French and the Christian court. The governor Joseph Gallieni answered with martial law, abolished the monarchy in February 1897, executed ministers and sent the queen into exile.
story.zh:
梅里纳王国拥有新教教堂、学校、印刷所和由英国军官训练的军队；先后娶了三位女王的首相拉尼莱亚里沃尼自1883至1885年战争以来一直抵挡着法国人。1894年法国要求建立完全的保护国。塔那那利佛政府拒绝后，巴黎派出约一万五千名士兵和数千名挑夫。

这次远征成了军事灾难的代名词。部队不得不从海岸穿过沼泽和森林修筑道路，热病使其减员严重：约六千人病死，战死者只有二十余人。9月，杜歇纳将军派出一支快速纵队先行，几发炮弹落在女王宫附近后，拉纳瓦洛娜三世升起白旗。

抵抗并未结束。“红披肩”起义者在1895至1896年间起事，同时反对法国人和信奉基督教的宫廷。总督约瑟夫·加利埃尼以戒严回应，于1897年2月废除君主制，处决大臣，并将女王流放。

summary.en: When Khalid bin Barghash seized the throne of Zanzibar without British approval, Royal Navy ships bombarded the palace on 27 August 1896. The war lasted under an hour, often cited as the shortest in recorded history; about 500 defenders were killed or wounded, and a British-backed sultan was installed.
summary.zh: 哈立德·本·巴尔加什未经英国同意夺取桑给巴尔王位后，英国皇家海军舰船于1896年8月27日炮轰王宫。战争持续不到一小时，常被称为有史以来最短的战争；约五百名守军死伤，英国扶植的苏丹随即登基。

sources.title: Kevin Patience, Zanzibar and the Shortest War in History (1994)
Britannica: Zanzibar: History
Wikipedia: Anglo-Zanzibar War

note: Accounts give the duration as 38 to 45 minutes.

summary.en: Herbert Kitchener’s Anglo-Egyptian army, armed with Maxim guns, artillery and gunboats, destroyed the army of the Khalifa ʿAbdallahi outside Omdurman. About 11,000 Mahdist soldiers were killed against fewer than 50 on Kitchener’s side, and the Mahdist state collapsed.
summary.zh: 赫伯特·基钦纳率领装备马克沁机枪、火炮和炮艇的英埃联军在恩图曼城外歼灭哈里发阿卜杜拉希的军队。马赫迪军约一万一千人阵亡，基钦纳一方阵亡不到五十人，马赫迪国随之崩溃。

sources.title: Winston S. Churchill, The River War (1899)
P. M. Holt, The Mahdist State in the Sudan, 1881–1898 (2nd ed., 1970)
Britannica: Battle of Omdurman
Wikipedia: Battle of Omdurman

story.en:
Kitchener’s campaign up the Nile took two years and was built on a railway laid straight across the Nubian desert from Wadi Halfa. By the end of August 1898 his 25,000 British, Egyptian and Sudanese troops were camped on the river at Karari, north of Omdurman, with gunboats offshore.

At dawn on 2 September the Khalifa ʿAbdallahi sent some 50,000 men across the open plain in waves. Most never got within a few hundred metres of the British lines; machine guns, magazine rifles and shellfire cut them down. Later in the morning a charge by the 21st Lancers, in which the young Winston Churchill rode, ran into a hidden force of Mahdist warriors in a dry watercourse and was one of the few moments of hand-to-hand fighting.

Kitchener entered Omdurman that afternoon. He had the Mahdi’s tomb destroyed and his bones thrown into the Nile, which caused outrage even in Britain. The Khalifa escaped and was killed in 1899. Sudan became an Anglo-Egyptian condominium, ruled in practice by Britain until 1956.
story.zh:
基钦纳沿尼罗河而上的战役历时两年，依靠一条从瓦迪哈勒法笔直穿越努比亚沙漠的铁路。到1898年8月底，他的两万五千名英国、埃及和苏丹士兵在恩图曼以北的卡拉里河边扎营，炮艇停泊河上。

9月2日黎明，哈里发阿卜杜拉希派出约五万人分波次穿越开阔平原冲锋。大多数人在离英军阵线几百米处就被机枪、弹匣步枪和炮火击倒。上午晚些时候，年轻的温斯顿·丘吉尔所在的第21枪骑兵团发起冲锋，撞上埋伏在干河床中的马赫迪战士，这是少有的白刃战时刻之一。

当天下午基钦纳进入恩图曼。他下令摧毁马赫迪陵墓，把遗骨抛入尼罗河，此举甚至在英国国内也激起愤慨。哈里发逃脱，1899年被杀。苏丹成为英埃共管地，实际由英国统治至1956年。

summary.en: A small French expedition under Captain Jean-Baptiste Marchand reached Fashoda on the White Nile after a two-year march from the Atlantic, hoping to secure a French belt across Africa. Kitchener arrived with a far larger force in September; after weeks of crisis France backed down in November, and Britain kept the Nile valley.
summary.zh: 让-巴蒂斯特·马尔尚上尉率领的法国小分队从大西洋岸跋涉两年抵达白尼罗河畔的法绍达，希望建立横贯非洲的法国地带。9月基钦纳率更大兵力到达；经过数周危机，法国于11月让步，英国保住了尼罗河流域。

sources.title: David Levering Lewis, The Race to Fashoda (1987)
Britannica: Fashoda Incident
Wikipedia: Fashoda Incident

story.en:
Marchand left the Congo coast in 1896 with a few French officers and about 150 Senegalese riflemen, hauling a dismantled steamer, the Faidherbe, through the forests and swamps of central Africa. On 10 July 1898 they raised the tricolour over the ruined Egyptian fort at Fashoda. Paris hoped that a French presence on the upper Nile would force Britain to reopen the Egyptian question.

Two months later Kitchener steamed upriver from Omdurman with gunboats and some 1,500 men. The two commanders met politely; Kitchener, in Egyptian uniform, flew the Egyptian flag beside the British one and pointed out that he could not let the French stay. For weeks the newspapers of London and Paris talked of war.

France, divided by the Dreyfus affair and outgunned at sea, gave way. Marchand withdrew in December. The humiliation turned French policy toward an understanding with Britain: Egypt for Britain, Morocco for France, sealed in the Entente Cordiale of 1904. Fashoda itself was renamed Kodok in 1904 to erase the memory.
story.zh:
1896年，马尔尚带着几名法国军官和约一百五十名塞内加尔步兵从刚果海岸出发，拖着一艘拆散的汽船“费代尔布号”穿越中非的森林和沼泽。1898年7月10日，他们在法绍达废弃的埃及堡垒上升起三色旗。巴黎希望法国在尼罗河上游的存在能迫使英国重新讨论埃及问题。

两个月后，基钦纳带着炮艇和约一千五百人从恩图曼溯河而上。两位指挥官彬彬有礼地会面；身着埃及军服的基钦纳把埃及旗与英国旗并排升起，并指出他不能容许法国人留下。数周之内，伦敦和巴黎的报纸都在谈论战争。

因德雷福斯事件而分裂、海上又处于劣势的法国让步了。马尔尚于12月撤离。这次屈辱使法国政策转向与英国和解：埃及归英国，摩洛哥归法国，由1904年的英法协约确认。法绍达本身在1904年被改名为科多克，以抹去这段记忆。

summary.en: Chiefs, lawyers, clergy and teachers from across South Africa met in Bloemfontein and founded the South African Native National Congress to defend African rights in the new, white-ruled Union. John Dube became its first president and Sol Plaatje its secretary; it was renamed the African National Congress in 1923.
summary.zh: 来自南非各地的酋长、律师、神职人员和教师在布隆方丹集会，成立南非土著国民大会，在白人统治的新南非联邦中捍卫非洲人的权利。约翰·杜比任首任主席，索尔·普拉杰任书记；1923年更名为非洲人国民大会。

sources.title: Peter Walshe, The Rise of African Nationalism in South Africa: The African National Congress 1912–1952 (1970)
South African History Online: The founding of the ANC
Britannica: African National Congress
Wikipedia: African National Congress

story.en:
The Union of South Africa, formed in 1910, gave the vote almost entirely to white men. Pixley ka Isaka Seme, a young lawyer educated at Columbia and Oxford, called on Africans to set aside ethnic divisions and meet in a single national body. On 8 January 1912 delegates gathered in a hall in Bloemfontein. They opened with prayers and a hymn, and elected the educator John Dube, absent at his school in Natal, as president.

The first great test came at once. The Natives Land Act of 1913 restricted African land ownership to about 7 per cent of the country. Sol Plaatje travelled the countryside recording evicted families and wrote Native Life in South Africa; delegations went to London in 1914 and 1919 and were turned away.

For decades the Congress relied on petitions and respectable protest. In the 1940s a Youth League including Nelson Mandela, Walter Sisulu and Oliver Tambo pushed it toward mass action. Banned in 1960, it led the struggle from exile and prison, and in 1994 it won the country’s first democratic election.
story.zh:
1910年成立的南非联邦几乎只把选举权给了白人男子。曾在哥伦比亚大学和牛津大学求学的年轻律师皮克斯利·卡·伊萨卡·塞梅号召非洲人抛开族群分歧，组成统一的全国性组织。1912年1月8日，代表们在布隆方丹的一座会堂集会，以祈祷和赞美诗开场，推选当时正在纳塔尔自己学校里的教育家约翰·杜比为主席。

第一个重大考验接踵而至。1913年的《土著土地法》把非洲人拥有土地限制在全国约百分之七的范围内。索尔·普拉杰走遍乡村记录被驱逐的家庭，写成《南非的土著生活》；代表团于1914年和1919年前往伦敦，均被拒之门外。

数十年间，大会依靠请愿和体面的抗议。1940年代，包括纳尔逊·曼德拉、沃尔特·西苏鲁和奥利弗·坦博在内的青年联盟推动它走向群众运动。1960年被取缔后，它在流亡和狱中领导斗争，并在1994年赢得南非首次民主选举。

summary.en: Rumours that women were to be taxed led tens of thousands of Igbo and Ibibio women in south-eastern Nigeria to protest against the British-appointed warrant chiefs in November–December 1929, using the custom of “sitting on a man”. Colonial troops killed more than 50 women, but the system of warrant chiefs was reformed.
summary.zh: 1929年11至12月，有关妇女将被征税的传言使尼日利亚东南部数万名伊博族和伊比比奥族妇女以“坐在男人身上”的传统方式抗议英国委任的“委任酋长”。殖民军队打死五十多名妇女，但委任酋长制度随后被改革。

sources.title: Judith Van Allen, “Aba Riots or Igbo Women’s War? Ideology, Stratification, and the Invisibility of Women”, in Women in Africa (1976)
Toyin Falola and Adam Paddock (eds.), The Women’s War of 1929: Gender and Violence in Colonial Nigeria (2011)
Britannica: Aba Women’s Riots
Wikipedia: Women's War

story.en:
The spark was a conversation in the village of Oloko in November 1929. A man counting people and livestock for the warrant chief Okugo asked a widow, Nwanyeruwa, how many goats and sheep she had. Men had been taxed since 1928, and she took the census as the first step toward taxing women. She raised the alarm, and the news spread through women’s networks across the markets of the region.

Thousands of women gathered at the compounds of warrant chiefs and colonial offices. They used a traditional sanction known as “sitting on a man”: surrounding the offender, singing mocking songs, dancing and banging on his hut until he gave in. Okugo was tried and jailed. As the protests spread to Aba, Opobo and other towns, women attacked banks and European trading stores. At Opobo in December troops fired on a crowd, and in all more than 50 women were killed.

The British called it the Aba Riots; the women called it Ogu Umunwanyi, the Women’s War. Two commissions of inquiry followed, and the warrant-chief system was abolished in favour of councils based more closely on local institutions.
story.zh:
导火索是1929年11月奥洛科村的一次谈话。一名为委任酋长奥库戈清点人口和牲畜的男子问寡妇恩瓦涅鲁瓦有几只山羊和绵羊。男人自1928年起已被征税，她认为这次普查是向妇女征税的第一步。她发出警报，消息通过妇女网络传遍该地区的各个集市。

数千名妇女聚集在委任酋长的院落和殖民官署前。她们使用一种被称为“坐在男人身上”的传统惩戒：围住冒犯者，唱嘲讽歌，跳舞，敲打他的屋子，直到他屈服。奥库戈被审判入狱。抗议蔓延到阿巴、奥波博等城镇，妇女们冲击银行和欧洲商行。12月在奥波博，军队向人群开枪，前后共有五十多名妇女遇难。

英国人称之为“阿巴骚乱”，妇女们则称之为“妇女战争”。随后两个调查委员会成立，委任酋长制度被废除，代之以更贴近地方制度的议会。

name.en: National Party victory and the start of apartheid
name.zh: 国民党胜选与种族隔离的开端

summary.en: D. F. Malan’s Herenigde Nasionale Party, allied with the Afrikaner Party, won a majority of seats though a minority of votes in an election open almost only to white South Africans. It began to build apartheid: race classification, residential segregation, separate education and the removal of Coloured voters from the common roll.
summary.zh: 在几乎只有白人能投票的选举中，丹尼尔·马兰领导的重新联合国民党与南非白人党结盟，以少数选票赢得多数议席，随即着手构建种族隔离制度：种族分类、居住隔离、分隔教育，并把有色人种选民逐出共同选民名册。

sources.title: Saul Dubow, Apartheid, 1948–1994 (2014)
Deborah Posel, The Making of Apartheid, 1948–1961 (1991)
Britannica: Apartheid
Wikipedia: 1948 South African general election

story.en:
The National Party campaigned in 1948 on a single word, apartheid, “separateness”. Its supporters feared that wartime industry had drawn too many Africans into the cities, and the party promised to reverse the trend. Thanks to rural constituencies with fewer voters, Malan’s alliance won 79 seats to 71 for Jan Smuts’s United Party and its ally, though Smuts’s side had won more votes. Smuts lost his own seat.

The new government moved quickly. The Population Registration Act of 1950 classified every person by race; the Group Areas Act assigned residential zones; the Bantu Education Act of 1953 gave African children an education designed, as Hendrik Verwoerd said, for a subordinate place in society. Mixed marriages were banned. Pass laws controlled where Africans could live and work, and whole neighbourhoods such as Sophiatown in Johannesburg and District Six in Cape Town were bulldozed.

Apartheid lasted more than four decades. It provoked the Defiance Campaign, the Freedom Charter, Sharpeville and Soweto, and growing isolation abroad, until the negotiations that led to the elections of 1994.
story.zh:
国民党在1948年的竞选中只打出一个词：“种族隔离”（apartheid，意为“分开”）。其支持者担心战时工业把太多非洲人吸引到城市，该党承诺扭转这一趋势。由于选民较少的农村选区占优，马兰的联盟赢得79席，史末资的统一党及其盟友得71席，尽管后者得票更多。史末资本人甚至丢掉了自己的议席。

新政府行动迅速。1950年的《人口登记法》对每个人进行种族分类；《集团住区法》划定居住区；1953年的《班图教育法》给予非洲儿童的教育，用亨德里克·维沃尔德的话说，是为他们在社会中的从属地位而设计。异族通婚被禁止。通行证法控制非洲人在哪里生活和工作，约翰内斯堡的索菲亚镇、开普敦的第六区等整片街区被推土机夷平。

种族隔离持续了四十多年。它激起了蔑视不公正法运动、《自由宪章》、沙佩维尔和索韦托事件，以及日益加深的国际孤立，直到谈判促成1994年选举。

name.en: Chinua Achebe publishes Things Fall Apart
name.zh: 钦努阿·阿契贝出版《瓦解》

summary.en: Achebe’s first novel, published by Heinemann in London, told the story of Okonkwo, a proud Igbo wrestler and farmer whose world is broken by missionaries and colonial rule. Translated into some 50 languages, it became the most widely read African novel and a founding text of modern African literature.
summary.zh: 阿契贝的第一部小说由伦敦海涅曼出版社出版，讲述了骄傲的伊博族摔跤手和农夫奥贡喀沃的世界如何被传教士和殖民统治摧毁。该书被译成约50种语言，成为读者最多的非洲小说，也是现代非洲文学的奠基之作。

sources.title: Ezenwa-Ohaeto, Chinua Achebe: A Biography (1997)
Britannica: Things Fall Apart
Wikipedia: Things Fall Apart

summary.en: Built with Soviet finance and engineers after the West withdrew its offer of funding, the High Dam ended the Nile’s annual flood, created Lake Nasser and doubled Egypt’s electricity supply. It flooded Lower Nubia, displacing some 100,000 Nubians, and prompted UNESCO’s campaign to move Abu Simbel and other temples.
summary.zh: 西方撤回资助承诺后，高坝在苏联资金和工程师支持下建成。它终结了尼罗河每年的泛滥，形成纳赛尔湖，使埃及电力供应翻番；它也淹没了下努比亚，约十万努比亚人被迫迁徙，并促成联合国教科文组织迁移阿布辛贝等神庙的行动。

sources.title: UNESCO: Monuments of Nubia – International Campaign to Save the Monuments of Nubia
Terje Tvedt, The River Nile in the Age of the British (2004)
Britannica: Aswan High Dam
Wikipedia: Aswan Dam

story.en:
For Nasser the High Dam was the symbol of a new Egypt: it would control the flood, irrigate new land and power industry. When the United States and Britain withdrew their offer to finance it in July 1956, he answered within a week by nationalising the Suez Canal, partly to pay for the dam. The Suez crisis followed. The Soviet Union then supplied loans, machinery and engineers, and construction began in January 1960.

The dam, a rock-fill wall about 3.8 kilometres long, was completed in 1970 and inaugurated in January 1971, a few months after Nasser’s death. Behind it Lake Nasser stretched some 500 kilometres into Sudan. It protected Egypt from the droughts of the 1980s and supplied much of its electricity.

The costs were heavy. The silt that had fertilised the valley for millennia now settled in the lake, and farmers turned to chemical fertiliser. Nubian villages disappeared under the water and their people were resettled. An international campaign led by UNESCO cut the temples of Abu Simbel into blocks and raised them 65 metres between 1964 and 1968.
story.zh:
在纳赛尔看来，高坝是新埃及的象征：它将控制洪水、灌溉新地、为工业供电。1956年7月美国和英国撤回资助承诺后，他在一周内宣布将苏伊士运河收归国有作为回应，部分就是为了支付修坝费用，苏伊士危机随之爆发。苏联随后提供贷款、机械和工程师，工程于1960年1月动工。

大坝为长约3.8公里的堆石坝，1970年完工，1971年1月落成，此时纳赛尔已去世数月。坝后的纳赛尔湖向南延伸约500公里，深入苏丹。它使埃及免受1980年代干旱之害，并提供了大量电力。

代价也很沉重。千百年来滋养河谷的淤泥如今沉积在湖底，农民转而依赖化肥。努比亚村庄沉入水下，居民被迫迁移。1964至1968年，联合国教科文组织领导的国际行动把阿布辛贝神庙切割成块，整体抬高了65米。

summary.en: After police raided Liliesleaf Farm in Rivonia in July 1963, leaders of the ANC’s armed wing were tried for sabotage in Pretoria. Nelson Mandela’s speech from the dock declared an ideal for which he was “prepared to die”. Eight defendants were sentenced to life imprisonment in June 1964.
summary.zh: 1963年7月警方突袭里沃尼亚的利利斯利夫农场后，非国大武装组织的领导人在比勒陀利亚以破坏罪受审。纳尔逊·曼德拉在被告席上的演说宣称，为了理想他“准备献出生命”。1964年6月，八名被告被判终身监禁。

sources.title: Kenneth S. Broun, Saving Nelson Mandela: The Rivonia Trial and the Fate of South Africa (2012)
Nelson Mandela Foundation: The Rivonia Trial
Wikipedia: Rivonia Trial

name.zh: 罗得西亚单方面宣布独立

summary.en: To avoid majority rule, Ian Smith’s white-minority government declared Southern Rhodesia independent of Britain. No country recognised it; the UN imposed sanctions, and from 1966 African nationalist guerrillas fought a long bush war that ended with elections and the independence of Zimbabwe in 1980.
summary.zh: 为避免多数人统治，伊恩·史密斯领导的白人少数政府宣布南罗得西亚脱离英国独立。没有国家予以承认；联合国实施制裁，1966年起非洲民族主义游击队展开长期丛林战争，最终以选举和1980年津巴布韦独立告终。

sources.title: Carl Watts, Rhodesia’s Unilateral Declaration of Independence: An International History (2012)
Britannica: Unilateral Declaration of Independence
Wikipedia: Rhodesia's Unilateral Declaration of Independence

story.en:
By 1965 Britain had granted independence to Zambia and Malawi under African majority governments, and it would not do the same for Southern Rhodesia while some 220,000 whites ruled about four million Africans. Prime Minister Ian Smith refused to accept “no independence before majority rule”. On Armistice Day, 11 November 1965, his cabinet signed a declaration that deliberately echoed the American Declaration of 1776.

Harold Wilson’s government ruled out military force and relied on sanctions, which leaked badly through South Africa and Portuguese Mozambique. Inside the country the nationalist movements ZANU and ZAPU, their leaders including Robert Mugabe and Joshua Nkomo long in detention, turned to guerrilla war. The fighting intensified in the 1970s, after Mozambique’s independence opened a long border to ZANU’s fighters.

By 1979 tens of thousands had died. The Lancaster House conference in London agreed a ceasefire and elections, which Mugabe’s ZANU won in February 1980. On 18 April 1980 Rhodesia became Zimbabwe, named after the great stone ruins in its south, and Salisbury was renamed Harare two years later.
story.zh:
到1965年，英国已让赞比亚和马拉维在非洲人多数政府下独立；而在南罗得西亚，约二十二万白人统治着约四百万非洲人，英国不愿照此办理。总理伊恩·史密斯拒不接受“多数统治之前不独立”的原则。1965年11月11日停战纪念日，他的内阁签署了一份刻意模仿1776年美国《独立宣言》措辞的宣言。

哈罗德·威尔逊政府排除动武，依靠制裁，但制裁通过南非和葡属莫桑比克严重泄漏。在国内，民族主义运动津巴布韦非洲民族联盟和津巴布韦非洲人民联盟（其领导人罗伯特·穆加贝和约书亚·恩科莫等长期被拘押）转向游击战。1970年代莫桑比克独立后，津民盟战士得以利用漫长的边境，战事随之升级。

到1979年，已有数万人死亡。伦敦兰开斯特宫会议达成停火和选举协议，穆加贝的津民盟在1980年2月的选举中获胜。1980年4月18日罗得西亚改名津巴布韦，以南部宏伟的石头遗址命名；两年后索尔兹伯里改名哈拉雷。

summary.en: Julius Nyerere’s ruling party TANU committed Tanzania to ujamaa, an African socialism of self-reliance: banks and major industries were nationalised and leaders were barred from holding shares or renting out houses. The later forced villagisation of the 1970s moved millions of rural people but failed to raise output.
summary.zh: 朱利叶斯·尼雷尔领导的执政党坦盟承诺坦桑尼亚走“乌贾马”道路，即自力更生的非洲社会主义：银行和主要工业收归国有，领导人不得持有股份或出租房屋。1970年代后来强制推行的村庄化运动迁移了数百万农村人口，却未能提高产量。

sources.title: Julius K. Nyerere, Freedom and Socialism / Uhuru na Ujamaa (1968)
Andrew Coulson, Tanzania: A Political Economy (2nd ed., 2013)
Britannica: Arusha Declaration
Wikipedia: Arusha Declaration

name.zh: 埃塞俄比亚革命与“德尔格”

summary.en: Strikes, mutinies and anger at the hidden famine in Wollo brought down Emperor Haile Selassie, deposed on 12 September 1974 by a committee of junior officers, the Derg. The Derg abolished the monarchy, nationalised land and, under Mengistu Haile Mariam, unleashed the Red Terror of 1977–78.
summary.zh: 罢工、兵变以及对沃洛被隐瞒的饥荒的愤怒推翻了皇帝海尔·塞拉西：1974年9月12日，他被下级军官组成的委员会“德尔格”废黜。德尔格废除君主制，将土地收归国有，并在门格斯图·海尔·马里亚姆领导下发动了1977至1978年的“红色恐怖”。

sources.title: Bahru Zewde, A History of Modern Ethiopia, 1855–1991 (2nd ed., 2001)
Andargachew Tiruneh, The Ethiopian Revolution 1974–1987 (1993)
Britannica: Ethiopia: The revolution
Wikipedia: Ethiopian Revolution

story.en:
In 1973 a British documentary by Jonathan Dimbleby revealed a famine in Wollo province that had killed tens of thousands while the imperial court denied it. In early 1974 inflation, a teachers’ strike, taxi drivers’ protests and army mutinies over pay shook Addis Ababa. A committee of soldiers elected from army units, the Derg (“committee” in Geʿez), gradually took control, arresting ministers one by one.

On 12 September 1974 officers read a proclamation deposing the 82-year-old Haile Selassie and drove him away from the palace, according to most accounts, in a small blue Volkswagen. In November the Derg executed some sixty former officials without trial. The emperor died in custody in August 1975, almost certainly murdered.

The Derg declared Ethiopia socialist and in 1975 nationalised all rural land, ending the power of the landlords. Mengistu Haile Mariam emerged as its leader in 1977 and, facing civilian Marxist rivals, unleashed the Red Terror, in which tens of thousands of young people were killed. His regime fell to rebel armies in 1991.
story.zh:
1973年，英国记者乔纳森·丁布尔比的纪录片揭露了沃洛省的饥荒：数万人死亡，帝国宫廷却矢口否认。1974年初，通货膨胀、教师罢工、出租车司机抗议和士兵因军饷哗变震动了亚的斯亚贝巴。一个由各部队推选士兵组成的委员会，即“德尔格”（吉兹语意为“委员会”），逐步掌握大权，逐一逮捕大臣。

1974年9月12日，军官们宣读诏告废黜82岁的海尔·塞拉西，据多数记载，他们用一辆蓝色小型大众汽车把他带离王宫。11月，德尔格未经审判处决了约六十名前官员。皇帝于1975年8月死于羁押中，几乎可以肯定是被谋杀。

德尔格宣布埃塞俄比亚为社会主义国家，1975年将全部农村土地收归国有，终结了地主的权力。门格斯图·海尔·马里亚姆于1977年成为领导人，为对付文职马克思主义对手而发动“红色恐怖”，数万名青年遇害。1991年他的政权被反政府武装推翻。

summary.en: Donald Johanson and Tom Gray found the partial skeleton of a female Australopithecus afarensis, about 3.2 million years old, in the Afar region of Ethiopia. About 40 per cent complete, she showed that human ancestors walked upright long before their brains grew large.
summary.zh: 唐纳德·约翰森和汤姆·格雷在埃塞俄比亚阿法尔地区发现了一具约320万年前的雌性南方古猿阿法种部分骨架。骨架完整度约40%，表明人类祖先在大脑变大之前很久就已直立行走。

sources.title: Donald Johanson and Maitland Edey, Lucy: The Beginnings of Humankind (1981)
Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History: Australopithecus afarensis
Wikipedia: Lucy (Australopithecus)

note: Wikidata dates the fossil itself (about 3.2 million years ago); this record marks its discovery.

story.en:
On the morning of 24 November 1974 the American palaeoanthropologist Donald Johanson and his student Tom Gray were surveying a gully at Hadar, on the Awash River, when Johanson noticed a fragment of arm bone on the slope. Nearby lay pieces of a skull, thigh bone, ribs, pelvis and jaw, all apparently from one individual. That night, as the team celebrated in camp, the Beatles song “Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds” played again and again on a tape recorder, and the skeleton got its name.

The bones belonged to a small adult female, a little over a metre tall. Her pelvis and knee showed that she walked on two legs, but her skull was ape-sized. Named Australopithecus afarensis in 1978, her species became the reference point for debates about human origins for a generation.

In Ethiopia she is called Dinkinesh, Amharic for “you are marvellous”. The original bones are kept in the National Museum in Addis Ababa; between 2007 and 2013 they toured the United States, and in 2025 they went on display in Prague.
story.zh:
1974年11月24日上午，美国古人类学家唐纳德·约翰森和他的学生汤姆·格雷在阿瓦什河畔哈达尔的一条冲沟中考察，约翰森注意到坡上有一块臂骨碎片。附近还散落着头骨、股骨、肋骨、骨盆和下颌的碎片，看来都属于同一个体。当晚队员们在营地庆祝，录音机里一遍遍播放披头士乐队的《露西在缀满钻石的天空》，骨架由此得名。

这些骨骼属于一名身材矮小的成年女性，身高略超过一米。她的骨盆和膝关节表明她用双腿行走，但头骨只有猿类大小。1978年她所属的物种被命名为南方古猿阿法种，此后一代人的人类起源争论都以她为参照。

在埃塞俄比亚，她被称为“丁基内什”，阿姆哈拉语意为“你真了不起”。原始骨骼保存在亚的斯亚贝巴的国家博物馆；2007至2013年曾在美国巡展，2025年在布拉格展出。

summary.en: At independence from Portugal in November 1975 the MPLA held Luanda while the FNLA and UNITA, backed by Zaire, South Africa and the United States, fought it with the MPLA backed by Cuban troops and Soviet arms. The war outlasted the Cold War, financed by oil and diamonds, and ended only when UNITA’s leader Jonas Savimbi was killed in 2002.
summary.zh: 1975年11月安哥拉脱离葡萄牙独立时，安人运控制罗安达；受扎伊尔、南非和美国支持的安解阵和安盟与得到古巴军队和苏联武器支持的安人运交战。这场以石油和钻石为财源的战争延续到冷战之后，直到2002年安盟领导人若纳斯·萨文比被击毙才告结束。

sources.title: Justin Pearce, Political Identity and Conflict in Central Angola, 1975–2002 (2015)
Piero Gleijeses, Visions of Freedom: Havana, Washington, Pretoria, and the Struggle for Southern Africa, 1976–1991 (2013)
Britannica: Angola: Civil war
Wikipedia: Angolan Civil War

story.en:
Portugal’s Carnation Revolution of April 1974 ended five centuries of colonial rule almost overnight, but Angola had three rival liberation movements: the MPLA, strong in Luanda and among the Mbundu; the FNLA, rooted among the Bakongo and backed by Zaire; and UNITA, led by Jonas Savimbi from the Ovimbundu highlands. A power-sharing agreement collapsed within months.

In October 1975 South African columns drove north toward Luanda while FNLA troops approached from the north. Fidel Castro sent thousands of Cuban soldiers by sea and air, and on 11 November Agostinho Neto proclaimed independence in a capital under fire. Cuban forces would stay for fifteen years; the battle of Cuito Cuanavale in 1987–88 led to talks in which South Africa agreed to leave Namibia and Cuba to leave Angola.

Peace in 1991 and elections in 1992 failed when Savimbi rejected his defeat, and the fighting that followed was among the most destructive of the war. Hundreds of thousands died and millions were displaced. Savimbi was killed in an ambush in February 2002, and a ceasefire followed within weeks.
story.zh:
1974年4月葡萄牙康乃馨革命几乎一夜之间结束了五个世纪的殖民统治，但安哥拉有三个相互竞争的解放运动：在罗安达和姆本杜人中势力强大的安人运；扎根巴刚果人、得到扎伊尔支持的安解阵；以及若纳斯·萨文比从奥文本杜高原领导的安盟。权力分享协议几个月内就破裂了。

1975年10月，南非纵队向北直逼罗安达，安解阵军队则从北面逼近。菲德尔·卡斯特罗经海路和空运派出数千名古巴士兵；11月11日，阿戈斯蒂纽·内图在炮火下的首都宣布独立。古巴军队此后驻留了十五年；1987至1988年的奎托夸纳瓦莱战役促成谈判，南非同意撤出纳米比亚，古巴同意撤出安哥拉。

1991年的和平协议和1992年的选举因萨文比拒不接受落败而失败，随后的战斗是整场战争中最具破坏性的阶段之一。数十万人死亡，数百万人流离失所。2002年2月萨文比在伏击中被击毙，数周后双方停火。

summary.en: Drought, civil war and the Derg government’s policies caused a famine in northern Ethiopia that killed hundreds of thousands of people, by some estimates up to a million. A BBC report from the Korem relief camp in October 1984 led to Band Aid, Live Aid and one of the largest relief efforts in history.
summary.zh: 干旱、内战和德尔格政府的政策在埃塞俄比亚北部造成饥荒，数十万人死亡，有估计高达一百万。1984年10月英国广播公司从科雷姆救济营发出的报道催生了“乐队援助”“拯救生命”演唱会和史上规模最大的救援行动之一。

sources.title: Alex de Waal, Evil Days: Thirty Years of War and Famine in Ethiopia (Africa Watch, 1991)
Peter Gill, Famine and Foreigners: Ethiopia since Live Aid (2010)
Wikipedia: 1983–1985 famine in Ethiopia

note: Mortality estimates range from about 400,000 (de Waal) to 1 million (the figure often cited by the UN).

story.en:
The rains failed in northern Ethiopia in 1983 and 1984, but drought alone did not cause the famine. Tigray and Wollo were war zones, where the Derg was fighting the Tigray People’s Liberation Front and Eritrean rebels; government forces burned crops and markets in rebel areas and restricted food movement. In September 1984 the regime spent heavily on celebrations of the tenth anniversary of the revolution while people were dying in the north.

On 23 October 1984 the BBC broadcast a report by Michael Buerk and the cameraman Mohamed Amin from Korem, where tens of thousands of starving people had gathered. Buerk spoke of “a biblical famine” in the 20th century. The musician Bob Geldof watched it and within weeks recorded “Do They Know It’s Christmas?” with Band Aid; the Live Aid concerts of July 1985 followed.

The aid saved many lives but was also manipulated. The government used the crisis to resettle hundreds of thousands of northerners in the south, a programme in which many died, and Alex de Waal argued that counter-insurgency had killed more than the drought.
story.zh:
1983年和1984年埃塞俄比亚北部降雨不足，但仅凭干旱并不足以造成饥荒。提格雷和沃洛是战区，德尔格正与提格雷人民解放阵线和厄立特里亚反政府武装作战；政府军焚烧叛军地区的庄稼和集市，限制粮食流动。1984年9月，政府大肆花钱庆祝革命十周年，而北方的人们正在死去。

1984年10月23日，英国广播公司播出了迈克尔·伯克和摄影师穆罕默德·阿明从科雷姆发回的报道，那里聚集了数万名饥民。伯克称之为20世纪的“一场圣经式的饥荒”。音乐人鲍勃·格尔多夫看了报道，几周内就与“乐队援助”录制了《他们知道现在是圣诞节吗？》，1985年7月又举办了“拯救生命”演唱会。

援助挽救了许多生命，但也被操纵。政府借危机把数十万北方人迁往南方，许多人在迁移中死去；亚历克斯·德瓦尔认为，平叛行动造成的死亡比干旱更多。

name.en: South Africa’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission
name.zh: 南非真相与和解委员会

summary.en: Chaired by Archbishop Desmond Tutu, the commission heard testimony from more than 21,000 victims of apartheid-era abuses and considered over 7,000 applications for amnesty, granted only to those who fully disclosed politically motivated crimes. Its 1998 report held both the state and liberation movements responsible for violations.
summary.zh: 由德斯蒙德·图图大主教主持的委员会听取了两万一千多名种族隔离时期暴行受害者的证词，审理了七千多份大赦申请，只有完全坦白出于政治动机之罪行者才获赦免。其1998年的报告认定国家和解放运动双方都应对侵权行为负责。

sources.title: Truth and Reconciliation Commission of South Africa Report (1998), Department of Justice
Antjie Krog, Country of My Skull (1998)
Britannica: Truth and Reconciliation Commission, South Africa
Wikipedia: Truth and Reconciliation Commission (South Africa)

story.en:
South Africa’s negotiated transition left a hard question: what to do about the killings, torture and disappearances of the apartheid years. A general amnesty would have buried them; Nuremberg-style trials might have wrecked the settlement. The answer, set out in a 1995 act, was a commission that would trade amnesty for truth.

The first hearings took place in East London in April 1996. Victims and their families spoke in their own languages in town halls and churches, and the proceedings were broadcast every week. In one of the early sessions Desmond Tutu, the chairman, put his head on the table and wept. Perpetrators, from security policemen to guerrillas, applied for amnesty; some led investigators to the graves of the people they had killed.

The final report, handed to President Mandela in October 1998, named the state as the main perpetrator but also condemned abuses by the ANC, which tried to block its publication. Critics noted that few of those refused amnesty were ever prosecuted and that promised reparations were slow and small. The model has since been copied in many countries.
story.zh:
南非通过谈判实现的转型留下一个难题：如何处置种族隔离年代的杀戮、酷刑和失踪。全面大赦会把真相掩埋；纽伦堡式审判则可能破坏和解协议。1995年的一部法律给出的答案是成立一个以大赦换真相的委员会。

首场听证会于1996年4月在东伦敦举行。受害者及其家属在市政厅和教堂里用各自的语言讲述，听证过程每周广播。在早期的一次会议上，主席德斯蒙德·图图把头伏在桌上痛哭。从安全警察到游击队员，加害者纷纷申请大赦；有些人带调查人员找到了被他们杀害者的坟墓。

1998年10月提交给曼德拉总统的最终报告认定国家是主要加害者，但也谴责了非国大的侵权行为，非国大曾试图阻止报告发表。批评者指出，被拒绝大赦的人很少受到起诉，承诺的赔偿迟缓而微薄。此后许多国家仿效了这一模式。

summary.en: After two civil wars against Khartoum, ended by the 2005 Comprehensive Peace Agreement, southern Sudanese voted almost unanimously for independence in a January 2011 referendum. South Sudan became Africa’s newest state on 9 July 2011, but fell into its own civil war in December 2013.
summary.zh: 经历两场对抗喀土穆的内战之后（第二次内战以2005年《全面和平协议》结束），苏丹南部民众在2011年1月的公投中几乎一致投票支持独立。2011年7月9日南苏丹成为非洲最年轻的国家，但在2013年12月陷入自身的内战。

sources.title: Douglas H. Johnson, The Root Causes of Sudan’s Civil Wars (updated ed., 2016)
Britannica: South Sudan
Wikipedia: South Sudan

summary.en: Beginning with a child in the Guinean village of Meliandou in December 2013, the largest Ebola outbreak on record spread to Liberia and Sierra Leone. By its end in 2016 there had been about 28,600 cases and 11,300 deaths; it overwhelmed weak health systems and led to the first effective Ebola vaccine.
summary.zh: 这次有记录以来最大规模的埃博拉疫情始于2013年12月几内亚梅连杜村的一名儿童，随后蔓延至利比里亚和塞拉利昂。到2016年疫情结束时，约有28,600例病例、11,300人死亡；它压垮了薄弱的卫生系统，并促成了第一种有效的埃博拉疫苗。

sources.title: World Health Organization: Ebola outbreak 2014–2016, West Africa
Paul Richards, Ebola: How a People’s Science Helped End an Epidemic (2016)
Wikipedia: Western African Ebola virus epidemic

note: The index case is dated to December 2013; the outbreak was identified in March 2014.

story.en:
Investigators later traced the epidemic to Meliandou, a village in the forest region of south-eastern Guinea, where a two-year-old boy fell ill in December 2013, possibly after contact with bats that roosted in a hollow tree nearby. Ebola had never been seen in West Africa, and for three months it was mistaken for cholera or Lassa fever while it spread through funerals and clinics across the borders of Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone.

By mid-2014 it had reached Monrovia, Freetown and Conakry, cities of millions with very few doctors. Liberia had about 50 doctors for 4 million people before the epidemic, and health workers were among the first to die. The WHO declared an international emergency in August 2014. Treatment centres turned patients away for lack of beds.

The tide turned in early 2015, through international field hospitals, contact tracing and, as Paul Richards argues, communities that changed burial customs themselves. A trial in Guinea in 2015 showed that the rVSV-ZEBOV vaccine was highly effective; it was used in later outbreaks in Congo.
story.zh:
调查人员后来把疫情追溯到几内亚东南部森林地区的梅连杜村：2013年12月，一名两岁男孩发病，可能接触过栖息在附近空心树里的蝙蝠。西非此前从未出现过埃博拉，三个月里它被误诊为霍乱或拉沙热，同时通过葬礼和诊所跨越几内亚、利比里亚和塞拉利昂的边界传播。

到2014年年中，疫情已蔓延到蒙罗维亚、弗里敦和科纳克里这些人口数百万而医生极少的城市。疫情暴发前利比里亚约有五十名医生服务四百万人口，医护人员是最早的死者之一。世卫组织于2014年8月宣布国际紧急状态。治疗中心因床位不足而拒收病人。

2015年初形势好转，靠的是国际野战医院、接触者追踪，以及保罗·理查兹所强调的社区自发改变丧葬习俗。2015年在几内亚进行的试验表明rVSV-ZEBOV疫苗非常有效，此后在刚果的疫情中得到使用。
